name: Desert Trails RV Park & Golf Course
access: Paved city streets about 2 mi south of the line through El Centro (Imperial Ave or 4th St, crossing I-8). Flat.
priceTent: The official rate sheet has no tent line. Dry park is $25/night, water and electric (gives you an outlet) is $37, full hookup is $45–50. Rates cover 2 people, with 2.5% off for cash. Expect the dry-park rate for a tent.
reservations: Call ahead. Office hours aren't published. After-hours number (emergencies only): 760-791-2902. There is a $180 cancellation fee on reservations. Open year-round, and November is the start of snowbird season.
cyclistNotes: Tents are not mentioned on the operator's site. AAA lists about 100 tent sites, Good Sam lists a dedicated tenting area, and The Dyrt lists tent sites, so call to confirm. Restrooms are in 5 buildings, 3 of them with showers. Also: laundry, heated pool and hot tub. Mostly a 55+ snowbird park. A Campendium review describes disrepair, urban noise and crime, and spotty wifi. App DB entries osm-way-44388939, camp-res-94 and camp-res-135 are all this one park.

name: Country Life RV Park
access: About 1.5 mi on paved streets: E Ross Rd near Old Hwy 111, east El Centro.
priceTent: No tent rate. RV full hookup $50/day for 2 people, plus $1 per extra person.
reservations: Call. The Hipcamp page is an inactive placeholder, so you can't book it there.
address: 375 E Ross Rd, El Centro, CA 92243
cyclistNotes: Sources conflict on tents. OpenStreetMap tags it tents=no. AAA (seen only in a search summary) lists 6 tent sites out of 169. MHBO describes a manufactured-home community, so expect mostly long-term residents. Call before counting on it.

name: Vacation Inn RV Park
access: About 1.5 mi on paved streets, south El Centro.
priceTent: No tents: AAA lists it as 30 sites, RVs only.
reservations: Contact the park directly.
cyclistNotes: No tents according to AAA (seen only in a search summary). The Dyrt's generic site types list tents, but nobody has reviewed it there. Don't plan on it.
sources: AAA El Centro campgrounds listing (seen in a search summary)

name: Sunbeam Lake RV Resort
access: About 8 mi west of El Centro on paved roads (Evan Hewes Hwy / Drew Rd to Seeley). Flat.
priceTent: $41/night for an RV (reported Nov 2023). No published tent rate.
reservations: Reservations accepted. A September 2025 reviewer got a last-minute spot while an hour out. Call first.
address: 1716 Sunbeam Lake Dr, El Centro (Seeley), CA 92243
cyclistNotes: Tents are unconfirmed. The Dyrt and RVezy list tent sites, Campendium lists none, and the operator's site blocked our request. It is 8 mi in the wrong direction from Brawley, so it's only worth it as an El Centro fallback.

name: Rio Bend RV & Golf Resort
access: About 8 mi west of El Centro via Drew Rd (paved).
priceTent: No tents. RVs only: AAA says 'No tent. Self-contained units/RVs only', and AllStays says '55+, no tent'.
reservations: Phone or the contact form on the website.
cyclistNotes: Tent-banned 55+ snowbird resort. The Dyrt's tent tag is generic. Bar and grill on site.
sources: AAA and AllStays listings (seen in search summaries)

name: Imperial Valley Expo (fairgrounds RV area)
access: About 2.5 mi west of County Route S31 into Imperial (paved).
priceTent: No tents. AllStays says it is open for the fair only, RVs only.
reservations: Call the fairgrounds.
cyclistNotes: About 80 RV spaces used around fair time (the Mid-Winter Fair is in late winter). Not a tent option in November.
sources: AllStays and ParkAdvisor listings (seen in a search summary)

name: Palm Lane RV Park
access: On W Main St in downtown Brawley, right on the route.
priceTent: unknown
reservations: Call. No online booking.
cyclistNotes: The only RV park in Brawley. It has 27 sites, mostly for full-time residents, and one listing says short-term guests are welcome. The Dyrt tags tent sites but has no reviews. Worth one call if you need to stop in Brawley.

name: Wiest Lake County Park
access: About 3 mi east of CA 111 on paved county roads (Rutherford Rd / Dietrich Rd), roughly 4–5 mi north of Brawley. Flat.
priceTent: No 2026 rate published. Reports: $30 for a hookup site (2018); dry sites around $10 (undated).
reservations: Reserve through Imperial County Parks (countyparksandrecreation@co.imperial.ca.us). Reviewers say there are no check-in signs and the ranger is hard to find, so they took an empty site.
cyclistNotes: The county's 2026 parks page lists RV (partial and dry) and tent camping. Reports on showers conflict: a December 2020 tent camper found clean bathrooms with showers, a 2022 review says there are none. There's a loud, smelly cattle feedlot next door, so bring earplugs. Shade trees, lakeside, about 27 sites. The best legal tent stop near Brawley.

name: Finney Lake (Imperial Wildlife Area, Finney-Ramer Unit)
access: About 3 mi from CA 111 via Titsworth Rd, Smith Rd, then Williams Rd. The last stretch is dirt, and GPS often routes you to the wrong end of Williams Rd.
priceTent: Camping is free, but anyone 16+ without a California fishing or hunting license needs a CDFW Lands Pass: $5.97/day in 2026, bought online in advance (valid only for the date printed). You also need a free daily entry permit from the self-registration booth.
reservations: No reservations. Self-register at the booth, first come first served.
address: Williams Rd, Calipatria, CA 92233 (Imperial WA office: 8700 Davis Rd, Niland)
cyclistNotes: Legal under 14 CCR §551(m): camping allowed only in the designated area at Finney Lake. Ramer Lake next door is closed until further notice. A January 2022 reviewer said the pit toilet was gone. Flies and odor (March 2025 review). Waterfowl hunters are around in November, so expect gunfire at dawn. Parts of the wildlife area can close for winter flooding. Carry all water.

name: Del Yermo RV Park
access: In Calipatria, 3 blocks east on Alamo St from CA 111/115.
priceTent: $25/night for an RV (reported April 2023). No tent rate.
reservations: Call. In 2023 the manager was reportedly on site only noon–5 PM, three days a week.
cyclistNotes: 45 full-hookup sites, mostly long-term residents. Only one shower and restroom per sex, with broken door locks (2023). A December 2024 reviewer reported a DEA raid, ongoing drug activity and threats with guns. Not recommended. Tents are unconfirmed (The Dyrt's tag is generic).

name: Red Hill Marina County Park ("Red Hill Park")
access: From CA 111 at Sinclair Rd (about mile 275), roughly 5 mi west on paved Sinclair Rd past the wildlife refuge, then Garst Rd and Red Hill Rd. Reviewers describe rough backroads and dirt at the end.
priceTent: No published rate. Reports: $7 for a tent (2017), $12 (January 2018).
reservations: Through County Parks. No office on site.
cyclistNotes: The county's 2026 page lists tent camping and RV (partial/dry) camping with no dump station. It's on the shrunken Salton Sea shore beside Sonny Bono NWR, with good birding. Brutal mosquitoes at dusk. A 2022 visitor found it 'super sketchy' with long-term residents and no staff. Phone-signal data was logged there on 10/30/26.

name: Slab City (open camping on state land)
access: From Niland, about 3.5 mi east on Main St and Beal Rd, paved to Salvation Mountain (Niland's Main St was being rebuilt in spring 2026). After that, sandy or dirt lanes. Gentle climb.
priceTent: Free
reservations: None. Pitch anywhere unoccupied.
address: Beal Rd / Low Rd, Niland, CA 92257
cyclistNotes: Legally grey. It is an unregulated settlement on state-owned land where camping has been tolerated for decades, not a designated campground. No restrooms (September 2026 guide). A tank at the community church dispenses water. A shooting in 2024; reviewers through 2026 describe trash and decline but food vendors and an open mic. Don't wander east: the Chocolate Mountain Aerial Gunnery Range is a live-fire area. Mojo's Slab Camp (next entry) is the softer landing.

name: Mojo's Slab Camp
access: Through Slab City to Coachella Canal Rd, about 4.5 mi from Niland. Paved most of the way, last bit dirt.
priceTent: Free to $25/night (The Dyrt).
reservations: Reservations possible. A January 2024 reviewer pulled in after dark with no booking and was welcomed.
address: 10100 Coachella Canal Rd, Slab City (Niland), CA 92257
cyclistNotes: An established host camp inside Slab City with restrooms, showers, a communal kitchen and a campfire scene. Reviewed January 2024 and July 2026. Several local dogs roam loose. Its legal standing is the same grey area as the rest of Slab City.

name: Bee Land! True Off-Grid Camping (Hipcamp)
access: A cleared dirt track off CA 111 between Niland and Bombay Beach. The host sends directions on arrival day.
priceTent: $36/night plus Hipcamp fees. Hipcamp lists the site as 'vehicles' only.
reservations: Hipcamp request to book, not instant. Active and bookable, 12 bookings, 4 of 4 recommend.
address: Off CA 111 about 5 mi SE of Bombay Beach (exact location given after booking)
cyclistNotes: 5 bare acres, no facilities, for self-contained campers. Tents aren't a listed site type, so message the host first. Only useful if you're stuck between Niland and Bombay Beach.

name: Fountain of Youth Spa RV Resort
access: About 3.5 mi NE of CA 111 on paved Hot Mineral Spa Rd, then Spa Rd. Gradual climb.
priceTent: No tents: the 2025–26 terms say 'No tent or car camping permitted.' Dry camp for RVs is $45–50/night.
reservations: Online or by phone. Check-in 1 PM. No day use any more.
cyclistNotes: TENT-BANNED. Active 55+ community. Earlier reviews (2018–22) of tents in the dry camp are out of date. The rules also say restrooms may not be used for bike or phone charging. Use Glamis North or Bashford's across the road instead.

name: Bashford's Hot Mineral Spa
access: About 3.5 mi NE of CA 111 on paved Hot Mineral Spa Rd (the turn is about 4 mi SE of Bombay Beach). Gradual uphill.
priceTent: Operator's site (2014 footer, may be dated): $42/night without hookups, $50 with full hookups, for 2 people including the mineral baths. Extra person $10.
reservations: Call. Facilities are for registered guests only. Check-out at noon. Season Oct 15–May 15.
address: 10590 Hot Mineral Spa Rd, Niland, CA 92257
cyclistNotes: The operator's site lists 'Tent sites' and AAA lists tents. Some directories call it an adult or 55+ park, so mention that when you call. Six mineral baths, pool, laundry. A reviewer has wintered there every year since 2023 (September 2026 review).

name: Palm Springs RV Park & Glamis North Hot Springs
access: About 3.75 mi NE of CA 111 on paved Hot Mineral Spa Rd. Gradual uphill toward the Chocolate Mountains.
priceTent: Not published: the rate shows in the reservation system once you pick dates. RV sites were $50 in 2024. 25% off Sunday–Wednesday nights. Price covers hot springs, pools and saunas.
reservations: Reserve online (CampLife) or by phone. Only 2 tent sites, so book ahead. Minimum stay on weekends and holidays. Check-in from 2 PM. Self check-in by a link in the confirmation email.
address: 10595 Hot Mineral Spa Rd, Niland, CA 92257
cyclistNotes: Best tent stop between Niland and the Salton Sea State Recreation Area (SRA). Two tent sites near the pool complex, each with a PRIVATE BATHROOM AND ELECTRICITY (up to 5 tents per site). Season is Oct 23, 2026 to Apr 11, 2027. Store and cafe on site. The Chocolate Mountains block the westerly wind.

name: Private Hot Springs & Organic Farm (Hipcamp, host Gordon)
access: Hot Mineral Spa Rd (paved, about 3.75 mi), then the host's private driveway into a fenced date farm.
priceTent: $72/night plus Hipcamp fees. One group (up to 5) at a time, so the whole site is yours.
reservations: Hipcamp instant book. Check-in 4–9 PM, meeting the host. Check-out 10 AM.
address: Off Hot Mineral Spa Rd, Niland/Bombay Beach (address given after booking)
cyclistNotes: Private natural hot-spring tubs, a flush toilet in a private bathroom, and reverse-osmosis drinking water. 302 bookings, 99% recommend, reviewers praise the host. Arrive by 9 PM.

name: Bombay Beach Campground (Salton Sea SRA)
access: Beach access road in Bombay Beach.
priceTent: Closed
reservations: Closed.
cyclistNotes: CLOSED per the official park page (checked Nov 2, 2026). A cyclist camped here in 2022, but don't plan on it. In town: New Bombay Market, The Chow and the Ski Inn for food.

name: Salton Sea Seclusion (Hipcamp)
access: About 2 mi inland (NE) from CA 111 north of Bombay Beach. Access details come after booking; expect dirt.
priceTent: $25/night plus Hipcamp fees.
reservations: Hipcamp instant book, same day OK (0 hours' notice).
address: Near Bombay Beach (address given after booking)
cyclistNotes: 30 undeveloped acres, 8 tent/RV spots, no facilities. Fill water in Bombay Beach. The host's dogs roam. Only 8 bookings, 88% recommend.

name: Salt Creek Beach Campground (Salton Sea SRA, primitive)
access: Directly off CA 111.
priceTent: Primitive: $10/night (seniors 62+ $8).
reservations: No reservations, first come first served. Park open 24 hours.
cyclistNotes: Open beach camping with picnic tables, fire pits and portable toilets. Not on the official closure list (only Mecca Beach and Bombay Beach are). Trains and the highway are close. The SR 111 washout with one-way traffic control is in this stretch of the park.

name: Corvina Beach Campground (Salton Sea SRA, primitive)
access: Directly off CA 111.
priceTent: Primitive: $10/night (seniors 62+ $8).
reservations: First come first served. Pick any open spot.
address: CA 111, Salton Sea SRA (100-225 State Park Rd, Mecca, CA 92254)
cyclistNotes: Water spigots plus free COLD showers (reviews January 2025 and earlier). Pit toilets, tables, fire rings, no shade. Trains pass close by. 2.5 mi short of the full-service HQ/New Camp.

name: Mecca Beach Campground (Salton Sea SRA)
access: Directly off CA 111.
priceTent: Closed
reservations: Closed.
address: Salton Sea SRA, CA 111, Mecca, CA 92254
cyclistNotes: CLOSED since April 24, 2026 under District Order 555-26-21, maintenance repairs, no reopening date (still closed as of Nov 2, 2026). Go 1 mi on to HQ/New Camp.

name: Salton Sea SRA – Headquarters & New Camp campgrounds (hike-and-bike sites)
access: Turn off CA 111 at the park entrance, then a short paved road (State Park Rd).
priceTent: Developed tent site $20/night, primitive $10, hookup $30 (gives you an outlet). Seniors 62+ get $2 off. The park lists hike-and-bike sites but doesn't publish their fee.
reservations: ReserveCalifornia (park 704), October–May. On Nov 2 the availability calendar showed open sites through Nov 17. Walk-ups get a site if one is free. Campground open 24 hours. Visitor center 9 AM–4 PM daily.
address: 100-225 State Park Rd, Mecca (North Shore), CA 92254
cyclistNotes: The park's 'main campground remains open' (checked Nov 2, 2026). Flush toilets and showers; reviewers in 2024 said the showers take tokens, so get them during visitor-center hours. OpenStreetMap marks hike-and-bike tent sites beside New Camp. Shade ramadas. Freight trains are loud, so bring earplugs. This is the last sure tent stop before Indio (about 30 mi).

name: Oasis Palms RV Resort
access: Paved and flat, about 10.4 mi south of Mecca toward the north-west shore of the Salton Sea.
priceTent: $55/night 'Grass/Tent Site', including water, electricity, sewer and Wi-Fi for up to 4 adults; $320 weekly.
reservations: Phone or email (OasisRVResorthelp@gmail.com). Bookings are usually taken up to a month ahead. Check-in 1 pm, check-out 11 am; register at the front office.
cyclistNotes: The website sells grass/tent sites outright, and a 2016 cyclist had tents confirmed by email. It has a pool, spa, laundry, showers and drinking-water stations (use those rather than the site taps), and a gas station within walking distance. OSM lists an older phone, +1 760-397-1011. Too far off the variant unless you are already routing via the Salton Sea.

name: BLM Mecca Hills – Painted Canyon Rd dispersed camping
access: From Mecca, about 4.5 mi NE on paved Box Canyon Rd (gradual climb), then Painted Canyon Rd: 1–4.5 mi of soft, deep sand wash where cars need 4WD. On a loaded bike that is mostly pushing. BLM: Box Canyon Rd has been CLOSED from Pinto Rd to Painted Canyon Rd since Oct 21, 2026 (flood damage from Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel), so the pull-offs east of the Painted Canyon Rd junction are cut off.
priceTent: Free (BLM limit: 14 days in any 28)
reservations: None.
address: Painted Canyon Rd off Box Canyon Rd, Mecca, CA 92254
cyclistNotes: Camp only along the non-wilderness road corridor: bicycles are banned inside the wilderness. Pit toilets halfway up Painted Canyon Rd (2025). Recreational shooting nearby. The sand wash was probably damaged by the storm. Last resort only.

name: Lake Cahuilla Veterans Regional Park
access: From the line at Ave 58 / Harrison St (about mile 331), roughly 9 mi west on paved, flat Ave 58 / Airport Blvd to Jefferson St. Alternatively about 8 mi south of central Indio via Jefferson St.
priceTent: Primitive or no-hookup sites reported at $25–30/night (2022–25). Water and electric about $30–40. Festival weekends $50–75. Online booking fee about $8.
reservations: Online 24/7 at RivCoParks.org, or on site before 9 PM. Primitive lakeshore sites were first come first served (2022). The fishing gate locks at sunset and there's an electronic gate, so arrive in daylight.
cyclistNotes: 91 sites with a primitive tent area on the lake shore, a small bathhouse with showers (coin-operated per one guide), a pool in summer and dark skies. Reviews from November 2025 say it's very clean, but the derby weekend (Nov 8, 2025) sold out. This is the best full-service tent stop between the SRA and Indio, but it's 9 mi off route.

name: Forsythe Equestrian Club (Hipcamp)
access: About 5 mi west of CV Link on Ave 54 (paved, flat). Exact address after booking.
priceTent: $75/night plus Hipcamp fees (combined tent/RV site).
reservations: Hipcamp instant book, same day OK. Check in on arrival.
address: Vista Santa Rosa (address given after booking)
cyclistNotes: A working horse farm with flush toilets, showers, kitchen, wifi and electric hookups. 39 bookings, 93% recommend. Pricey, but closer than Lake Cahuilla.

name: Coachella Lakes RV Resort (no tents)
access: Paved, 0.9 mi from the Dillon Rd exit (146), where bikes must leave I-10.
priceTent: No tent sites: Campspot shows 0 tent sites, with RV sites from $90/night. Campendium's 'tent camping: yes' tag is wrong.
reservations: Campspot.
cyclistNotes: Right at the bike exit, but it rents only RV sites and cottages.

name: Indian Waters RV Resort & Cottages
access: About 1 mi via Jackson St, Indio.
priceTent: No tents permitted.
reservations: Online or by phone.
cyclistNotes: New ownership: now a Streamside RV Resorts park, formerly a Thousand Trails property. The Dyrt and a 2021 reviewer say tents are not permitted despite photos showing them. RV sites and cottages only.

name: Motorcoach Country Club (Class A only, no tents)
access: Paved. South Indio, about 3 mi off the line.
priceTent: No tents: Class A motorcoach resort.
reservations: n/a for tents
cyclistNotes: The operator site describes it as a 'Class A Luxury RV Resort' with private Class A lots.

name: Outdoor Resort Indio
access: About 3 mi via Ave 48, Indio.
priceTent: No tents: Class A motorcoaches only.
reservations: Online.
cyclistNotes: 'California's premier Class A motorcoach resort'. Not an option for a tent.

name: Indian Wells Sun RV Community (no tents)
access: Paved, 3.9 mi from central Indio.
priceTent: No tenting (2021 reviewer: 'one of the reasons for no tenting allowed'). RV sites were about $119/night in Feb 2025.
reservations: Sun Outdoors online.
cyclistNotes: RV-only; not a tent option.

name: Shadow Hills RV Resort
access: Half a mile off the line in north Indio: Jefferson St at Varner Rd, near I-10.
priceTent: Hipcamp from $39/night plus fees; the lowest rate, probably the tent site. 21 grass tent sites, 10 × 20 ft, no tent supplied.
reservations: Hipcamp instant book, same day OK (0 hours' notice), or call. Check in on arrival.
cyclistNotes: The operator advertises tent sites. Restrooms are a short walk, showers free (2021 review). Pool and spa, laundry, wifi, gated. Can be very windy. Sites by Jefferson St get road noise. Best confirmed tent spot in Indio, at the end of this segment.

name: Pinal County Fairgrounds & Event Center campground
access: Paved and flat, but backwards: from downtown Casa Grande (mile 0) ride about 11.5 mi EAST via E Florence Blvd toward Eleven Mile Corner, then to 512 S Eleven Mile Corner Rd.
address: 512 S Eleven Mile Corner Rd, Casa Grande, AZ 85194
priceTent: $10 cash ($10.43 card) per tent per night for dry/tent camping with restrooms and showers; $25 cash ($25.85 card) for a site with water and 30/50A electric if you want power; weekly rates available.
reservations: No reservations; first-come, first-served. After hours, pay at the box by the office or find the camp host on duty (reviewers say call before closing so the host can let you in). 14-night limit per 6 months; checkout 11 am. Blackouts: Oct 30-Nov 1 2026 dry camping only (motorcycle swap meet); NO open camping Nov 16-19 2026. Nov 2-15 is normal.
cyclistNotes: This is the only tent-legal campground in the Casa Grande area. Every in-town park is 55+ and/or RV-only (see gapWarnings). It is 11.5 mi behind you if you're heading west, so it only makes sense for a rest day. Open lot with no designated tent pads. Animals and noise during events. No fires on pavement, no firearms.

name: Casa Grande RV Resort & Cottages
access: Paved, about 3 mi north of downtown on N Pinal Ave at W Rodeo Rd.
address: 195 W Rodeo Rd, Casa Grande, AZ 85122
priceTent: No tent sites. RV sites were about $77/night (reported Mar 2025); cottages are lodging, not camping.
reservations: Office open Mon-Sat 9 am-4 pm, closed Sunday.
cyclistNotes: This is the trip app's 'Unnamed campground' (OSM way 1348098748) at Pinal Ave & Rodeo Rd. AAA lists it as 'No tent - RVs only', and the operator advertises only 282 RV sites and 34 cottages. All ages, but not a tent option.

name: RoVer's Roost SKP Co-op (Escapees members, 55+)
access: I-8 exit 167 (Montgomery Rd), then 1.5 mi north on paved road.
address: 3241 S Montgomery Rd, Casa Grande, AZ 85193
priceTent: Not available to a non-member tent cyclist. For Escapees RVers: dry camping $10, full hookups $30/day.
reservations: CampSpot or phone, for Escapees members only.
cyclistNotes: Baseline entry. Rules (Feb 2026): lots and spaces go to Escapees and to guests of a resident member, and the boondock area is for RV units. It is a 55+ co-op. Not a tent option. Showers and laundry are for registered residents and guests.

name: Silverado RV Resort (Eloy)
access: Paved, about 11 mi southeast of Casa Grande in Eloy (Tonto Rd / La Brea St), behind you.
priceTent: Not applicable: a 55+ RV resort.
reservations: unknown
cyclistNotes: Listed by Campendium as 'Silverado 55+ RV Resort'. This is a baseline app entry that should be marked not usable for a tent camper.

name: Wild West RV Ranch (primitive tent site)
access: Paved state highways, flat. From Maricopa (mile 21.7) ride about 12.5 mi south on AZ 347 / John Wayne Pkwy to AZ 84 ('Peters Corner'). Alternative: from Casa Grande ride about 18 mi west on AZ 84 through Stanfield to the ranch, then about 12.5 mi north on AZ 347 to Maricopa next morning. That adds about 9 mi to the planned line.
address: 860 S John Wayne Pkwy (AZ 347 at AZ 84, Peters Corner), Maricopa, AZ 85139
priceTent: Primitive tent site booked via Hipcamp. The listing shows 'from $25/night'; one directory quoted the tent site at $40. Includes restrooms, hot showers, a water spigot, Wi-Fi, a picnic table and a fire pit. The tent site has no electric; RV sites have 30/50A pedestals (RV from about $50, Good Sam).
reservations: Book on Hipcamp; same-day bookings accepted. Check-in from 2 pm with a host meet-and-greet; call for a late arrival. Open all year, all ages.
cyclistNotes: The best real tent campground between Casa Grande and Buckeye: a dedicated primitive tent site near restrooms and hot showers. Tent campers reviewed it in Aug and Oct 2026 (clean bathroom, easy check-in, some shade). Its own websites are dead (wildwestrvranch.com is an unconnected Wix domain; the old wildwestrvresort.com is now spam), so use Hipcamp or the phone. Main drawback: 12.5 mi off the line each way.

name: Harrah's Ak-Chin Casino overnight RV lot (emergency only)
access: Paved: from the line in Maricopa ride about 2.5 mi south on AZ 347 / John Wayne Pkwy.
priceTent: Free. Overnight RV/vehicle parking only, per reviewers; tent use is not documented anywhere.
reservations: Ask security or the front desk before setting up. In 2022 security first turned an RVer away, then allowed the back lot. No stated night limit.
cyclistNotes: Last-resort fallback on Ak-Chin tribal land. The documented use is RVs sleeping in a parking lot, not tents, and the casino's own site says nothing about RV parking, so ask and accept a 'no'. 24-hour restrooms, food and water inside. Semis also use the lot at night. The newest reviews are from 2022.

name: BLM dispersed: desert tracks between AZ 238 and Empire Blvd (south end of Sierra Estrella)
access: On the line itself. From about mile 31.3 (N Rahma St off AZ 238) the route leaves pavement and follows unnamed OSM tracks across BLM land north to 'Empire Blvd'. Surface is dirt and sand with wash crossings; BLM calls these roads 'extremely sandy or silty' and requires 4WD to reach the wilderness boundary. Per BLM's land-status GIS, the line is on BLM land for most of miles 31-42.
address: BLM public land along the route's dirt tracks north of AZ 238 near N Rahma St, Maricopa County
priceTent: Free; no permit. BLM limit is 14 days in any 28-day period.
reservations: None; first come.
cyclistNotes: Free, legal, no facilities at all. At miles 39-42 camp WEST of the north-south track: the Sierra Estrella Wilderness boundary is just east, and bikes are banned inside (the line passes about 165 ft from it at mile 42). A mapped BLM vault toilet sits at the Quartz Peak trailhead, about 1.7 mi east of mile 41.7, but the way there is deep sand. Tribal land is only 0.3-1 mi away near miles 28-34, so don't stray onto it. Carry all water from Maricopa; nothing is available from mile 25 to 58. Rainbow Valley BLM land gets target shooters, so camp out of sight of the track. Fireworks and exploding targets are banned year-round; seasonal fire restrictions were lifted July 22, 2026. No Lower Sonoran camping closures or BLM Arizona alerts were listed on Nov 1, 2026.

name: BLM dispersed: unpaved W Riggs Rd section (miles 45-47)
access: On the line: the unpaved track / 'W Riggs Rd' section between Empire Blvd and the start of pavement at about mile 48.6 crosses BLM land at about miles 45-47. Dirt and sand.
address: BLM land along W Riggs Rd (unpaved) east of S 163rd Ave, Rainbow Valley, Maricopa County
priceTent: Free; 14 days in any 28.
reservations: None.
cyclistNotes: The last free camp right on the line before pavement resumes. Rainbow Valley homes start just west; only the BLM block is legal, so stay clear of private parcels. No water; the nearest is a fire station about 12 mi ahead (mile 57.8).

name: BLM dispersed: west end of W Riggs Rd past Rainbow Valley Rd
access: At the W Riggs Rd / S Rainbow Valley Rd junction (mile 52.6, where the line turns north), keep going WEST about 1.1-1.2 mi on W Riggs Rd (gravel per OSM) to BLM land at the north end of the Maricopa Mountains. S 189th Ave / Baseline Rd (unpaved) and a track about 1 mi south of the junction also reach BLM land.
address: End of W Riggs Rd west of S Rainbow Valley Rd, Rainbow Valley, Maricopa County
priceTent: Free; 14 days in any 28.
reservations: None.
cyclistNotes: The closest legal free camp to paved Rainbow Valley Rd, about mile 50-53, which fits a 50-mile wind day. Residential lots border the BLM land, so camp well inside the boundary. Nearest water: Goodyear Fire Station 6, about 5 mi on at mile 57.8 (ask).

name: BLM dispersed: W Ray Rd west of S Tuthill Rd (Buckeye Hills east)
access: Where the line turns from W Ray Rd north onto S Tuthill Rd (about mile 61), continue about 0.9-1.3 mi west on W Ray Rd (asphalt per OSM) to BLM land.
address: W Ray Rd west of S Tuthill Rd, south of Buckeye, Maricopa County
priceTent: Free; 14 days in any 28.
reservations: None.
cyclistNotes: Land status comes only from BLM GIS; no camper reports found. The point is not inside the Lower Gila Terraces ACEC (checked against BLM's ACEC layer). Equestrian and other private parcels are nearby, so obey any 'no trespassing' signs. Fire Station 326 is right on the line at mile 61.2 for water.

name: Estrella Mountain Regional Park new campground (under construction)
access: Paved Goodyear arterials: from S Tuthill Rd at about mile 62.5, ride about 8-9 mi east (Elliot Rd / Estrella Pkwy / Vineyard Ave) to the park entrance at 14805 W Vineyard Ave.
priceTent: unknown; rates for the new campground not found.
reservations: Maricopa County Parks online system (exploremaricopacountyparks.org / reservations.maricopacounty.gov), up to 6 months ahead. The county says the park only 'periodically' rents host sites; call.
cyclistNotes: Don't count on it. The county says the 50-site campground (2 restroom buildings with showers, dump station) is under construction Feb 2025 through Mar 2027. Jan 2026 commission minutes said work continues, and an Apr 29, 2026 county release still called it 'under development'. If it has opened early, it would be the only shower campground between Maricopa and Buckeye. Phone before detouring.
verifyNote: Checked against https://maricopacountyparks.net/assets/1/6/ESTRELLA_MOUNTAIN_REGIONAL_PARK_-_Area_Closure_and_New_Campground_Construction.pdf: Maricopa County is building the new campground; construction runs to about March 2027, so there is no camping yet.

name: Vescent RV Park
access: Paved, about 1 mi north of the line on Buckeye's east side, on MC 85 next to Vescent Church.
priceTent: unknown
reservations: unknown
cyclistNotes: Appears only in OpenStreetMap; no website, phone or reviews found. It shares its location with Vescent Church. Worth asking in person while passing through Buckeye, but treat it as unverified.

name: The Sunset Nooks (Hipcamp tent site)
access: Small private lot in south Buckeye by the Gila River, about 1 mile off the line at the Buckeye end (street address shown after booking). Paved streets, walk-in tent pad.
priceTent: $55/night for the single tent site (about $64.53 all-in with the Hipcamp fee), up to 8 people. Host supplies a pop-up tent, table, chairs, BBQ and charcoal.
phone: unknown (contact host Cory W. through the Hipcamp app)
reservations: Hipcamp instant book, 1-night minimum, no advance notice needed. Message the host with your ETA. Music down at 8pm, off at 10pm.
cyclistNotes: This is the only bookable tent pitch with a shower and toilet at the Buckeye end: 44 bookings, 96% recommend. It sits at corridor mile ~70, the start of this segment, so it works as a Buckeye night, not a mid-segment stop. A toilet is listed but its type isn't stated.

name: Skyline Regional Park campground (City of Buckeye)
access: Paved: from Beloat Rd ride about 8 mi straight north on Watson Rd (crossing I-10 at exit 117) to 2600 N Watson Rd. The last 2 mi climb about 500-600 ft into the White Tank foothills (camp elevation 1,476 ft).
priceTent: $20/night per site (last reported Dec 2025). Restrooms with sinks and toilets; no water, showers or hookups.
reservations: 7 primitive sites (A-G). Reserve online through the City of Buckeye at least 3 days ahead; unreserved walk-up stays are limited to one night (Dec 2025 review). Max 7 nights. The gate reportedly locks around 10 pm (one report says 9:30 pm), so arrive early.
cyclistNotes: Legal, cheap, quiet and dark, but completely dry: the city says there is no drinking water in the park. Fill up in Buckeye (Circle K on Monroe Ave) before the climb. Sites C-E are farther from the busy trailhead. It is a 17-mi round-trip detour north, not on the way west.

name: Leaf Verde RV Resort (Sun Outdoors / Sun RV)
access: Paved, about 4.5 mi north of downtown Buckeye on Apache Rd, near I-10.
priceTent: No tent sites listed. RV sites were about $85/night (May 2024).
reservations: Office reportedly closed on weekends (2024).
cyclistNotes: A large Sun Communities RV park with mostly long-term residents. Its Hipcamp property listing shows only RV site types (Standard/Deluxe/Premium, 376 sites) and reviewers call the Wi-Fi unusable. Expect 'RVs only'. Note that leafverde.com now redirects to Sun Outdoors.

name: BLM dispersed off W Robbins Butte Game Rd (south of Buckeye; 'Buckeye Hills BLM')
access: From the line at Buckeye, take AZ 85 south across the Gila River (about 4-5 mi on the highway shoulder) to W Robbins Butte Game Rd, then 1-2 mi west on dirt with soft gravel and sand spots. Campers use a strip of about 1 mi on the SOUTH side of the road.
address: W Robbins Butte Game Rd off AZ 85, Buckeye, AZ
priceTent: Free
reservations: None.
cyclistNotes: Last resort only. Legality is muddled: 'no overnight camping / no shooting' signs were seen in Apr 2025, rangers told campers 'no camping' in 2021, the adjoining Robbins Butte Wildlife Area (AZ Game & Fish) bans camping, and The Dyrt lists the nearby 'Buckeye Hills BLM' spot as CLOSED. People were still camping there in Jan-Feb 2026, and a sheriff patrols mornings. Reviews from 2021-2026 report heavy shooting (ricochets near a trailer in Aug 2024), theft, dumping and crowding. Not a good place for a solo tent.

name: Skyline Regional Park campground (City of Buckeye)
access: 2600 N Watson Rd, Buckeye. About 9 miles north of the line on paved Watson Rd (crosses I-10), climbing gently into the White Tank foothills. Coordinate is the OSM park centroid. The campsites are near the park entrance.
priceTent: $20/night per campsite (7 sites, A to G). Each site has two 12x12 ft tent pads, a picnic table, a grill and a fire ring.
reservations: Reservation required: request online or call Mon-Fri 9am-7pm. The city calls back within 72 hours to confirm and take payment, so same-day booking isn't realistic. Park hours are 5am-10pm.
cyclistNotes: There's no drinking water anywhere in the park (the city says so explicitly), so carry it all in. Restrooms have sinks and toilets but no showers. It's only worth the 9-mile detour if you booked it a few days ahead.

name: 3Acre Desert RV Camp (Hipcamp)
access: Private fenced 3-acre lot about 1 mile off the line, between Arlington and Wintersburg (address after booking). It borders a wash and State Trust land. Drive-in, 2WD access.
priceTent: $25/night for an RV site (about $29.58 with Hipcamp fees). Tent use isn't listed, so ask the host.
address: near Tonopah/Arlington, AZ (exact address after booking)
reservations: Request-to-book, not instant. Message the host the day before. 1 booking so far, 100% recommend.
cyclistNotes: Apart from Stage Stop, this is the only private option between Buckeye and Tonopah. The listing is RV-only, so get the host's OK to pitch a tent before counting on it. Potable water, fire pit and trash are listed.

name: Buckeye Ranch RV Resort
access: 105 N 339th Ave at I-10 exit 103, about 4-5 miles north of the Salome Hwy line on paved roads.
priceTent: No tent sites. RV sites are $58+/night and cabins $102+/night on Hipcamp.
reservations: Campspot/Hipcamp, request-to-book.
cyclistNotes: New big-rig resort with full-hookup RV sites and cabins only, no tent sites. Listed here so you don't detour for it.

name: Stage Stop RV Park / Wintersburg General Store
access: 2614 S Wintersburg Rd, right at the line on Salome Hwy. The store is at the park entrance.
priceTent: No tent rate. RV daily is $60 with utilities, plus a $300 refundable deposit on all lodging.
reservations: Register at the Wintersburg General Store (open daily 5am-9pm; office Mon-Fri 6am-8pm, Sat-Sun 12-8pm). Rentals require a deposit and 2 IDs.
cyclistNotes: Worker park for Palo Verde nuclear plant staff. Showers are for tenants. Tent policy is unknown, so ask at the store. The store itself is the key resupply on this stretch: groceries, fresh produce, fuel and an ATM, with Tin Top Bar & Grill on site.

name: Saddle Mountain RV Park
access: 40902 W Osborn Rd, half a mile south of I-10 exit 94 (411th Ave), on pavement.
priceTent: Full-hookup sites are $50/night plus tax for 2 people. A Nov 2024 RoverPass listing showed tents at $30 (or $35 with power), but the 2026 operator site lists RV sites only.
reservations: Call or email; $200 refundable deposit. Office is open Mon-Fri 9am-3pm (Sep-Apr). After hours, self check-in at the desk by the office door: pick a site from the board and pay by envelope.
cyclistNotes: Reopened under new management after showing 'permanently closed' in 2023. Ask whether they'll put a tent on an RV site. Self check-in makes late arrival easy. Flies from nearby egg and chicken farms have been reported in the area.

name: El Dorado Hot Spring
access: 41225 W Indian School Rd, Tonopah, 0.3 mile on pavement from I-10 exit 94 (411th Ave).
priceTent: About $50/night (Feb 2026 review; The Dyrt lists 'from $40'). Has primitive tent sites plus 30A electric sites.
website: unknown (old eldoradohotspring.com no longer resolves; listings link to a Facebook page)
address: 41225 W Indian School Rd, Tonopah, AZ 85354
reservations: Call ahead. A March 2026 guest reported no check-in instructions and a double booking, so confirm by phone the same day.
cyclistNotes: The one confirmed tent camp with showers at Tonopah. Outdoor showers and new restrooms were built in 2024. It's a clothing-optional hot spring with one 24/7 nude-only pool, and you can hear the interstate. Pilot, Chevron and Exxon are across exit 94.

name: BLM land along Hovatter Rd (I-10 exit 53) - unverified fallback
access: Take I-10 exit 53, then go south on Hovatter Rd. It's dirt and 'smooth but very sandy' at the start, so expect to push a loaded bike. The land is BLM Yuma Field Office until the Kofa NWR boundary about 20+ miles south. The coordinate is the road near the interchange, not a known campsite.
priceTent: Free under the standard BLM rule (14 days in any 28) if the parcel is BLM.
reservations: First-come.
cyclistNotes: This is the only spot right on the interstate between Tonopah and Quartzsite, about 41 miles from Tonopah. I found no camper reports. Check a land-status map (BLM vs State Trust) before pitching and stay well away from the freeway. Bouse Wash rest area (restrooms, water unreliable) is 1 mile west; the Pilot at exit 45 is 8 miles west.

name: Gold Nugget Rd BLM dispersed (I-10 exit 26)
access: I-10 exit 26 (Gold Nugget Rd), then south 1/4 mile. Loose small gravel and firm sand.
priceTent: Free, 14-day maximum.
reservations: First-come.
cyclistNotes: The first free pitch right on the interstate after Tonopah, 7-8 miles before Quartzsite. Cactus debris means puncture risk (reviewers say it isn't dog-friendly), plus freeway hum and ATVs. BLM says short-term camping around Quartzsite is limited to five designated areas and this isn't one of them, so obey any 'no camping' signs (Scaddan Wash is 6 miles on). The newest review is Feb 2024.

name: Scaddan Wash BLM 14-day camping area
access: Leave I-10 at exit 19 (Riggles Ave) and ride about 1.5-2 miles east on Dome Rock Rd E (the south frontage road; rough, so reviewers use the shoulder) to the area. Inside it's dirt and sand with washes.
priceTent: Free, 14-day limit. A seasonal camp host registers campers.
address: Dome Rock Rd E, Quartzsite, AZ 85346
reservations: First-come; register with the host if present.
cyclistNotes: The designated free area closest to town, within bike range of all Quartzsite services. Very loud near the freeway, so go well south. A Dec 2025 review reports dumped tires and a microwave.

name: Plomosa Road BLM 14-Day Camping Area
access: Paved US 95 north about 5.5 mi, then east on asphalt Plomosa Rd. Camp on the gravel flats on either side and respect the marked day-use boundaries.
priceTent: Free, 14 days in 28. One Campendium user entered '$44' in Feb 2026; every other report says free.
reservations: First come. A seasonal host is sometimes present.
cyclistNotes: Less dusty and roomier than the areas near town (Feb 2026 review). It is 13 mi round trip in the wrong direction, so it's only a fallback.
address: US 95 at Plomosa Rd, about 6 mi north of Quartzsite, AZ

name: Hi Jolly BLM 14-day camping area
access: 3 miles north of Quartzsite on US 95 at milepost 112 (paved highway), gravel inside.
priceTent: Free, 14-day limit. Register with the camp host for a free 14-day pass when one is on duty.
reservations: First-come.
cyclistNotes: Crowded with RVs in season, though clean. Camp toward the east side, away from US 95 noise. Water, dump and propane are in town, 3 miles away.

name: Tumbleweed RV Park (Rose's RV Park)
access: 600 Kuehn St, Quartzsite, next to I-10. City streets.
priceTent: $8-40/night per The Dyrt, which lists 'Standard (tent/RV)' sites. Showers were coin-op ($5 in 2019) and free in 2023.
reservations: Call; no online booking.
cyclistNotes: The cheap end of its range may be a tent or dry spot. Constant I-10 noise. A 2019 reviewer rode a bike to town and the RV show from here.

name: Quail Run RV Park
access: Paved, on Central Blvd (US 95 N).
priceTent: No tents. RV is $55.
cyclistNotes: The park rules say 'Tent camping is not allowed.' A 2025 cross-country support group stayed here in RVs.
reservations: OSM says reservations are required.

name: 88 Shades RV Park - no tents
access: 575 W Main St, Quartzsite.
priceTent: No tent sites (RV $35/night).
cyclistNotes: RV-only snowbird park. Earlier research and every current listing show RV sites only.
reservations: Check-in is open 24 hours with an after-hours drop box.

name: Q View RV Park (formerly B-10 Campground)
access: 615 W Main St in central Quartzsite, near I-10 exit 17/19. City streets.
priceTent: $25/night 'Dry Camping', plus a $2.50 booking fee, a 3% card fee and tax ($125/week). Hookup sites are $35-50.
phone: (928) 927-4393 (site says this line is temporarily down; temporary number 501-691-5757)
reservations: Book online or call. Open 365 days.
cyclistNotes: This is the baseline 'B-10 Campground' under its new name. It offers dry camping 'for non-RV folks' (a guest review quoted on its site), private hot showers that aren't coin-op, Starlink Wi-Fi, laundry and fire pits. The old B-10 had numerous tent sites. Confirm the dry site takes a tent when you book. Walking distance to everything in town.

name: La Posa LTVA (North/South/West/Tyson Wash)
access: About 2 miles south of Quartzsite on US 95 (from I-10 exit 17), with four sub-areas. Permits are sold at the entrance host station. Dirt roads inside, reported rough after the 2026 flooding.
priceTent: In season (Sept 15-Apr 15) the cheapest legal permit is the $40 short-visit permit covering any 14 consecutive days; there's no one-night rate. The long-term permit is $180. A 2024 BLM plan proposed $200/$600, but I found no sign it was adopted.
reservations: First-come; buy the permit on site or at the Yuma Field Office.
cyclistNotes: The only Quartzsite camp with public water taps (8, though a reviewer calls the water salty, so carry drinking water), 10 vault toilets, dump and trash. Poor value for one night next to the free 14-day areas.
address: US 95 south of I-10, Quartzsite, AZ 85346. Coordinates are the Tyson Wash host station, where permits are sold.

name: Desert Gardens RV Park (Sky Resorts)
access: 1240 Acacia Rd, south-west Quartzsite. City streets.
priceTent: Tent rate not published. RV sites start at $36/night (Good Sam).
reservations: Book online or call. Open year-round.
cyclistNotes: The Dyrt lists tent sites, but the operator site advertises full-hookup RV sites only and AllStays calls it 55+. Call first.

name: Road Runner BLM 14-day camping area
access: About 6 miles south of I-10 on US 95 to milepost 99, then just west via N 53rd St / La Paz Valley Rd. Hard-packed gravel, with a steep drop-off at the road edge.
priceTent: Free, 14-day limit. A host issues free permits in season.
address: La Paz Valley Rd, Quartzsite, AZ 85346
reservations: First-come.
cyclistNotes: Huge and nearly empty in late Oct 2025. Go west, away from US 95 traffic. Note it's a 12-mile round trip off the westbound route.

name: Dome Rock Mountain BLM 14-day camping area
access: On the westbound route: Dome Rock Rd W (south frontage road), 3-5 miles west of town. Rocky but passable dirt. The camp host is near the entrance. Coordinates vary by source (Campendium 33.6494,-114.2715; The Dyrt 33.6409,-114.3151); the area is large.
priceTent: Free. Get the free 14-day permit from the seasonal camp host.
reservations: First-come; register with the host.
cyclistNotes: Up to about 400 sites on hard, flat desert. Load all water in Quartzsite. Stay out of the marked gas-pipeline corridor. It's just past the segment end (mile ~176-178) and already on the road to Blythe, so it's the natural first night west of town.
address: Dome Rock Rd W, between I-10 exits 17 and 11, Quartzsite, AZ 85346

name: Saddle Mountain BLM dispersed camping
access: The Salome variant runs right past it on W Courthouse Rd, paved from the east. Many entrances; a popular one is near Courthouse Rd mile marker 13. Sites sit on rocky, rutted dirt spurs (coordinate is approximate). From the main I-10 line it's about 8-10 riding miles SW of exit 94 via Indian School Rd, Saddle Vista Rd, Salome Hwy and Courthouse Rd. Don't follow GPS onto Salome Hwy from I-10 exit 81: it's dirt until Courthouse Rd.
priceTent: Free, 14 days in any 28.
reservations: First-come, no permit or host.
cyclistNotes: Fill water at Tonopah (exit 94) or the Saddle Vista Ranch RV fill (about 10c/gal per a 2024 review). Reviews from Oct 26-27, 2026 call the fly swarms 'unbearable' (nearby egg/chicken farms), so expect them in early November. Also: weekend target shooting, rocky ground (bring stakes that hold in gravel), and a power-plant smell on some winds.

name: Indian Hills RV Resort
access: 67668 Salome Rd, on paved Salome Rd at the SE edge of Salome. The variant passes the gate.
priceTent: $39.20/night on Hipcamp for a 50x55 ft back-in 'RV/tent' site with full hookups and 30/50A (about $48.78 with fees). A furnished teepee is $85, casitas $125+.
reservations: Hipcamp instant book (same-day OK, 1-night minimum) or call. Office hours aren't published.
cyclistNotes: The best-equipped tent stop on the variant: hot showers, laundry, free Wi-Fi, a store and fitness room, all ages. It's the first camp after the 41-mile empty Harquahala Valley stretch. 13 Hipcamp bookings, 100% recommend.

name: Centennial Park (La Paz County)
access: 69725 Centennial Park Rd, about 3 miles east of Salome off US 60 (toward Wenden). Gravel park roads.
priceTent: $10/night dry camping, or $20 with water and electric (May 2025 review). Dump is $10.
reservations: First-come with an on-site host (2022). Late-arrival rules unknown.
cyclistNotes: The cheapest legal pitch around Salome, plus a desert golf course. Facilities have been unreliable: 2018 and 2021 reviews mention showers, but in 2022 the restrooms were locked (porta-potties) and the well water was not drinkable. Call before relying on its water or showers.

name: Salome KOA Journey
access: 64812 Harcuvar Dr, just off US 60 about 2.5 miles west of Salome (near milepost 54). The variant line passes the entrance. KOA's own directions say 'US 60 to MP 54, then 2 mi S on Harcuvar Dr', but mapped coordinates put the park about 0.2 mile from US 60.
priceTent: Tent rate not published. KOA lists Deluxe and Premium tent sites; Good Sam mentions a gravel overflow tent area. RV sites start around $51/night (Good Sam).
reservations: Online, KOA app or phone. Office is roughly 8am-4pm daily, with lit after-hours check-in. Open all year.
cyclistNotes: Pool, hot tub, laundry and a camp store. Salome Restaurant is about 0.2 mile away on US 60. New owners (the Johnston family, Dec 2025) are restoring a breakfast kitchen.

name: Ramblin' Roads RV Resort (Hope)
access: 60655 US 60 at Hope. The variant goes by the door.
priceTent: Tent rate not published. The Dyrt lists sites 'from free to $35/night'.
reservations: Call or email. Arriving late: fill out an envelope at the after-hours registration on the front of the building (lobby open until 9pm). After 9pm, take any open site and pay when the lobby opens at 9am. Office Mon-Sat 9am-2pm, Oct 1 to Apr 1.
cyclistNotes: The operator's amenity list explicitly includes TENT CAMPING (plus good well water and free Wi-Fi), but it's a 55+ park. Confirm they'll take your party before relying on it.

name: Vicksburg Pit Rd BLM dispersed
access: From Vicksburg Junction (US 60, variant mile about 66.5), about 2-3 miles north toward SR 72 and Vicksburg to Vicksburg Pit Rd. The access is wide, well-graded gravel; cross the railroad tracks slowly. From the main I-10 line: exit 45 (mile about 145), then about 8 miles north on Vicksburg Rd.
priceTent: Free, 14-day maximum.
reservations: First-come.
cyclistNotes: Quiet, few campers and dark skies (Feb 2026 reviews). Flies even in December. The BLM land borders private parcels, so stay on BLM. No services: get water at the Pilot at I-10 exit 45 or in Salome.

name: Steve and Dawn Desert Getaway
access: 10 fenced acres north of US 60 near Vicksburg; GPS may show Salome. About 5.6 miles in a straight line north of the variant, probably on dirt roads. Address comes with the booking.
priceTent: $15-30/night. There are 3 dry sites for tent or RV (no water or power at the site) and 2 full-hookup RV sites.
reservations: Request to Book through The Dyrt.
cyclistNotes: The listing says there is 'as yet no bathroom on-site'. It's far off the line, so only worth it if everything closer is full.

name: 3 Dreamers RV Park
access: 54000 US 60, about 3 miles west of Vicksburg Junction, right on the variant.
priceTent: $32/night per The Dyrt (probably the RV rate). No tent rate on the operator site.
reservations: Call. Office and campstore are open Mon-Sat 11am-5pm (Oct-Mar), closed Sunday. A Dec 2025 review says the owners helped with a late-night arrival.
cyclistNotes: The Dyrt lists tent sites, but the operator's site mentions only full-hookup RV sites. Call first. New owners in 2025; clean hot showers, laundry, campstore and propane.

name: The Collier 15 (Hipcamp)
access: Fenced 55-acre property just off US 60 between Vicksburg Junction and Brenda (address after booking). Short dirt driveway.
priceTent: $22.75/night (about $26.79 with Hipcamp fees) for an RV/tent site with full hookups and a 30A outlet. Two sites: 'The 2 mesquites' (concrete pad, fire pit) and 'The Willow'.
reservations: Hipcamp instant book, 1-night minimum, no advance notice. 17 bookings, 86% recommend.
cyclistNotes: The host calls it 'perfect for tent camping', and you get an outlet to charge. A toilet is listed but no shower. Buckaroos store in Brenda is about 5 miles west. Same host as The Dusty 40 next door.

name: The Dusty 40 (Hipcamp)
access: 40-acre desert parcel next to The Collier 15, just off US 60 between Vicksburg Junction and Brenda. Dirt access.
priceTent: $8/night (about $11 with fees). Pitch anywhere on the property.
reservations: Hipcamp instant book, 1-night minimum. 5 bookings, 100% recommend.
cyclistNotes: Bare land the host is still cleaning up, with broken glass in spots, so watch your tires and tent floor. Bring all water.

name: Black Rock RV Village (Brenda)
access: 46751 E US 60 in Brenda, on the variant, 3.7 miles before it rejoins I-10 at exit 31.
priceTent: No tent rate. RV sites are $40-45/night.
reservations: Office closes at 3pm and is closed Sundays.
cyclistNotes: Lists RV sites only, so ask about a tent before counting on it. Black Rock Cafe on site (limited hours) and Buckaroos Country Store nearby make Brenda a food stop either way. Wi-Fi only works at the diner and pavilion.

name: Desert Gold RV Resort (Brenda) - no tents
access: 46628 US 60, Brenda.
priceTent: No tent sites.
cyclistNotes: Reviewers on The Dyrt report the rule 'No tents or backpacking.' Listed so you skip it. Buckaroos Country Store and Black Rock Cafe are next door in Brenda.

name: Ramsey Mine Rd BLM dispersed
access: Ramsey Mine Rd runs south from US 60 about 1 mile west of Brenda and crosses over I-10 on a bridge (no interchange). Camp along the smaller parallel gravel road on flat, hard ground. From the main I-10 line: exit 31 (mile about 159.5), then about 3.5 miles east on US 60 and south.
priceTent: Free, 14-day maximum.
reservations: First-come.
cyclistNotes: Room for 40-50 rigs, rarely more than 15 (Jan 2026). About 1 mile from Buckaroos Country Store (groceries, sandwiches) and Black Rock Cafe in Brenda. OHVs raise dust on Ramsey Mine Rd itself, and I-10 hum starts around 6am. Fires only Oct-Mar; no wood gathering.

name: Park Place RV Park
access: Paved. I-10 exit 19, then 0.4 mi north on Riggles Ave.
priceTent: No tents. RV night is $45 + tax.
reservations: Book by phone. Register and prepay on arrival.
cyclistNotes: The posted park rules say 'No tents' and full-hookup RVs only, with a 10-year age limit on rigs. Don't plan on it.

name: Quartzsite RV Resort
access: Paved. I-10 exit 19, then north on Riggles Ave.
priceTent: Tent rate not published. A full-hookup RV night is $55 in November 2026.
reservations: OSM gives reception hours of 8am to 7pm. Call ahead.
cyclistNotes: A small park with 27 full-hookup RV sites. The website mentions only RV sites, so ask before counting on a tent.

name: Arizona Sun RV Park
access: Paved. I-10 exit 19, then 1/2 mi north on Plymouth Ave and 1/4 mi on Quail Trail.
priceTent: Tent rate not published. A daily RV site is $47 + $6.20 tax.
reservations: Call for reservations. Check-in is at 1 PM.
cyclistNotes: 126 full-hookup sites with shower houses and laundry. The Dyrt tags it for tents, but the operator only lists RV rates, so call. The park is across the street from BLM desert.

name: Desert Edge RV Park
access: Paved, near I-10 exit 19.
priceTent: unknown
reservations: OSM says reservations are recommended. Call.
cyclistNotes: The park's domain (desertedgervpark.com) now redirects to a parking page, so it may have changed hands. Its status is unverified.

name: Pattie's RV Park & Propane
access: On paved E Main St (Business 10), between exits 19 and 17.
priceTent: unknown
reservations: Small park, call ahead.
cyclistNotes: A small park with back-in full-hookup sites, a smoothie and coffee bar, and laundry (2021 review). It also rents trailers. No tent information.

name: Rice Ranch RV Park
access: Paved streets in town.
priceTent: No tents. RV sites run $42–79.
reservations: Online or by phone.
cyclistNotes: The operator's FAQ says it 'does not offer dry camping or tent sites'. Every stay must be on a full-hookup RV site.

name: Crawford's RV Park
access: On paved E Main St (Business 10).
priceTent: Tent rate not published. Off-season daily RV site is $45 + tax (2026–27 rates).
reservations: Reservations by phone. The park says overnighters are welcome.
cyclistNotes: 67 full-hookup sites, laundry and a rental cabin. The site never mentions tents, so call.

name: Texas BBQ RV Park
address: Quartzsite, AZ (on Main St near I-10)
access: Paved, in town.
priceTent: unknown
reservations: unknown
cyclistNotes: A cheap, basic lot with a bathroom, trash and a dump station, right beside I-10 (2022 reviews). No phone or tent policy found.

name: Split Rail RV Park
access: Paved. About 1.25 mi north of Main St on US 95 (Central Blvd).
priceTent: Tent rate not published. Nightly site is $50.
reservations: Book online or call.
cyclistNotes: New management, with ATV rentals on site. The Dyrt also lists this address as 'Pyramid Lane RV Park' and 'Safari RV Park', which look like old names. No tent policy published.

name: Shady Lane RV Park
access: Paved, two blocks north of Main St on Central Blvd.
priceTent: Tent rate not published. RV was $35 in 2024.
reservations: Reservations by phone. Open Sept 15 to Apr 15.
cyclistNotes: Showers are coin-operated, 50 cents per 5 minutes. Mostly full-time workers live here (Oct 2025 review). One 2023 reviewer arrived late and staff came out to help. The Dyrt's 'tent sites' tag is unverified.

name: Kofa Mountain 55+ RV Park
access: Paved, on Central Blvd.
priceTent: Tent rate not published. RV was $35 (Mar 2026).
reservations: Call. Cash or check only.
cyclistNotes: An age-55-plus RV park. It has community showers but no published tent option, so it is unlikely to take a passing tent.

name: American Trails RV Park & Tiny Cabins
access: Paved, on Central Blvd.
priceTent: Tent rate not published. Daily RV is $45 (30 A) or $50 (50 A), March to November.
reservations: Online through Newbook, or call.
cyclistNotes: About 90 RV sites plus tiny-home rentals, a pool and laundry. A reviewer called it a senior community. Tents aren't mentioned.

name: The Scenic Road RV Park
access: Paved, on Central Blvd.
priceTent: No tents
reservations: Call.
cyclistNotes: The park rules say 'Tent camping is not allowed.'

name: JR's 55+ RV Park
access: Paved, on Central Blvd.
priceTent: No tents. RV was $28.
reservations: Call.
cyclistNotes: An age-55-plus park. OSM tags it tents=no.

name: La Mirage RV Park
address: Quartzsite, AZ (near Main St & Central Blvd)
access: Paved, in town.
priceTent: unknown
reservations: unknown
cyclistNotes: An April 2024 reviewer found no bathrooms or showers, only a laundromat, and called the price outrageous. Skip it.

name: Tyson Wells RV Park (Tyson Wells Market Center)
access: Paved streets in town, just south of Main St and Central Blvd.
priceTent: $25 per overnight, $125 per week, $225 per month plus electricity (operator's 2026 page)
reservations: Call. RV parking season is Oct 1 to Mar 31.
cyclistNotes: The cheapest paid lot in town. It is the swap-meet grounds, and the January shows don't start until Jan 1. A Dec 2021 reviewer was living there in a tent, so tents have been accepted, but the operator doesn't say so: call first. It has toilets and hookups. Showers are unconfirmed.

name: Holiday Palms RV Resort
access: Paved, on W Main St. The streets inside are paved.
priceTent: Tent rate not published. Peak-season (Nov 1 to Apr 30) RV sites start at $65/night plus tax and electric.
reservations: Book online or call. There is an after-hours check-in box at the office door.
cyclistNotes: Has a heated pool, hot tub and clean bathhouses, and is open all year. Its rules and FAQ never mention tents. Pricey for one night.

name: Hassler's RV Park
access: Paved, on W Main St.
priceTent: unknown
reservations: Call. A registration form is on the website.
cyclistNotes: An adult-oriented park under new owners, with the welded 'Mechanical Zoo' sculptures. The Dyrt tags it for tents, but that is unverified.

name: Gunny's RV Park & Military Museum
access: Paved, in town.
priceTent: unknown
reservations: unknown
cyclistNotes: A small RV park run by a retired Marine, with a military museum (2023 review). The Dyrt flags it as no tents. Low value for a cyclist.

name: Burrwood RV Park
address: La Paz Valley Rd, 5 mi south of Quartzsite on US 95, AZ 85346
access: Paved US 95 south about 5 mi.
priceTent: No tents
reservations: Call. Open Oct 1 to Apr 30.
cyclistNotes: An age-55-plus community. Its website says 'No tents, cars, vans, or non-self-contained rigs.'

name: La Paz RV Park
address: 52301 Century, Quartzsite, AZ (about 5 mi south on US 95)
access: Paved US 95 south about 5 mi.
priceTent: unknown
reservations: unknown
cyclistNotes: Only OSM data exists for this park. It is far off the line and not worth the detour.

name: River Sands RV Resort
access: Paved. I-10 exit 1, then about 0.5 mi north on Ehrenberg-Poston Hwy.
priceTent: No tent sites. RV runs $39–112.
reservations: Book on Campspot or call reservations at (928) 298-5097. Office 9am to 5pm, Arizona time.
cyclistNotes: An RV resort that takes only RVs 20 years old or newer, plus cabins and tiny homes. There is no tent option.

name: Villa Verde RV & Mobile Park
access: Paved. I-10 exit 1, then 1/4 mi north on Poston Rd and 1/8 mi west.
priceTent: Unknown. $21 was reported earlier and $40 cash in 2022.
reservations: Pay cash at the office. A 2022 camper said the office staff disappeared.
cyclistNotes: A run-down mobile-home park with some RV sites. A 2021 review says there are no showers and no bathrooms. Use it only as a last resort.

name: Arizona Oasis RV Resort
access: Paved, at I-10 exit 1 on the Arizona riverbank.
priceTent: No tent rate published. RV sites run $63–115.
reservations: Book online (RMS) or call. Check-in 12 PM, check-out 11 AM. The park is gated.
cyclistNotes: An older listing description mentioned 'tent camping', but the 2026 website lists only RV sites, cabins and rentals. Call before counting on it. It has a pool, spa and river beach. The Flying J is next door.

name: Ehrenberg–Cibola Road BLM Dispersed Camping
address: Ehrenberg–Cibola Rd, southeast of Ehrenberg, AZ 85334
access: From the Flying J at I-10 exit 1, take the south frontage road to Cibola Rd, which becomes Ehrenberg–Cibola Rd heading southeast. It is compacted gravel, washboarded for about 2 mi. Pull off onto open BLM desert about 3–3.5 mi from the exit.
priceTent: Free. Rangers enforce the 14-day limit.
reservations: First come, any hour
cyclistNotes: The free fallback on the Arizona bank if the river parks are full or you arrive after the offices close. A Nov 2024 camper said you can barely hear I-10 from here. OHVs can raise dust at times. Fill water at the Flying J or Chevron at exit 1. BLM's Sandbowl page confirms dispersed camping is available in this area.

name: Ehrenberg Sandbowl (BLM OHV area)
address: Off Ehrenberg/Cibola Rd, south of I-10 exit 1, Ehrenberg, AZ
access: BLM directions: from the Ehrenberg exit take the south frontage road about 1 mi west, then turn left onto gravel Ehrenberg/Cibola Rd. The bowl itself is very soft sand, and a 2021 visitor's vehicle got stuck. Expect to push the bike.
priceTent: Free
reservations: None
cyclistNotes: Camping here is legal, but it's an OHV playground with dust and engine noise. Ehrenberg–Cibola Rd, 3.5 mi out, is the better free choice.

name: Levee Road BLM Dispersed Camping (Colorado River, AZ side)
address: Levee Rd south of Ehrenberg, AZ (across the river from McIntyre Park)
access: 8–9 mi south of Ehrenberg on a washboard dirt levee road. One 2018 driver took 1.5 hours to cover 11 mi in an RV. There are OHVs on weekends.
priceTent: Free, 14 days
reservations: None
cyclistNotes: Riverfront spots, but rough, trashy in places and a long dirt slog with a loaded bike (Dec 2025 review). Only worth it if you want the river. McIntyre's paid tent sites are directly across the water.

name: The Cove RV Resort (formerly Riviera RV Resort)
access: Paved. Just over the Colorado River on the California side, at Riviera Dr (I-10 exit 243). It is 0.1–0.5 mi from where the bike/foot bridge and I-10 land. One reviewer called the access road 'sketchy'.
priceTent: Tent rate by phone. RV sites are $60/night plus Blythe's 10% lodging tax.
reservations: Call; the office is open 8am to 5pm daily, California time. The store is open 8–5 Sunday to Thursday and 8–6 Friday and Saturday. A 2020 guest got a site at 9:30 pm, but call ahead for a late arrival.
cyclistNotes: The operator's own listing on The Dyrt (verified 2023) says: 'Backpacking instead of traveling by RV? We have sites to accommodate every kind of traveler, whether by bike, trailer or RV.' Campendium also tags it for tents. The 2026 website lists only RV sites, park models and day use, so confirm the tent rate. Restrooms and showers were recently renovated, and there's coin laundry, a pool and spa, Wi-Fi (new in 2026) and a store. This is the closest paid tent option to the line on the whole segment.

name: Mayflower County Park (Riverside County)
access: All paved. From Hobsonway at Intake Blvd, go north on Intake Blvd (US 95) about 3.3 mi, east on 6th Ave 2.5 mi, then follow Colorado River Rd 0.5 mi to its end in the park. About 6.7 mi one way.
priceTent: Tent or dry site about $35 (2023 dry-camp rate) and possibly higher now. Sites with water and electric were $49 in Sept 2026. Booking yourself online added an $8 fee in 2023.
reservations: Riverside County reservations online (rivcoparks.org blocks automated fetches) or call the office. Check-in is reported quick and friendly. Office hours not verified, so call before arriving late. Maximum stay 14 nights.
cyclistNotes: There is a separate tent and dry-camping area by the river (27 dry sites), plus 152 sites with water and electric for power. Hot showers and flush toilets, but only one bathhouse and it's far from some sites. Water spigots are everywhere, though one reviewer said the water tastes odd. Reviews from Sept and Oct 2026 confirm it's open and clean. There are no services nearby, so shop in Blythe first.

name: McIntyre RV Resort (Peter McIntyre County Park)
address: 8750 Peter D McIntyre Ave, Blythe, CA 92225
access: All paved. From Hobsonway at Intake Blvd, go south on Intake Blvd under I-10 for about 6 mi, then turn left onto Peter D McIntyre Ave (asphalt). About 6.6 mi one way.
priceTent: Standard tent site from $38/night, beachfront tent site from $43 (Campspot, Nov 2026). A 30-amp RV site is $50 if you need power.
reservations: Book on Campspot (campspot.com/park/mcintyre-rv-resort-blythe-ca); walk-ins welcome. Office 7am to 4pm daily, California time.
cyclistNotes: About 20 tent sites on grass by the river, with newly renovated hot showers and restrooms for registered guests, a small store (ice and snacks), free Wi-Fi and a lagoon. New owners since June 1, 2025. A Campspot review from Oct 2026 and a Campendium review from Nov 2025 confirm it's open. Tent sites have no outlet.

name: Hidden Beaches River Resort
access: Paved. Intake Blvd north about 3 mi, then 6th Ave east about 3 mi.
priceTent: No tents. Winter (Oct 1 to Apr 1) RV rate is $50/night.
reservations: Call from 8am.
cyclistNotes: The rates page says 'Our spaces are for fully self contained RVs only' and 'Dry Camping Not Available'. The Dyrt's tent tag is wrong. Don't send a tent here.

name: Burton's Mobile Home & R.V. Park
access: On the line along E Hobsonway.
priceTent: No tents
reservations: unknown
cyclistNotes: A mobile-home park with a few RV sites. OSM tags it tents=no.

name: Midland LTVA
address: Midland–Rice Rd, about 8 mi north of Blythe, CA
access: Paved Lovekin Blvd north, which becomes Midland–Rice Rd after the railroad tracks, about 8–10 mi.
priceTent: No tents. The permit costs $40 for 14 days or $180 for the season, but this LTVA takes only self-contained units.
reservations: Permits from the on-site host
cyclistNotes: BLM limits Midland to self-contained units with a fixed holding tank of at least 10 gallons. There are no toilets and no potable water. Not usable with a tent.

name: BLM land at Wiley's Well Rd, I-10 exit 222 (beside Wiley's Well Rest Area)
address: Wiley's Well Rd at I-10 exit 222 (north side), 15 mi west of Blythe
access: Leave I-10 at exit 222. The Wiley's Well Rest Area sits on Wiley's Well Rd just north of the freeway. Ride a few hundred yards north on paved Wiley's Well Rd, or along the dirt powerline track parallel to I-10, and camp on open BLM desert out of sight of the road. Flat, firm ground.
priceTent: Free; 14-day limit. No LTVA permit is needed because this is outside the Mule Mountain LTVA. Water and flush toilets are at the rest area 0.3 mi away, 24 h.
reservations: None. You may NOT sleep inside the rest area itself: Caltrans has an 8-hour limit and no tents.
cyclistNotes: Not a documented campsite; legal by land status. The BLM surface-management map shows BLM on every side of the interchange, inside Chuckwalla National Monument, and OSM shows no solar fencing here. It is the only spot between Blythe and Chiriaco where a dry camp sits beside water and toilets. It is 10 mi past the last store (BB Travel Center, exit 232) and 50 mi before Chiriaco. Two state prisons are 3 mi south, so stay north of I-10. Check for 'closed to camping' signs. Caltrans plans a rest-area water rebuild with no dates announced.

name: Wiley's Well Campground (Mule Mountain LTVA, BLM)
address: Wiley's Well Rd, 9 mi south of I-10 exit 222
access: Exit 222, then south on Wiley's Well Rd: 3 mi paved past the Chuckwalla Valley and Ironwood state prisons, then 6 mi of graded dirt that is normally washboarded. BLM notice dated Oct 15, 2026: the road was damaged by Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel, is 'impassable for RVs and trailers', and is 4x4 only. A loaded bike will be slow, with possible walking. 18 mi round trip.
priceTent: $40 LTVA short-visit permit, required Sept 15-Apr 15. It covers 14 consecutive days at any CA/AZ LTVA; there is no nightly rate.
reservations: No reservations. Buy the permit from the camp host (not always present) or a BLM office. Tents are allowed only at designated sites within 500 ft of the vault toilet.
cyclistNotes: A real campground with tables, fire rings, a very clean vault toilet, trash and a dump station, but NO water; bring it from the rest area 9 mi back. Coon Hollow, 3 mi further south on the same damaged road, takes the same permit. Probably not worth the detour this week.

name: BLM land at Corn Springs Rd, I-10 exit 201 (south-west of the interchange)
address: Corn Springs Rd / Chuckwalla Valley Rd at I-10 exit 201, 9 mi east of Desert Center
access: Exit 201, south side. Paved Chuckwalla Valley Rd meets Corn Springs Rd at the ramps; go a few hundred yards west of Corn Springs Rd onto BLM desert. Keep clear of the fenced Maverick Solar project north and east of the exit.
priceTent: Free; 14-day limit.
reservations: None.
cyclistNotes: Undocumented; legal by land status (BLM surface-management map, inside Chuckwalla National Monument). It saves the sandy 7.8-mi ride to Corn Springs campground. A dry camp: the nearest water is Wiley's Well RA, 21 mi back, or Chiriaco, 29 mi ahead. Small dirt service roads (pipeline/utility) criss-cross the area.

name: Corn Springs Campground (BLM)
address: Corn Springs Rd, Chuckwalla Mountains, Desert Center, CA 92239
access: Exit 201, then south and west on Corn Springs Rd: about 7-8 mi of compacted/graded dirt with soft sandy wash crossings (a 2019 review said '4WD recommended'), climbing gently to about 1,600 ft. Condition after the October 2026 storm is unknown.
priceTent: $6/night, first come first served, 14-day limit.
reservations: First come, first served: 9 sites including 1 group site, no reservations. Quiet hours 9pm-8am.
cyclistNotes: A palm oasis with petroglyphs, shade ramadas, tables and grills; usually nearly empty midweek. BLM lists potable water, but a Jan 30, 2026 visitor reported 'No water available', so carry all you need. The round trip is more than 15 mi of dirt and sand. The Countri Bike rider (2016-17) considered it and went on to Chiriaco.

name: Lake Tamarisk Desert Resort (no tents)
access: Paved: exit 192, then 2 mi north on Rice Rd (CA 177) and Parkview Dr.
priceTent: Tents not allowed. Park rules: 'Only one RV per site - everyone must sleep in the RV; no tent camping' and 'Tents and outdoor sleeping is not permitted.' RV sites start at $50/night including electricity.
reservations: RoverPass online or phone. Check-in is at 1 pm; register at the office.
cyclistNotes: The only campground at Desert Center, and it bans tents. It is a 55+ park, and RVs must be 15 years old or newer. The county library next door has water Tue/Thu 10-6 and Sat 10-2.

name: BLM land south of Desert Center, I-10 exit 192
address: South side of I-10 exit 192, Desert Center, CA 92239
access: Exit 192 (Desert Center). On the south side a rough dirt track (OSM grade 4) runs south-west across BLM land; camp a few hundred yards in. Off limits: the town lots, the Caltrans yard, and the fenced Oberon/Athos solar fields north and east of the exit.
priceTent: Free; 14-day limit.
reservations: None.
cyclistNotes: Undocumented; legal by land status (BLM surface-management map). Halfway between Blythe and Chiriaco. Desert Center has NO store, water or gas, so carry dinner, breakfast and water for the 19 mi to Chiriaco. Lake Tamarisk Library, 2 mi north, has a fountain only Tue/Thu/Sat in the daytime.

name: BLM land north of Eagle Mountain Rd, I-10 exit 189
address: Eagle Mountain Rd at I-10 exit 189, 3 mi west of Desert Center
access: Exit 189, then north on paved Eagle Mountain Rd. BLM desert lies on both sides just north of the interchange.
priceTent: Free; 14-day limit.
reservations: None.
cyclistNotes: Undocumented; legal by land status (BLM surface-management map; no solar fields mapped here). An alternative to the Desert Center exit. Dry camp.

name: Red Cloud Mine Road Dispersed Camping (BLM)
address: Red Cloud Mine Rd at I-10 exit 182, Desert Center, CA 92239
access: Exit 182 (Red Cloud Rd), south side. A big gravel lot sits right by I-10, and dispersed sites run along a 2.2-mi graded dirt road toward the Chuckwalla Mtns. Light washboard and dips, with soft sand in places: a 2WD van got stuck in 2022.
priceTent: Free; 14-day limit.
reservations: None.
cyclistNotes: The only DOCUMENTED dispersed area near the line between Blythe and Chiriaco (Campendium, 6 reviews, latest Apr 2023). Freeway noise near the lot, a high-voltage line nearby, Border Patrol around. It is 9.5 mi before the Chiriaco store, which makes it the stop if daylight runs out (sunset is about 4:45 pm PST). No water.

name: Chiriaco Summit - Patton Museum Dry Camp Area
address: Behind the General Patton Memorial Museum, 62450 Chiriaco Rd, Chiriaco Summit, CA 92201
access: Exit 173. Paved to the museum, then take the dirt access road on the right side of the museum (sign: 'Welcome to Chiriaco Summit Dry Camp Area') to marked sites behind it. About 0.3 mi; the Chevron and cafe are about 400 m away.
priceTent: Free. There are no facilities at the sites; water and restrooms are at the Chevron food mart (open 24 h) and the coffee shop, 400 m away.
reservations: First come, first served. A camp host takes your name and plate number. If you arrive after dark, set up and check in the next morning (Dec 2024 review). Maximum stay is 5-7 nights.
cyclistNotes: The key camp on this segment: free, hosted, on BLM land, with marked sites including tent-only spots and stone fire rings. The NPS lists Chiriaco Summit as a camping option south of the park. Nearby: the Chevron food mart (24 h), Foster's Freeze (8am-9pm) and the coffee shop (6am-11pm). A 2021 reviewer got free water at the station. Some I-10 truck noise. A cyclist camped here in 2016 and sat in the coffee shop until it closed. A Jan 2026 reviewer described a dozen trucks parked in the area, so confirm with the host or the store. It is 68 mi from Blythe and 49 mi from the last water at Wiley's Well.

name: Joshua Tree South BLM Dispersed Camping (Cottonwood Springs Rd)
address: Cottonwood Springs Rd at I-10 exit 168 (north side), 4 mi west of Chiriaco Summit
access: Exit 168, then north on paved Cottonwood Springs Rd; dirt roads branch east and west just north of the freeway and are passable by car. Camp only in the BLM sections on the NPS map: east of the road between I-10 and the Edison power-line road, west of the road north of the power line, and a block further east. It is checkerboarded with private land, and the NPS says to camp 300+ ft from roadways.
priceTent: Free; 14-day limit.
reservations: None, first come. There are hundreds of fire-ring sites and it effectively never fills.
cyclistNotes: 155 Campendium reviews through May 2026; a 2024 tent camper liked it, and the NPS BLM map was updated May 2026. The ground is crushed granite and sand, with little freeway noise. Mostly RVs, busier on weekends; good Verizon/T-Mobile coverage. No water: fill at Chiriaco, 4.3 mi east, or at Cottonwood, 6 mi uphill (needs the $15 park entry). This is also mile ~4 of the Mecca variant.

name: Cottonwood Campground (Joshua Tree National Park)
address: Pinto Basin Rd by the Cottonwood Visitor Center, Joshua Tree National Park
access: Exit 168, then 7 mi north on paved Cottonwood Springs Rd/Pinto Basin Rd, climbing about 1,250 ft (1,750 to 3,000 ft). Slow when loaded; return the same way. The NPS describes the park's paved roads as crumbling and uneven.
priceTent: $35/site/night (up to 6 people and 3 tents), plus a $15 per-person 7-day park entry on a bike. Group tent-only sites cost $55.
reservations: Reservation only, year-round, on recreation.gov. There is NO cell service at the campground, so book before leaving I-10. Check-in at noon; the campground is open 24 h. Availability on the night of Nov 1: 43-50 sites free for Mon-Thu Nov 2-5 and Mon Nov 9, 26 for Sun Nov 8, but only 1 site (B16) left for each of Fri Nov 6 and Sat Nov 7.
cyclistNotes: The only campground with potable water and flush toilets between Blythe and Indio; no showers. Limit is 14 nights Oct-May. A riding group in Dec 2019 found it full, and rangers enforced the rules. The only current park alert is the Geology Tour Rd flood closure, which is not on this route. Worth the climb only for water and a proper site.

name: Box Canyon Rd / Mecca Hills BLM dispersed camping (ROAD CLOSED)
address: Box Canyon Rd (old SR 195) through the Mecca Hills, between I-10 exit 168 and Mecca
access: CLOSED. A BLM notice dated Oct 21, 2026, still posted Nov 1, says: 'Box Canyon Road is closed from Pinto Road to Painted Canyon Road due to flooding damage from Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel'; follow the Riverside County closure signs. When open, the road is paved and descends gently, with BLM land at variant miles ~12-19. My reading is that the 5.8 mi between Mecca and Painted Canyon Rd lie outside the closure; that is an inference, not stated.
priceTent: Free (when the road is open).
reservations: None.
cyclistNotes: Cyclists wild-camped in the canyon in Oct 2023 (on a closed road) and Mar 2024. Camp only in the non-wilderness road corridor: bikes are banned in the Mecca Hills Wilderness on both sides. Never camp in a wash bottom, and expect wind to blow sand into the tent. Near the canyon mouth (variant mile ~20) the land is tribal (BIA), where you cannot camp.

name: Thousand Trails Palm Springs RV Resort
access: Paved and flat. On Varner Rd just north of I-10 at Washington St, about 0.5 mi off the line.
priceTent: No tent site type is offered. Non-member RV sites were about $46/night (Campendium, Dec 2025). WiFi costs extra.
reservations: Non-members can book nightly online. Campsite check-in is at noon; the office is open Mon-Fri 9-5. A reviewer advises arriving in daylight.
cyclistNotes: Open for the season 9/15/2026-5/15/2027. Its rules allow '1 RV, 2 vehicles, and 2 tents' per site, but booking only offers RV back-in and pull-through sites. Call and ask whether a tent-only cyclist can take an RV site. It has a pool, spa, showers and laundry, and sits right on the line.

name: DragonflyHill Desert Farm (Hipcamp)
access: About 9.6 mi from the line in north Palm Springs (N Palm Canyon at Via Escuela) via Gene Autry Trail, 20th Ave, Mountain View Rd and Long Canyon Rd/21st Ave (bike router). The last mile is a maintained dirt road. About 200-250 ft of net climbing (to about 770 ft). The host sends directions because phone GPS is often wrong.
address: 21st Ave area between Palm Springs and Desert Hot Springs (exact address after booking)
priceTent: $39/night, $45.93 with Hipcamp fees, for the 'Under Desert Skies' tent/RV site with power and water hookups.
