reservations: Request to book (not instant). The host approves, then emails registration and waiver forms, and gives a 15-minute orientation on arrival. Full refund if you cancel 3 or more days ahead. Request at least a day or two before you arrive.
cyclistNotes: The closest good tent spot to Palm Springs: hot outdoor showers, accessible porta-potties, mineral well water and an outdoor kitchen. 575 bookings, 97% recommend. The host warns of frequent high winds and near-freezing winter nights. The pool is winterized mid-Oct to April. It is a sober community farm.

name: Palm Springs / Joshua Tree KOA
access: About 11.7 mi from the line in north Palm Springs (N Palm Canyon at Via Escuela) via Gene Autry Trail, 20th Ave and Mountain View Rd to Dillon Rd (bike router). The router uses some minor desert roads, and Dillon Rd is the paved fallback. You climb about 500 ft, to roughly 1,040 ft.
address: 70405 Dillon Rd, Desert Hot Springs, CA 92241
priceTent: Tent rate not found (the KOA site blocks automated reading). A 2021 tent camper called the price 'a bit much'. RV sites ran about $91 (Jun 2025).
reservations: Book with KOA online or by phone. Office hours and after-hours check-in not confirmed; staff escort guests to sites.
cyclistNotes: The only conventional tent campground between Indio and Whitewater: a 287-site resort with a separate tent area (sinks shared), keypad bathhouses with private showers, a hot-spring pool and hot tub, a store and coin laundry. A Mar 2025 review mentions strong wind hitting tents. Reviews run through Mar 2026. The detour is about 23 mi round trip, so treat it as a fallback.

name: Joshua Tree, Palm Springs, Coachella Adjacent (private campground, The Dyrt)
access: About 11.1 mi from the line in north Palm Springs via Gene Autry Trail, 20th Ave, Mountain View Rd and minor roads near Corkill Rd (bike router). The last roads may be sandy. Climb of about 450 ft.
address: Desert Hot Springs, Dillon Rd/Corkill Rd area (exact address on booking)
priceTent: $15-25/night (The Dyrt listing).
reservations: Request to book on The Dyrt (the host approves). Call or text ahead.
cyclistNotes: A fenced private desert lot with hot showers, drinking water, toilets and a small camp store, but no shade. The cheapest option in the Desert Hot Springs cluster. Rated 5.0 from 4 reviews dated 2023 to Mar 2026, so it looks active.

name: Catalina Spa & RV Resort
access: About 10.4 mi from the line in north Palm Springs via Gene Autry Trail, 20th Ave, Mountain View Rd and Corkill Rd (bike router). Climb of about 400 ft.
address: 18800 Corkill Rd, Desert Hot Springs, CA 92241
priceTent: No tent rate. RV sites from $45/night with free electricity and water (operator site, 2026).
reservations: RV check-in is at noon. After the office closes, resort ambassadors park late arrivals until 9 pm. The manager decides which rigs are accepted.
cyclistNotes: Hot-springs RV resort, open year round, under new management. The operator's pages list only RV sites and cottages; The Dyrt has a generic tent/RV tag. Call and ask whether they will take a tent.

name: Sam's Family Spa Hot Water Resort
access: About 12.4 mi from the line in north Palm Springs via Gene Autry Trail, 20th Ave, Mountain View Rd and Dillon Rd area roads (bike router). Climb of about 550 ft (to about 1,110 ft).
address: 70875 Dillon Rd, Desert Hot Springs, CA 92241
priceTent: No tent rate. RV sites from $85/night with 2 resort wristbands (operator site, 2026).
reservations: Book online or by phone. RV check-in is 2-3 pm; the operator's own pages disagree. Late stays must re-register at the office. A Mar 2026 late arrival got no welcome packet or bathroom code.
cyclistNotes: The Dyrt still lists tent sites, but the 2026 operator site lists only RV sites, tiny homes, studios and motel rooms. Treat it as call-first. 24-h keypad restrooms and showers, 4 mineral pools.

name: Rancho Capotista (private desert campground, The Dyrt)
access: About 12.6 mi from the line in north Palm Springs via Gene Autry Trail, 20th Ave, Mountain View Rd and minor desert roads (bike router), less than 1 mi from the KOA. Climb of about 600 ft, to roughly 1,140 ft.
address: Desert Hot Springs, near the Palm Springs/Joshua Tree KOA (exact address on booking)
priceTent: $40/night (The Dyrt).
reservations: Request to book; the host takes reservations by phone.
cyclistNotes: 'Raw desert camping' where you pick any spot on the property. The listing shows water hookups and trash pickup but no toilets or showers. Only one review (2023). Low priority.

name: Relaxing Hide Away (Hipcamp)
access: About 12.8 mi from the line in north Palm Springs via Gene Autry Trail, 20th Ave, Mountain View Rd and the Dillon Rd area (bike router). Climb of about 700 ft, to roughly 1,230 ft, at Desert Edge east of Desert Hot Springs. This is beyond the 10-mi target.
address: Desert Edge, east of Desert Hot Springs (exact address after booking)
priceTent: Site 1: $50/night, $58.89 with Hipcamp fees, with water and power hookups. Site 2: $40, $47.11 with fees, toilet only.
reservations: Hipcamp Instant Book.
cyclistNotes: A 10-acre dark-sky desert lot with a hot tub. 93% recommend (51 ratings, 121 bookings). Only worth the ride if nothing nearer works.

name: Scorpion Ranch (Hipcamp)
access: About 13.7 mi from the line in north Palm Springs via Gene Autry Trail, 20th Ave, Mountain View Rd and the Dillon Rd area (bike router). Climb of about 800 ft, to roughly 1,300 ft. This is beyond the 10-mi target.
address: Desert Hot Springs, Desert Edge area (exact address after booking)
priceTent: $40/night, $47.01 with Hipcamp fees, for the 'Scorpion Ranch Camping' tent site.
reservations: Hipcamp Instant Book.
cyclistNotes: A 5-acre retro ranch with mesquite and palm shade, a toilet and water but no shower. 98% recommend (52 ratings). Far off the line.

name: Palm Springs Oasis RV Resort
access: Paved and flat. On Date Palm Dr in Cathedral City, about 0.4 mi off the line.
address: 36100 Date Palm Dr, Cathedral City, CA 92234
priceTent: No tent rate. Non-member RV site about $95 (Jan 2024 review).
reservations: Thousand Trails/Encore booking; ask by phone.
cyclistNotes: An Encore/Thousand Trails park. All 140 sites are full-hookup RV pads, mostly long-term guests, under the airport approach. Reviewers complain about the showers. Expect a no on tents, but it is right on the line.

name: Happy Traveler RV Park (aka Happy Traveller)
access: Paved and flat. About 1.4 mi from the line through south Palm Springs streets to W Mesquite Ave. About 1.1 mi from downtown.
address: 211 W Mesquite Ave, Palm Springs, CA 92264
priceTent: No tent rate published (call for rates). RV sites about $100 (Nov 2025).
reservations: Call or email happytrav@hotmail.com. A night manager is on site.
cyclistNotes: The only campground in central Palm Springs, sheltered from the valley winds. The operator lists only full-hookup RV sites and says nothing about tents. Call. Reviewers say the bathhouse is dated.

name: Windy Point x Palm Springs (Hipcamp off-grid lot)
access: Paved and flat. Just off CA-111 at Windy Point via Overture Dr/Palm Oasis Ave, about 0.5 mi off the line. You enter over a 6-inch curb.
address: Palm Oasis Ave area, Windy Point, north Palm Springs (exact address after booking)
priceTent: $30.40/night, $37.63 with Hipcamp fees.
reservations: Hipcamp Instant Book. The host sends a custom wind report before your stay.
cyclistNotes: A 7,500 sq ft lot with a 5-ft chain-link fence, a lockable gate, a streetlight and a picnic table. It is completely self-contained: no water, toilet, power or trash, and the host asks you to bring a portable toilet. The host warns that 'Standard free-standing tents generally don't work here' because gusts can reach gale force. Book it only when the forecast is light, and read the host's wind report. NWS shows easterly flow Nov 5-8, which can still gust at the pass mouth. Water and snacks at Windy Cove Market & Gas, 60490 Overture Dr. 98% recommend (20 ratings).

name: Whitewater Preserve campground (Wildlands Conservancy)
access: Paved. Leave CA-111 at Tipton Rd and follow Whitewater Cutoff to Whitewater Canyon Rd at Bonnie Bell, then 4.2 mi up the 2-lane canyon road to the preserve. That is about 6.5-9.5 mi from the line depending on the turn (the bike router gives 9.5 mi from the I-10/CA-111 junction). You climb about 1,000 ft (roughly 1,100 to 2,190 ft). Next morning, descend and get on I-10 westbound at the Whitewater exit, which is bike-legal there.
priceTent: Free (donations appreciated).
reservations: Reserve at least 48 h ahead with the online request form (check the campground calendar first). Walk-ins are accepted only if the campground is not full and you check in at the ranger station before 4:15 pm. The preserve is open 8 am-5 pm. Check-out 11 am. Up to 3 nights per 30 days; capacity 30 guests a day. Reservations can be cancelled for hazardous weather.
cyclistNotes: The best-value stop on the segment: a free tent area with flush toilets, drinking water, a river and ponds. No fires of any kind, no generators, and no cell signal on site (signal starts about 3.5 mi down the road). The WHOLE PRESERVE WAS CLOSED SUN 11/1/2026 for hazardous weather and flood conditions, and the operator warns of more El Nino closures this winter. Confirm with whitewaterpreserve@wildlandsconservancy.org or by phone, and submit the form by about Nov 3 for a Nov 5-6 night. If you miss the 4:15 pm check-in, fall back to the Windy Point lot or to Banning KOA (about 15 mi on, with after-hours self check-in).

name: BLM land along lower Whitewater Canyon Rd (Sand to Snow NM), unverified dispersed camping
access: Paved road. About 1.5-2.5 mi up Whitewater Canyon Rd from Bonnie Bell, roughly 5 mi from the line. The BLM parcels are mixed in with private land, and boundaries are not marked as far as we know.
priceTent: Free, if camping is legal there.
reservations: None. Unverified; ask BLM before relying on it.
cyclistNotes: The BLM land-status map shows BLM parcels beside the lower canyon road inside Sand to Snow National Monument. The monument page sends campers to BLM's general dispersed-camping rules but says nothing about this canyon, and no camper or rider report was found. Last resort only, for example if you miss the preserve's 4:15 pm check-in. Stay out of sight of homes and make no fire. The pass mouth is very windy.

name: Cabazon Escape (private lot, The Dyrt)
access: Paved local streets. About 3-3.5 mi southeast of central Cabazon via Main St, Broadway, Bonita Ave and Almond St (the bike router gives 5.5 mi from the I-10 line). At about 1,520 ft, it is lower than Cabazon.
address: 0.12-acre lot southeast of Cabazon (no street address listed)
priceTent: unknown (the listing shows a $1 placeholder).
reservations: Request to book on The Dyrt, or by phone or email.
cyclistNotes: Listed in 2023 for tents and RVs. One of its two reviews (2023) called it 'more like a landfill' and left at once; the other, by a Dyrt staffer, praised waterfall access. It may be inactive. Call first; it is the only private listing at the Cabazon end.

name: Morongo Casino Resort & Spa (no camping)
access: On Seminole Dr beside I-10 in Cabazon, on the line.
priceTent: No camping. RV and overnight parking has been discontinued.
reservations: n/a
cyclistNotes: Don't plan on the casino. Reviews from Jun and Dec 2025 say RV and overnight parking is no longer offered (trucks only), and hotel guests may not sleep in vehicles. Use it for water, food and restrooms only. It sits on Morongo Reservation land.

name: Banning Stagecoach KOA
access: Paved and slightly downhill. From Ramsey St (the line) ride about 1 mi south on S San Gorgonio Ave (CA-243) under I-10. The ride back up next morning is mild, about 120 ft.
address: 1455 S San Gorgonio Ave, Banning, CA 92220
priceTent: Tent rate not found (koa.com blocks automated reading). Recent nightly reports, probably for RV sites: $50 (2022) and $54 (2025). Tent sites 95-99 have water only, no power.
reservations: Book with KOA online or by phone. The office closes around 5-6 pm (2022 review), but self check-in is available after hours; registration packets are left at the office.
cyclistNotes: The only campground in the Cabazon-Banning-Beaumont stretch confirmed to take tents (sites 95-99), and the safest late-arrival option in the pass. It is gravel and RV-oriented (a 2016 reviewer said it is 'really not for tent camping'), with one bathhouse. 2025-26 reviews report broken sprinklers, overgrown grass and occasional broken toilets. The pool is closed in winter, and train horns carry at night. Reviews continue through May 2026.

name: Silent Valley Club (membership RV resort)
access: Paved but a big climb. About 9 mi south up CA-243 (San Gorgonio Ave) from Banning, then about 1 mi west on Poppet Flats Rd (10.6 mi by bike router). Net climb about 1,250 ft, to roughly 3,580 ft. Not practical on a loaded bike.
address: Poppet Flats Rd off CA-243, south of Banning
priceTent: unknown (membership resort).
reservations: Membership basis; whether non-members can stay is not stated.
cyclistNotes: Listed with tent sites, but it is members-only and far uphill. Included only so it is not mistaken for a nearby option.

name: Country Hills RV Park
access: Paved. About 1.7 mi from the line in Beaumont via Pennsylvania Ave, 1st St, Michigan Ave and Roadrunner Dr, south of I-10 (bike router). The park is gated and needs a gate card.
priceTent: No tent rate. Full-hookup RV site $68/night for 2 people, plus a one-time $15 resort fee (operator site, 2026). Showers take quarters.
reservations: Book online or by phone with a credit card; cancel at least 72 h ahead. Check-in 1 pm. Gated, so call ahead for a late arrival (a 2023 guest arranged one).
cyclistNotes: The park rules are written entirely for RVs and say nothing about tents; The Dyrt's 'tent sites' tag is generic. Call before counting on it. Laundry is reported to cost $10 a load because of a card system.

name: Noble Creek Regional Park RV campground (Beaumont-Cherry Valley Recreation and Park District)
access: Paved and flat. About 0.8 mi west of Beaumont Ave on Oak Valley Pkwy.
address: 650 W Oak Valley Pkwy, Beaumont, CA 92223
priceTent: $35/night (2022) to $35-50 (The Dyrt), for RV sites. There are 9 dry sites.
reservations: Required. Currently by phone or office@bcvparks.com to the district office only (Mon-Thu 8-5, Fri 8-noon). No on-site check-in was reported.
cyclistNotes: The district's 2026 brochure lists 24 full-hookup, 15 half-hookup and 9 dry-camping sites. 2022 reviewers called it a parking lot with no visitor restrooms. The Dyrt shows tent sites and toilets, but no review confirms tents. A district notice says the park was closed for fire-camp operations one summer. Call.

name: Bogart Regional Park campground (Cherry Valley)
access: Paved, with about 400 ft of climbing (2,785 to 3,180 ft). From the line at Beaumont Ave and Cherry Valley Blvd, ride 2.3 mi via Cherry Valley Blvd, Live Oak Ave, Vineland/Noble/Dutton St and Cherry Ave (bike router). It is about 2 mi past the segment end.
address: 9600 International Park Rd (Cherry Ave), Cherry Valley, CA 92223
priceTent: $35/night (sites 1-30); pets $2/day (district fee page).
reservations: Book by phone or office@bcvparks.com with the district office, Mon-Thu 8-5 and Fri 8-noon. Online booking is suspended 'until further notice'. The park is open 7 am-sundown, with an attendant only Sat-Sun 8-3. The gate may be shut in the evening (a reviewer arriving after 5 pm worked the gate switch themselves). Max stay 7 nights.
cyclistNotes: A shaded foothill campground run by the local park district with flush restrooms and drinking water. At 3,180 ft it runs a few degrees colder than Banning, where lows of 51-57 F are forecast. The district warns of bears, and a campfire ban was in place at its last notice. Tents were barred during COVID (a cyclist found it closed to tents in 2021), but reviewers tent-camped in Aug 2025. Call by Friday noon for a weekend night.

name: Desert Shores Motorcoach Resort (Class A only, no tents)
access: Paved. South Indio, about 2.5 mi off the line.
priceTent: No tents: private Class A-only lots for sale or lease.
reservations: n/a
cyclistNotes: A private gated community of individually owned Class A lots. It is not a campground.

name: Emerald Desert RV Resort (no tents)
access: Paved. On the line at Frank Sinatra Dr, Palm Desert.
address: 76000 Frank Sinatra Dr, Palm Desert, CA 92211
priceTent: No tents. RV sites about $110-125 (2025-26).
reservations: n/a for tents
cyclistNotes: Operator rules: 'Tent Camping Not permitted. RVs must be self-contained.'

name: Outdoor Resort Palm Springs (no tents)
access: Paved. Ramon Rd, Cathedral City, about 1.6 mi off the line.
priceTent: No tents: owner-lot RV resort.
reservations: n/a for tents
cyclistNotes: Rental rules: '...tent trailers, pop-up trailers, tents, van conversions... are not allowed'.

name: Sky Valley Resort (self-contained RVs only, no tents)
access: About 10-11 mi north of the line on Dillon Rd in Sky Valley.
address: 74711 Dillon Rd, Desert Hot Springs, CA 92241
priceTent: No tents.
reservations: n/a for tents
cyclistNotes: The reservation terms say vehicles without an onboard bathroom are not allowed and units must be self-contained.

name: Fisherman's Retreat (San Timoteo Canyon)
access: Paved: about 6.3 mi from Cherry Valley Blvd/Calimesa Blvd (mile ~358.6) via Palmer Ave and San Timoteo Canyon Rd, about 785 ft downhill going in. On to Redlands is 10–11 mi via San Timoteo Canyon Rd and Alessandro Rd (470–730 ft of climbing), rejoining the line at ~mile 366–368, so the detour costs about 10 mi.
address: 32300 San Timoteo Canyon Rd, Redlands, CA 92373
priceTent: unknown
reservations: Unknown; call. It is a membership resort (Halo Resorts) with a separate non-member area.
cyclistNotes: Private RV resort on three stocked fishing lakes, with a store, restaurant and pool. Runs as a membership park with a non-member section. The Dyrt lists showers, drinking water and toilets. Non-member nightly rates, tent policy and 2026 status are all unverified (no website, Facebook only). Long detour into the canyon.

name: Yucaipa Regional Park
access: Paved: about 4.7 mi from Calimesa Blvd (Hist US 99, mile ~360.8) via Avenue G, Wildwood Canyon Rd, Yucaipa Blvd and 5th St to Oak Glen Rd, about 570 ft of climbing. On to Redlands via Oak Glen Rd, Avenue D, 17th St and Tennessee St is about 7 mi, rejoining at ~mile 366, so the detour costs about 6 mi. Stay on paved roads; routers may suggest the Crafton Hills Ridge Trail.
priceTent: Tent spaces A–I. The county lists $35 Mon–Thu / $45 Fri–Sun for no-hookup sites (max 6 people), and group tent camping at $5/person plus a $20 group fee. Add a $10 non-refundable reservation fee. Seniors/veterans/military get $5 off Sun–Thu. Expect roughly $35–55 total for one person.
reservations: Online only at parkreservations.sbcounty.gov, at least 24 h ahead (no same-day booking). Check-in 3 pm. If you arrive after the 5 pm closing, go straight to your site; after-hours instructions come in the confirmation email (check spam). Park hours are 7:30 am–5 pm from Oct 31, 2026 to May 2027.
cyclistNotes: San Bernardino County park with 9 designated tent spaces (A–I on the park map) next to the 42-site RV loop; tents are allowed only there. The county lists hot showers and restrooms, but a 2024 reviewer in group site A said there were no showers near the tent area. Potable water, fire rings, three fishing lakes. A June 2025 reviewer camped in 'tent site E'. Elevation about 2,600 ft, and power-safety shutoffs are possible. The park also closes on the third Wednesday of November (Nov 18), after his window.

name: The Unhitched Ranch (Hipcamp)
access: Paved but hilly: about 9 mi from Barton Rd (Loma Linda, mile ~372.7) via Barton Rd and Reche Canyon Rd, a narrow two-lane canyon road with commuter traffic; about 900 ft of climbing. Leave via Reche Canyon Rd and Washington St to Colton (7.5 mi, rejoining at ~mile 375), so the detour costs about 14 mi. The exact address comes after booking.
address: Reche Canyon, Colton/Loma Linda area (exact address after booking)
priceTent: $99.51/night base for the ranch's RV/tent site (about $117 with Hipcamp fees)
reservations: Hipcamp request-to-book (the host approves). Usually one group at a time on the ranch.
cyclistNotes: Family-run Clydesdale and longhorn ranch of about 40 acres, with wild burros nearby. Potable water, toilets, laundry, Wi-Fi, electric and water hookups, campfires allowed. 168 bookings, 100% recommend. Expensive for one rider, and the climb in is steep. The Hipcamp map pin is approximate.

name: Riverview Ranch (Hipcamp)
access: Paved: about 8.7 mi south from the line in Rialto (mile ~383) via Cactus Ave, Bloomington Ave, Cedar Ave, 34th St and Riverview Dr, mostly downhill (about 550 ft). Back to the Pacific Electric Trail is about 11 mi via Crestmore Rd, Rubidoux Blvd and Locust Ave (about 650 ft up, rejoining at ~mile 386), so the detour costs about 16 mi.
address: Jurupa Valley near Mt. Rubidoux (exact address after booking)
priceTent: $33.25/night base for the tent site (about $39 with Hipcamp fees)
reservations: Hipcamp instant book; arrival details come after booking.
cyclistNotes: Private, shaded property near Mt. Rubidoux and the Santa Ana River. The listing promises clean bathrooms and hot showers, plus potable water, a shared fire ring, picnic tables and Wi-Fi. The tent site has 36 bookings and the listing is 95% recommended. It is next door to Rancho Jurupa and is a cheaper, quieter alternative. The map pin is approximate.

name: Rancho Jurupa Regional Park
access: Paved: about 8.9 mi south from the line in Rialto (mile ~383) via Cactus Ave, Bloomington Ave, Cedar Ave, 34th St and Wallace St, mostly downhill (about 500 ft). To rejoin, take Crestmore Rd, Rubidoux Blvd and Locust Ave to the Pacific Electric Trail (11 mi, about 650 ft up, ~mile 386), so the detour costs about 17 mi.
priceTent: $40–55 per site per night (2025–26 reports; $55 is full hookup). No separate tent rate found.
reservations: Reserve at rivcoparks.org or 800-234-7275. Walk-ups register at the staffed entrance gate (single-file line). Late arrivals with a reservation get gate, bathroom and laundry codes (Dec 2025 review).
cyclistNotes: Large Riverside County campground on the Santa Ana River. The Lakeview side has gravel roads with water/electric sites; the Cottonwood side has paved full-hookup sites. Tents are allowed. Showers on both sides (tokens on the Lakeview side), laundry, a small store, ranger patrols. Busy and loud on weekends. A ranger warned campers to lock up bikes in 2020. rivcoparks.org blocks automated fetches, so fees come from reviews.

name: Harmony Heaven Campyard (Hipcamp)
access: Paved: about 3.5 mi north of the Pacific Electric Trail (mile ~397.6) via Hellman Ave, Lemon Ave, Beryl St and Carnelian St, about 570 ft of climbing. Back down to the trail at Carnelian St is 4 mi (~mile 399), so the detour costs about 6 mi. The exact address comes after booking.
address: Alta Loma, Rancho Cucamonga (exact address after booking)
priceTent: $64/night base for 'Starlight', a pre-pitched 4-person safari tent (about $75 with fees). A-frame campers from $79.
reservations: Hipcamp instant book.
cyclistNotes: Private half-acre 'campyard'. You sleep in the host's safari tent; no bring-your-own-tent site is listed, so ask the host. Private outdoor bathroom with a hot shower, outdoor kitchen, fire pit, pool, Wi-Fi, laundry and farm animals. 12 bookings, 100% recommend. It is the only tent-style stay near the Pacific Electric Trail between Rialto and Pomona. The map pin is approximate.

name: Fairplex RV Park (former Los Angeles/Pomona Fairplex KOA)
access: Paved and flat: 1.1 mi from Bonita Ave via White Ave (mile ~408). Back to Bonita Ave is 2.1 mi, so the detour costs about 2 mi.
priceTent: unknown; call (2020 reports: about $50–75 per site)
reservations: Call or book online; 72-h cancellation policy. Office hours are not published.
cyclistNotes: 183 full-hookup sites plus cabins beside the LA County Fairgrounds. Showers, laundry, heated pool and spa, mini-market, free Wi-Fi. As a KOA it sold tent sites with electric (2020 review), and The Dyrt and Campendium still list tent sites. It is no longer a KOA, and its own website now advertises only RV sites and cabins, so confirm tents by phone. Sites are tight and some are near traffic. The new Metro A Line stations at La Verne and Pomona (opened Sept 2025) are within a couple of miles.

name: Bonelli Bluffs RV Resort & Campground
access: Paved: about 2.6 mi from Bonita Ave (San Dimas, mile ~409) via Wheeler Ave and Puddingstone Dr to the resort entrance on Camper View Rd, about 200 ft of climbing onto the bluff. Continue via Puddingstone Dr and Walnut Ave back to Bonita Ave (3.7 mi, ~mile 411), so the detour costs about 4 mi. Avoid the park's dirt trails that routers suggest.
address: 1440 Camper View Rd, San Dimas, CA 91773
priceTent: $30/night walk-in tent site for up to 2 people; +$10 per extra person (max 6); pets $2/day
reservations: Tent sites can't be booked online; call 909-599-8355. The guest-service lobby and market are open Sun–Wed 8 am–5 pm and Thu–Sat 8 am–7 pm. A kiosk is open 24 h, with an after-hours line.
cyclistNotes: The best-equipped tent option in the LA basin: walk-in grass tent sites with picnic tables and fire pits above Puddingstone Lake. Clean restrooms, showers, laundry (6 am–11 pm), two pools, a market and free Wi-Fi. The tent area is on a slope with a carry from parking, so wheel the bike in. Expect small-plane noise from Brackett Field and occasional late weekend parties. LA County day-use areas close Mon/Tue, but the resort office lists hours every day. It is 31 line-miles from the theater, and the Metro A Line San Dimas station is a few miles away.

name: Marshall Canyon Regional Park campground
access: Paved and steep: about 6.3 mi north from Bonita Ave/White Ave in La Verne (mile ~407) into the foothills, about 1,070 ft of climbing.
address: La Verne foothills, CA 91750 (street address not verified)
priceTent: unknown
reservations: Reservation only, through LA County Parks (reservations.lacounty.gov). It appears geared to groups. LA County regional parks are closed Mondays and Tuesdays.
cyclistNotes: LA County says the park has 'forty campsites' with barbecues and a fire circle, available for reservation, next to the Marshall Canyon equestrian center. I found no details on individual bookings, fees or restrooms. Long climb. Use it only if Bonelli Bluffs and Fairplex are full.

name: Gould Mesa Trail Camp (Angeles NF)
access: 6.2 mi from Colorado Blvd (Pasadena, mile ~434.6): Orange Grove Blvd, Rosemont Ave and Arroyo Blvd to the Windsor Ave/Ventura St trailhead (paved, about 600 ft up), then 2 mi up the Gabrielino Trail (dirt and broken pavement, several creek crossings; bikes allowed). About 820 ft of climbing in all. From camp to the Elysian Theater is 11.9 mi.
address: Gabrielino Trail, Arroyo Seco, about 2 mi above the Windsor Ave/Ventura St trailhead, Altadena/La Cañada Flintridge
priceTent: Free (no camping fee; the Adventure Pass applies only to parked vehicles)
reservations: First-come, first-served; no reservations. Arrive before dark because of the creek crossings (sunset about 4:55 pm).
cyclistNotes: Free primitive trail camp with about 6–10 sites, tables, fire rings, a vault toilet and bear boxes. No potable water (creek only, treat it) and no showers. Steady day-hiker and mountain-bike traffic. It is not in the Eaton Fire closure, which shut the Millard and Idlehour camps through 2027, and a Feb 2026 reviewer used it. The new USFS website has no page for it, though, so call the district to confirm. Fire danger is 'Very High': no wood fires. It is the closest legal tent site to the Elysian Theater. Stay limit is 14 days.

name: Unnamed OSM caravan site on N Pinal Ave (likely RV section beside Rodeo Estates MHP)
access: About 3 mi north of downtown on N Pinal Ave (paved), behind the direction of travel.
priceTent: unknown
cyclistNotes: App baseline entry (OSM way 1348098748). It has no name and sits next to Rodeo Estates Mobile Home Park. I found no evidence that it takes overnight or tent guests. Do not count on it; candidate for removal from the app.
address: N Pinal Ave, Casa Grande, AZ 85122
reservations: unknown

name: Silverado RV Resort (55+)
access: Eloy, about 9–10 mi east-southeast of I-8 exit 174 on paved roads, behind you.
priceTent: No tent sites. Daily RV rate $55 (MAR Communities rate page).
cyclistNotes: Baseline entry. A 55+ active-adult community selling only RV sites and park-model homes. Not a tent option.
reservations: Online or by phone through MAR Communities.

name: High Chaparral RV Park (OSM 'Unnamed campground')
access: About 10 mi south-east of I-8 exit 174 on paved roads (Arizona City side), behind you.
priceTent: Tent rate unknown. RV overnight $37 with the 50% Passport America discount (reported Nov 1, 2026), so roughly double without it.
website: unknown (highchaparralrvpark.com now redirects to an unrelated spam site; do not use it)
cyclistNotes: Baseline 'Unnamed campground' node 13092955624 is this park. Adults-only (18+); kids allowed only Apr–Sep for up to 7 days. Mix of park models and RVs, pool, laundry. The Dyrt tags it 'tent sites' but no review or rule confirms tents. Call first.
address: 7575 W Battaglia Dr, Casa Grande, AZ 85193
reservations: Office check-in; reviewers checked in easily. Late-arrival policy unknown.

name: Motoland MX Park (weekend camping only)
access: South of I-8 between exits 172 and 167. Operator address: 'just east of 6734 Sisler Rd'. Local route unverified; about 2.5 mi on rural roads.
priceTent: Free on practice weekends (Fri–Sun). Race-weekend fee not published.
cyclistNotes: Operator FAQ: camping allowed only Friday–Sunday, and you should message ahead. You would pass on Monday Nov 2, so this is effectively not usable. The site says racing resumes in winter 2027 and posts no practice dates.
address: Just east of 6734 Sisler Rd, Casa Grande, AZ 85193
reservations: Message them before arriving; weekends only.

name: Mammoth Homestead (Hipcamp farm stay)
access: Listing says 'right off I-8'; Montgomery Rd exit 167 is the likely exit. Exact address is given after booking, and the Hipcamp pin is approximate.
priceTent: $32/night base plus Hipcamp fees. One RV/tent site, up to 4 guests; includes main-house bathroom, shower, laundry, water, 30A power and Wi-Fi.
cyclistNotes: The only full-service tent-friendly stop near the line in the Casa Grande area, but only about 11 mi into the day. New listing with no reviews yet. No campfires. Goats and chickens on site.
address: Casa Grande, AZ (exact address after booking)
reservations: Hipcamp booking required. Check-in 2–10 PM, meet the host, strict cancellation policy.

name: Desert Springs 55+ RV Ranch (OSM 'Unnamed campground')
access: I-8 exit 167, then 1.5 mi north on Montgomery Rd (paved).
priceTent: Tent rate unknown. RV about $30/night (2023 report).
cyclistNotes: Baseline 'Unnamed campground' way 761144406 is this park. Campendium: 55+ park, adults only (18+), full-time residents. The Dyrt's 'tent sites' tag is not backed by any review. Don't count on it; call. Feedlot and dairy smells on east winds.
address: 3290 S Montgomery Rd, Casa Grande, AZ 85193
reservations: Reservations accepted (Campendium). Late-arrival policy unknown.

name: Camp Liebre (Hipcamp, off-grid site)
access: About 4 mi east of I-8 exit 151 on paved AZ 84, then about 0.5 mi on unpaved Liebre Rd. Exact address after booking; the pin is approximate. About 0.5 mi off AZ 84 if you ride the AZ 84 alternative.
priceTent: $17/night base plus Hipcamp fees, with no amenities. One site, 6 guests max.
cyclistNotes: Raw pack-in/pack-out desert site next to a big saguaro: no toilet, no water, no campfires. You need to arrive with water. New listing with no reviews.
address: Off Liebre Rd, Maricopa, AZ (exact address after booking)
reservations: Hipcamp. Check-in 2–10 PM, meet the host, strict cancellation.

name: West Pinal County Park (Jim Kortsen / West Pinal Park campground)
access: I-8 exit 151 (AZ 84, mile 27.2), then about 1 mi east on paved AZ 84 to the entrance at 50801 W Hwy 84, then a well-graded gravel loop. On route if you ride AZ 84.
priceTent: $10/night standard site (plus about $2 online booking fee); larger or group sites about $35. Each site has a shade ramada, picnic table and grill. No cash.
phone: 520-866-6920 (Pinal County Parks office, weekdays, per camp host; Campendium lists 520-866-6910)
cyclistNotes: Clean county dry camp with sites far apart; a reviewer notes tent campers hear the I-8 road noise. Porta-potties only: no water, power or showers. Fill up in Stanfield or at Wild West RV Ranch, which also sells dump and fill. Ground fires banned. Feedlot smell on east winds. Volunteer camp host Oct–Easter. Last review Oct 10, 2026: clean, well maintained.
reservations: Online only (Campspot); cash no longer accepted. Booking on your phone on arrival works, including after dark; cell coverage is excellent on all carriers. Reserve ahead in winter, when it often fills. Stay limit 14 days (host) or 7 (Campendium).

name: Supreme's Therapeutic Ranch (Hipcamp)
access: About 3.5 mi north of AZ 84 near I-8 exit 151, on local roads of unknown surface. Exact address after booking; the pin is approximate.
priceTent: $36/night base plus Hipcamp fees. One site, 6 guests max.
cyclistNotes: The description says tent campers get bathroom and shower access, but the amenity list says no toilet, no showers and no potable water. Confirm with the host. Horses and chickens; campfires allowed. New listing with no reviews.
reservations: Hipcamp. Check-in 2–10 PM, meet the host, strict cancellation.

name: Patriot Place (private 5-acre camp, The Dyrt request-to-book)
access: About 3 mi north of the I-8 exit 151 area on S Hidden Valley Rd, which OSM tags as unpaved. Pin from The Dyrt.
priceTent: $10–$20/night (The Dyrt listing)
cyclistNotes: Host-run 5-acre private property in a 55+ neighborhood. The listing offers tent sites, showers and trash, and allows fires and quiet dogs. No reviews; unverified.
address: S Hidden Valley Rd area, Maricopa, AZ 85139 (approx.)
reservations: Request to book on The Dyrt; contact the host ahead.

name: Off Road Camp @ Jurassic Ranch (Hipcamp)
access: North of I-8 exit 151 toward Hidden Valley, about 9–10 mi on local roads, some likely unpaved. Exact address after booking; the pin is approximate.
priceTent: $32/night base plus Hipcamp fees. Includes water hookup and Wi-Fi.
cyclistNotes: Horse ranch 1,000 ft from a BLM off-road trailhead. Four dispersed RV/tent spaces with water and Wi-Fi but no toilet; campfires allowed. Booked once, no reviews. Far off the line; only worth it if everything else is full.
reservations: Hipcamp instant book.

name: Vekol Valley Road BLM dispersed (Sonoran Desert National Monument)
access: I-8 exit 144 (Vekol Rd), then south on graded gravel Vekol Rd with some washboard. The first ~0.3 mi is private land. BLM runs from about 0.4 to 1.2 mi, then a private parcel at about 1.2–1.6 mi, then BLM again from about 1.7 mi on. Climb is minor; the exit is at roughly 1,700 ft.
priceTent: Free (BLM 14-day limit)
cyclistNotes: Most popular free camp on this stretch, legal from an interchange. Campendium lists it as tent-OK; reviews from Nov 2025 and Feb 2026. Ride at least 1–2 mi in to escape truck noise and the trash near the entrance. Border Patrol traffic is frequent, military jets pass over, and it can be crowded in Feb–Mar. BLM warns the southern monument is a smuggling corridor. No water anywhere: carry everything from Casa Grande or Stanfield.
address: Vekol Valley Rd south of I-8 exit 144, Pinal County, AZ
reservations: None; walk in any time.

name: Freeman Rd exit 140 / Lost Horse Tank BLM dispersed (Sonoran Desert NM)
access: I-8 exit 140 (Freeman Rd). Go under the interstate and about 500 ft south on washboard gravel to a T, then right (west) on W Old 84, an old unmaintained paved road. Sites start within about 0.5 mi. BLM also lies north of the exit ('Freeman Rd Camping'). Elevation about 1,800 ft, near the Maricopa Mountains summit of I-8.
priceTent: Free (BLM 14-day limit)
cyclistNotes: Legal and close to an interchange; Campendium rates it 5.0 across 22 reviews (latest Nov 2025: no one else there, no road noise). A reviewer felt 'very comfortable and safe'. Strong Verizon signal from a nearby tower. No services for about 20 mi either way (Gila Bend Pilot is 21 mi on).
address: W Old 84 south of I-8 exit 140 (Freeman Rd), Maricopa County, AZ
reservations: None; walk in any time.

name: BLM Road #8029 dispersed (Sonoran Desert NM, gate off I-8, no ramp)
access: No interchange. A two-track leaves I-8 directly through a gate around milepost 135–136, with a 4-inch drop off the pavement, rocky and sandy. The first several miles are a wilderness cherry-stem with only ~50 ft of non-wilderness each side; open camping at the Big Horn area 3.5–4 mi in.
priceTent: Free (BLM 14-day limit)
cyclistNotes: Gray-area fallback only. Leaving a controlled-access interstate between interchanges is not a designated exit, so use it only if wind stops you between Freeman (38) and Gila Bend (59). Camp beside the two-track: bikes are banned inside the wilderness. The companion road #8011 leaves the EASTBOUND lanes and cannot be reached westbound.
address: I-8 about MP 135, Maricopa County, AZ
reservations: None.

name: BLM Road #8030 dispersed (Sonoran Desert NM, gate off I-8, no ramp)
access: No interchange. An unsigned two-track leaves I-8 through gates around milepost 129–130, with V-shaped wash dips and sandy washes; 4WD country. It passes old corrals and tanks, then enters a ~50 ft-wide wilderness cherry-stem corridor.
priceTent: Free (BLM 14-day limit)
cyclistNotes: Same gray-area access caveat as #8029. Weak cell signal in this dip between the Freeman and Gila Bend towers. Pitch near the road or the corral area, never in the wilderness.
address: I-8 about MP 130, Maricopa County, AZ
reservations: None.

name: BLM Road #8032 dispersed (Sonoran Desert NM, gate off westbound I-8)
access: No interchange. The road leaves the WESTBOUND lanes through a gate around milepost 127. It splits into several spots west of the wilderness boundary and eventually reaches AZ 238. Not suitable for trailers.
priceTent: Free (BLM 14-day limit)
cyclistNotes: Gray-area access as for #8029, but it is on your side of the highway. Sites further from I-8 are quieter. A couple of bars of cell signal. Gila Bend's Pilot is about 9 mi on.
address: I-8 about MP 127, Maricopa County, AZ
reservations: None.

name: BLM land along Old Highway 84, east of Gila Bend exit 119 (incl. the 'BLM road 8035' spot)
access: Legal route: I-8 exit 119 (Butterfield Trail, mile 58.7), north about 0.5 mi past the Pilot, then east on Old Highway 84. It is a compacted dirt track (OSM: grade 2, smoothness 'bad') on the north side of I-8. The first ~1.4 mi of the track is State Trust land, which needs a permit to camp. BLM begins at about 32.9234,-112.6413 and continues about 4 mi to the track's end at the 'BLM road 8035' spot (32.9090,-112.5950), which can also be reached by a gate straight off the I-8 shoulder near MP 124.
priceTent: Free (BLM 14-day limit). Buy water, food and a truck-stop shower at the Pilot or Love's.
cyclistNotes: The closest legal tent spot to Gila Bend, since no town campground takes tents. Fill up at the Pilot (exit 119), ride about 2 mi back east on the dirt track and camp on flat desert. It is within 0.5 mi of I-8, so expect truck noise. Some illegal dumping near town. Cell service is good. Land status comes from the BLM Surface Management Agency map, and The Dyrt describes free scattered sites beyond the gate at the 8035 end.
address: Old Highway 84, east of Butterfield Trail, Gila Bend, AZ 85337
reservations: None.

name: Sonoran Desert RV Park (55+, NO TENTS)
access: On the line: Butterfield Trail, just north of I-8 exit 119.
priceTent: Tents not allowed. Standard RV site $69.95 including tax (Oct–Dec 2026).
cyclistNotes: CORRECTION to the app's current 'best bet' (prior research said tents were confirmed). The park's posted rules say 'We no longer allow tent camping and we do not allow tents on our RV sites'; it is 'an adult 55+ RV park' and asks guests to be inside their RVs by 10 PM. The Campendium and The Dyrt 'tents: yes' tags date from its old Gila Bend KOA days. Do not plan a night here.
address: 800 S Butterfield Trail, Gila Bend, AZ 85337
reservations: Online via CampLife or phone. Winter office 10 AM–6 PM, check-in 1 PM.

name: Augie's Quail Trail RV Park (status unknown)
access: The Dyrt pin is on Butterfield Trail beside Sonoran Desert RV Park.
priceTent: unknown
phone: unknown (The Dyrt shows 928-683-2850, which is Sonoran Desert RV Park's number)
website: unknown (augiesquailtrailrvpark.com and aqtrvaz.com no longer resolve)
cyclistNotes: Only a bare listing on The Dyrt with no reviews; not in OSM. Probably closed or absorbed by the neighbouring park. Treat as nonexistent unless you see it in person.
reservations: unknown

name: Palms Mobile Home & RV Park
access: On the line in Gila Bend, one block off Pima St (I-8 Business), walking distance to Love's, Chevron and Circle K.
priceTent: Tent rate unknown. RV $25–$38/night (2021–2023 reports), half price with Passport America.
cyclistNotes: Mostly a run-down mobile-home community with a few back-in RV spaces. Reviewers report loose dogs, roosters, trains, an office that is often empty (pay through the door slot), and a sign advertising showers that one reviewer could not find. Laundry was reported burned in 2023. The only possible in-town option; ask whether they will take a tent, and expect no.
address: 788 W Williams St, Gila Bend, AZ 85337
reservations: Walk-in; call ahead because the office is often unattended.

name: Painted Rock Petroglyph Campground (BLM)
access: I-8 exit 102 (Painted Rock Dam Rd), then 10.7 mi north on paved road and 0.6 mi west on dirt Rocky Point Rd. Gentle grades. From mile 3 to mile 10 north of I-8 the road crosses private and Tohono O'odham land, so no camping until the campground. More than 10 mi off the line, but it is the only campground in the 36-mile Gila Bend–Sentinel gap.
priceTent: $8 per site per night, paid through Recreation.gov Scan & Pay (no cash or checks) plus a small Recreation.gov fee.
cyclistNotes: 59 big, spread-out sites with tables and fire rings, 2 vault toilets and trash; quiet, dark skies, petroglyphs next door. No water, so carry 6+ L from Gila Bend's Love's (about 25 riding miles: 13.5 on I-8 plus 11.3 in). Recreation.gov warns cell service is unreliable at the campground; set up Scan & Pay before you lose signal. Recreation.gov listing active (updated Mar 2026), every November date marked first-come.
address: 46101 Rocky Point Rd, Gila Bend, AZ 85337
reservations: All sites first-come, first-served, no reservations. Pay on site with Recreation.gov Scan & Pay. Late arrival fine; a reviewer pulled in at 9 PM and found plenty of space.

name: BLM land on Agua Caliente Rd, north of Sentinel exit 87
access: I-8 exit 87 (Sentinel), past Conde's and the Chevron, then north-west on paved Agua Caliente Rd. The first ~1.5 mi is State Trust land; BLM begins about 1.6 mi from I-8 (32.8804,-113.2259) and continues along the road. A BLM strip also lies about 0.4–1 mi south of I-8, behind a private frontage parcel, with no mapped road. Further east and south is the Goldwater Range: keep out.
priceTent: Free (BLM 14-day limit)
cyclistNotes: I found no camper reports for this exact spot. Land status comes from the BLM Surface Management Agency map, and BLM land is open to dispersed camping unless posted. Check for 'no camping' signs and camp out of sight of the road. Water and snacks at Conde's Middle of Nowhere and the Chevron at the exit (hours unverified). The State Trust land closer to I-8 is legal only with an Arizona State Land Department recreation permit.
reservations: None.

name: BLM land at Sentinel exit 87 (dirt track south or frontage road west)
access: I-8 exit 87 (Sentinel). South option: a graded dirt track (OSM grade3, way 1144544092) leaves the exit beside Conde's/Chevron and runs south. BLM land starts about 0.3 mi south of I-8 (32.854,-113.215) and runs at least 2 mi south. The Barry M. Goldwater Range (USAF), which is closed, begins 2-4 mi south: do not cross its signs or fence. North option: a paved frontage road runs west from the exit along the north side of I-8. BLM land starts about 1.3 mi west (32.859,-113.235), about 1.5 riding mi from the exit, and continues toward the Sentinel rest area. The first 1.3 mi north of the exit is State Trust land (ASLD permit needed). A third option, from segment I8-A: BLM land along paved Agua Caliente Rd, about 1.6 mi NW.
priceTent: Free (BLM dispersed, 14-day limit)
phone: 623-580-5500 (BLM Lower Sonoran Field Office / Phoenix District)
reservations: None; first come. Arrive any time.
cyclistNotes: I found no camper reports for these spots. The land status comes from the BLM Surface Management Agency map, checked at 6 points: BLM directly south of the exit and west along the north frontage road, State Trust land NW of the exit, and USAF range about 4 mi south. Camp out of sight of I-8; Border Patrol traffic is normal here. Water and snacks at Conde's Middle of Nowhere and the Chevron at the exit (hours unverified). ADOT's Sentinel rest areas, about 2-3 mi west (corridor mi 94.6 and 95.3), reopened in January 2024 with new restrooms and water but are not legal campsites.

name: Sun Portal Acres (Hipcamp)
access: I-8 exit 73 (Aztec): 0.3 mi on historic US 80/Aztec Rd, then about 1.8 mi south on unpaved N Avenue 69 1/2 E. The host says 2WD access; loose gravel, flat. South of I-8.
priceTent: $25/night base price on Hipcamp, plus fees (one RV/tent site, up to 4 guests)
reservations: Book on Hipcamp. Check-in 2-10 PM; strict no-refund cancellation; 1-night minimum; bookable 12 months out.
cyclistNotes: A new listing with no reviews yet. Private open-desert acreage with a firepit and trash bin, and nothing else. Carry all your water from Sentinel (13 mi back) or Dateland (6 mi ahead). Aztec has no store.

name: Aztec Hills Retreat (Hipcamp)
access: I-8 exit 73 (Aztec): historic US 80/Aztec Rd, then south on unpaved N Avenue 69 1/2 E, about 2.5 mi in all. Open 80-acre parcel south of I-8; you camp where you park.
priceTent: $15/night base price on Hipcamp, plus fees (40 dispersed RV/tent sites)
reservations: Book on Hipcamp.
cyclistNotes: It is the cheapest paid tent spot on this segment. One Hipcamp review (100%). No toilet, water or shade, but campfires are allowed. Sun Portal Acres is about 0.5 mi away if this one is full. Water: Dateland Travel Center, 6 mi ahead.

name: Oasis RV Park at Aztec Hills
access: On the old US 80 frontage road between exits 73 and 67, 0.5 mi south via Ave 66E/Morton Rd (1401 S Ave 66E). From Dateland exit 67, ride 1.6 mi back east on paved Old Highway 80 (about 2.2 mi total). From Aztec exit 73 the frontage road runs about 4 mi west to it; OSM shows part of it unpaved.
priceTent: Tent rate not published. RV full hookup was $35 (Mar 2025) and $40 (Mar 2026).
reservations: Call ahead. A 2025 reviewer got a call back within minutes for a one-night site. Also a Harvest Hosts host (self-contained RVs only).
cyclistNotes: 35-site, 10-acre park with a pool, laundry, showers and a rec hall. Quiet and dark, though trains are audible; reviewed Mar and Apr 2026. No listing (Campendium, The Dyrt, RoverPass) shows tent sites, and The Dyrt marks it RV-only. Ask by phone. Dateland RV Park, 3 mi on, takes tents.

name: Dateland RV Park
access: I-8 exit 67 (Dateland / Ave 64E): south of the interchange, 1/8 mi on the frontage road. Register at the Dateland Date Gardens gift shop / travel center across the road.
priceTent: Not published. Last reported nightly rate $26 (May 2023); The Dyrt lists 'from $25'. Ask for a tent rate.
reservations: Walk-in. Register at the gift shop; dateland.com lists 8 AM-9 PM daily for the travel center. After-hours arrival is unverified, so call before 9 PM.
cyclistNotes: Campendium and The Dyrt list tent camping. A cyclist tented here in Sept 2022 under trees, noting 'very sandy roads' and a long walk to the showers. Another rider called the 'tent spaces' RV pull-throughs. Private shower rooms (sink, toilet, shower), dated laundry. I-8 on one side, Union Pacific trains about every 30 min on the other. An April 2026 review says the water tastes 'thick'. The travel center has a Chevron, Pizza Hut and date shakes, the only food between Sentinel and Tacna.

name: BLM dispersed on S Avenue 52 1/2 E (Mohawk, I-8 exit 54)
access: I-8 exit 54. North side: about 0.3 mi west on Old Highway 80 / County 2nd St N, then north on S Avenue 52 1/2 E. BLM land begins at Old Hwy 80 and lines both sides of the road for 1.5+ mi. iOverlander says the road is washboard for the first 1/2 mi and some sites need you to cross a gravel berm. Between Dateland and here the old frontage road is abandoned (OSM access=no), so ride I-8 from exit 67 to exit 54 (about 13 mi).
address: S Avenue 52 1/2 E, Yuma County, AZ (north of I-8 exit 54)
priceTent: Free (BLM dispersed, 14-day limit)
reservations: None.
cyclistNotes: This is the only free camp found between Dateland (mi 112) and Wellton (mi 150). An iOverlander report calls it 'dozens of free, level BLM sites, well dispersed'. I could not open the full listing to date it. The federal land map shows BLM at every point I checked along the road (8 points). Fill water at the Mohawk Rest Area (I-8 MP 56, corridor mi 124.6-125.1), 1 mi before the exit: OSM tags a public drinking-water fountain, restrooms and vending machines. Nearest food is Tacna, 13 mi west.

name: Arizona State Trust land south of Tacna (ASLD recreation permit)
access: I-8 exit 42 (Tacna): south past the Pilot/Shell on Main St/Ave 40E toward Copper Mountain RV Park. The federal land map shows State Trust land around the park on the north, east and south (checked at 7 points). Use an existing two-track and keep clear of the RV park, fenced or leased parcels and anything posted.
address: South of I-8 exit 42, Tacna, AZ 85352
priceTent: Legal only with an Arizona State Land Department individual recreational permit: $15 for 12 months, bought online in advance. Camping is capped at 14 days per year.
reservations: No reservations. Buy the permit online before you lose signal and carry proof (a screenshot works).
cyclistNotes: This is a legal fallback only; I found no camper reports for these parcels. It splits the 38-mi Dateland-Wellton gap if the Mohawk BLM site does not work out. All Tacna services are at the exit. In 2013 a cyclist was allowed to tent free behind the Chaparral Motel in Tacna; that is not current, but asking a business is a last resort.

name: Copper Mountain RV Park (55+; tents only for active-duty military)
access: I-8 exit 42 (Tacna): south on Main St/Ave 40E, then County 9 1/2 St, about 1.3 mi paved.
priceTent: Not available to civilians. The park allows tents only for active-duty personnel ('Tents for Troops', max 4 nights). RV nightly was $55 (Jul 2023).
reservations: Seasonal Oct 1-Apr 15; reservations through the park.
cyclistNotes: Do not plan on a tent here. It is a 55+ park for self-contained RVs, and Camping Roadtrip and AllStays both say no tents. The State Trust land around it is the legal fallback (see previous entry). Tacna has a Pilot with Subway, a Shell, a Chevron Food Mart, Gonzo's market and Basque Etche restaurant.

name: Coach Stop RV Park (adults only)
access: In Wellton, just north of Los Angeles Ave on Wellton Mohawk Dr.
address: 30333 E Wellton Mohawk Dr, Wellton, AZ 85356
priceTent: Tent rate not published. Dry site $30/day, $42/day with electricity (rates effective Oct 2025).
reservations: Call the office or use the site's reservation form.
cyclistNotes: The rate page says 'Coach Stop RV Park is an Adults Only Park' (not stated as 55+). Its $30 dry-site rate is the cheapest showers-and-toilets option in Wellton if they accept a tent, which no source confirms. 190 sites, laundry, game room.

name: Arrowhead RV Park (55+)
access: In Wellton, from Los Angeles Ave (old US 80, the line) north 0.3 mi on Wellton Mohawk Dr.
priceTent: No tent sites: 55+ RV-only park. RV nightly $42 + tax with electric (2026-27 season).
reservations: Five pull-throughs, first come first served. Office Mon-Sat 8:30-noon and 1-4:30.
cyclistNotes: 'An active 55+ community' with 154 full-hookup sites. No tent option is listed anywhere.

name: Desert Sands RV Park
access: On Los Angeles Ave (old US 80), Wellton, directly on the line.
priceTent: unknown
reservations: unknown
cyclistNotes: The town directory gives this park the same phone number and description ('10 RV spaces, full hook-ups, cable TV, propane and coffee shop') as Lazy Cactus RV Park, so it may be the same operator or a directory mix-up. It has no reviews anywhere. Call the number and ask about both.

name: Sun Country RV Park (55+)
access: Just south of Los Angeles Ave on Fresno St, Wellton.
priceTent: No tent sites: 55+ RV-only park. Full-hookup RV sites from $30/night plus electric.
reservations: Book online or call; open all year.
cyclistNotes: Campendium tags it 55+ and a guest review on its own site calls it a 'small quiet 55 and over RV park'. The rules say one RV per site and no tent option is listed.

name: Desert Rose RV Park
access: Arizona Ave, Wellton, a block south of the line.
priceTent: No tents: AAA lists it as 'No tent. RVs only.'
reservations: unknown
cyclistNotes: It has 28 full-hookup spaces (town directory) and no reviews anywhere. AAA and AllStays both list it as RV-only.

name: Lazy Cactus RV Park
access: 10319 Maybelle St, beside the Wellton post office and town hall, one block off Los Angeles Ave.
priceTent: From $25/night (The Dyrt, owner-managed listing, updated June 2025)
reservations: Call; the park takes reservations.
cyclistNotes: A 10-unit park with a coffee shop. Its owner-claimed Dyrt listing offers RV and tent stays from $25. Neither The Dyrt nor Campendium lists showers or restrooms, so confirm before you count on them. Del Sol supermarket, Circle K, Family Dollar, Dollar General and Geronimo's are all within 0.5 mi. The only review is from 2019.

name: Lazy Coyote RV Village (55+)
access: Arizona Ave, one block south of Los Angeles Ave, Wellton.
priceTent: No tent sites: 55+ RV-only park.
reservations: Daily, weekly, monthly and annual RV rates; call.
cyclistNotes: The park's own site calls it 'a pet friendly, 55+ community with 90 full hookups'. Public dump station.

name: Pioneer RV Park (55+)
access: South of I-8 at exit 30: William St, then east on County 11th St.
priceTent: No tent sites: 55+ RV-only park.
reservations: Call.
cyclistNotes: Campendium tags it 55+ with full-time residents. 327 spaces, pool, spa, showers and laundry, per the town directory.

name: Tier Drop RV Park
access: From Wellton's main street (Los Angeles Ave/William St) go south on William St across I-8 at exit 30, then 0.7 mi west on County 11th St (the south frontage road). Paved.
priceTent: Tent rate not published. A tent camper paid $20 (Jan 2020). The operator lists RV daily at $40 (2026); a Campendium report says $37 (Feb 2026).
reservations: Book through the park website or by phone. The posted (summer) office hours are Mon-Fri 8-4. A 2023 guest arrived at 8:30 PM and paid cash in an envelope at the office. The website was returning errors on Nov 2, 2026, so phone ahead.
cyclistNotes: This is the most reliable tent spot between Dateland and Yuma. It advertises 'No Age Restrictions', which is rare here. Campendium lists 'Tent camping: Yes'. A repeat tent guest pitched 'in a more remote section, quiet and clean' (2020), and The Dyrt lists tents. AAA's directory says 'No tent. RVs only', so confirm by phone. Amenities: heated pool and spa, two laundries, restrooms and showers, clubhouse. Chevron and Jack in the Box are at exit 30; Del Sol supermarket is 1.5 mi.

name: Welton Canal dispersed area (BLM / State Trust patchwork)
access: From Wellton south on William St / S Avenue 29 E across I-8 (about 1.8 mi), then E County 13th St to the Wellton-Mohawk canal, about 2.7 mi from the line. Land is a checkerboard on the federal map: BLM (32.635,-114.140 and 32.637,-114.135), State Trust (32.640,-114.140) and Bureau of Reclamation canal land. Camp on the BLM piece, or carry an ASLD permit to be legal on the State Trust piece.
address: Near S Avenue 29 E and E County 13th St, Wellton, AZ 85356
priceTent: Free on the BLM parcel. The State Trust parcel needs the $15/yr ASLD recreational permit.
reservations: None.
cyclistNotes: The Dyrt lists tents. A Jan 2026 review: 'Good group of people using the area. The trains do move through the valley at night. Could not hear the highway. Level and easy entry.' A Dec 2023 reviewer said it is State Trust land needing a permit but had never seen anyone check. Stock up in Wellton first.

name: Old Desert Bull RV Park (55+)
access: From I-8 exit 30, south about 2.2 mi on S Avenue 29 E, then to 13550 Ave 28 E.
priceTent: No tent sites (10 full-hookup RV sites, 55+).
reservations: Call.
cyclistNotes: Campendium tags it 55+ and The Dyrt marks it RV-only. Listed so the app does not suggest it.

name: Brewery on an Organic Date Farm (Naked Date Farms / High Tanks Brewing, Hipcamp)
access: From Wellton exit 30: S Ave 29E, Colorado Ave, Canal Ave, E County 12th St, then E City 12 Rd west about 2.5 mi, S Avenue 25 E south about 1.5 mi, and Gila Ranch Rd. About 6.5 mi; the last leg is a well-kept dirt road ('a Corolla handles it'). Leaving west, rejoin I-8 at Dome Valley exit 21 (corridor mi 161.1) via Ave 25E north and paved old Hwy 80 west, about 8.3 mi. That loop adds only about 6 mi over riding I-8 straight through.
address: Gila Ranch Rd off S Avenue 25 E, Wellton, AZ 85356 (exact spot on booking)
priceTent: $40/night base price on Hipcamp, plus fees (dry 'RV/Tent' sites under the palms; max 7 nights)
reservations: Book on Hipcamp or request through The Dyrt. The Dyrt gives the camping season as Nov 1-Apr 30; the brewery and restaurant are open Nov-Apr, Thu-Sun 11-5.
cyclistNotes: This is the best-reviewed camp on the segment: 149 Hipcamp reviews, 97% recommend, a 2024 'Best in Arizona' finalist. Sites are named 'RV/Tent Site 1-6 - Dry Camping', and car, rooftop-tent and van campers reviewed it through April 2026. A reviewer reports a 'decent restroom with showers'. You camp in shade among Medjool date palms, with date beer and food Thu-Sun and live music some weekends. One complaint is a generator. Wi-Fi at the brewery only.

name: Camp'n Dirty (Hipcamp)
access: Same farm roads as the date farm, about 1 mi further west via Gila Ranch Rd and S Avenue 24 E (sand and rock). About 7.5 mi from Wellton exit 30, or about 9.3 mi from Dome Valley exit 21 via old Hwy 80 and Ave 25E.
priceTent: $35/night base price on Hipcamp, plus fees (5 private RV/tent sites)
reservations: Book on Hipcamp. Late arrival works: a Feb 2025 guest arrived 7-8 PM and the host flagged them in. It is very dark after sunset.
cyclistNotes: 40-acre off-grid desert property beside the Goldwater Range. Tent guests reviewed it in Nov 2025 and Jun 2024 (93% recommend, latest March 2026). No toilet or water. Eat and fill bottles at the date farm brewery, 1 mi east, on Thu-Sun.

name: Liguerta (Ligurta) Station RV Park
access: I-8 exit 21 (Dome Valley / Ligurta), north side on paved E Highway 80 (old US 80).
priceTent: unknown
reservations: unknown
cyclistNotes: It exists in OSM and in an unclaimed RoverPass listing (updated Jul 2025) that claims showers, laundry, a pool and a dump station, rated 2.0 from 4 reviews. It is not on Campendium, The Dyrt or Hipcamp. Phone before relying on it. The I-8 'Ligurta parking areas' at this exit are truck parking, not legal campsites.

name: BLM land at Dome Valley / Ligurta exit 21
access: I-8 exit 21: about 0.5 mi west on paved E Highway 80 (old US 80) on the south side. The federal map shows BLM on both sides of the road west of the exit (32.662-32.670 N, 114.300-114.315 W), and an OSM track enters it at 32.6672,-114.3044. North of the exit, BLM also starts about 0.5 mi up Ave 20E / Dome Valley Rd.
address: E Highway 80 west of I-8 exit 21, Yuma County, AZ
priceTent: Free (BLM dispersed, 14-day limit)
reservations: None.
cyclistNotes: I found no camper reports here; legality comes from the federal land-status map only. West of this exit I-8 climbs Telegraph Pass with no exit for about 7 mi. The unpaved alternative is the 'Route of Butterfield Stage' county road (OSM, surface unknown), about 11 mi NW to US 95 at the Yuma VFW BLM camp. There is no water between Wellton and the Fortuna Foothills, about 16 mi.

name: Fortuna de Oro RV Resort (Cal-Am, 55+)
access: I-8 exit 14 (Foothills Blvd), north frontage road east.

Rule 26 also bans camping within 1 mile outside the LTVA boundary. Use the free Pilot Knob 14-Day Area or Sidewinder Rd BLM instead.

A Jan 2026 report says the entrance is blocked by a dirt berm and a bush, so walk the bike around on the side track. It turns to mud after rain.

A '4x4 recommended' sign further in; ground is packed desert pavement.
priceTent: Free (14-day limit)

The mine waters the main road for dust, and it can be very windy when Yuma is calm. Gold Rock Ranch (showers) is about 4 mi further north. It costs about 10.5 mi round trip off the route, so use it only if the Pilot Knob areas will not do.
