website: unknown (goldrockranch.us no longer resolves as of Nov 2026)
reservations: unknown
cyclistNotes: AAA lists it as RVs only with no tents; MapQuest and The Dyrt list tent sites. The newest reviews are from 2022 and the website is dead, so call before committing to a 20-mile round trip. Mainly useful as a place to shower and do laundry.

name: Buttercup Campground (Imperial Sand Dunes RA)
address: Luis A. Aguilar Rd / Grays Well Rd at I-8 exit 156, Winterhaven, CA
access: Paved and flat: leave I-8 at exit 156 (Grays Well Rd) and go east past the Buttercup Ranger Station. Off the pavement it is soft sand.
priceTent: Free for a cyclist going by the rule's wording: the ISDRA permit ($55 weekly online, $70 on site, $185 season, Oct 1 to Apr 15) applies to 'primary street legal vehicles used for transportation to the recreation site'. Confirm with the ranger.
phone: Buttercup Ranger Station (760) 572-2220 (2020 brochure); BLM El Centro (760) 337-4400
reservations: First come, first served, 14-day limit. The ranger station is staffed Fri–Sun in season.
cyclistNotes: An OHV staging and camping area with vault toilets and dumpsters, and the land is BLM. Engines and generators run on weekends (Nov 7–8); weekdays are quiet. BLM rules allow small tent stakes. Caltrans lists the Sand Hills Rest Area on I-8, about 0.3 mi west, with drinking water and toilets. The border fence is close and Border Patrol is active. BLM's only current ISDRA closure (Cement Flats, from Sept 8, 2026) is in the north dunes on Hwy 78, not here.
sources: freecampsites.net listing #49858 (Imperial Sand Dunes RA - Buttercup)

name: Midway Campground (Imperial Sand Dunes RA)
address: Off Grays Well Rd, south of I-8 between exits 156 and 151
access: Exit 156, then about 2.4 mi southwest on Grays Well Rd (paved BLM road, flat), then a short gravel spur.
priceTent: Free for a cyclist (the ISDRA permit is per street-legal primary vehicle); confirm at Buttercup Ranger Station.
reservations: First come; 14-day limit.
cyclistNotes: Campendium marks tent camping 'Yes'. A camping strip parallel to I-8 facing the dunes, the border fence and Mexico, with vault toilets and dumpsters. Traffic noise is moderate.

name: Grays Well / Plank Road camping area (Imperial Sand Dunes RA)
address: End of Grays Well Rd at the Old Plank Road historic site
access: Exit 156, then about 3.4 mi on paved Grays Well Rd, flat. The pavement ends here. Going west to Gordons Well Rd / Evan Hewes means about 1.5 mi of compacted and sandy BLM track; otherwise ride back to exit 156.
priceTent: Free for a cyclist (permit is per street-legal primary vehicle); confirm with BLM.
reservations: First come; 14-day limit.
cyclistNotes: Paved access road, toilets, and the Old Plank Road display. The land is BLM. A dead end for road bikes.

name: Dune Buggy Flats (Imperial Sand Dunes RA)
address: Coachella Canal Rd / BLM 468 near I-8 exit 151 (Gordons Well)
access: From exit 151 (Gordons Well Rd), about 1.2 mi east on compacted and sandy BLM tracks (BLM 386/468), flat. Alternatively about 4.3 mi from exit 156 on mostly paved Grays Well Rd.
priceTent: Free for a cyclist (ISDRA permit is per street-legal primary vehicle).
reservations: First come; 14-day limit.
cyclistNotes: Gravel camping area with vault toilets and dumpsters (BLM brochure); the land is BLM. It is the last ISDRA camp before the route leaves I-8. Gordon's Well RV Park and its weekend diner are 1.5 mi west.

name: Gordon's Well RV Park & Storage
access: On the route: paved East Evan Hewes Hwy just west of I-8 exit 151, flat.
priceTent: Not published. The park has 99 full-hookup RV sites, mostly seasonal dune-trip rentals.
reservations: Reservations taken by phone or email (office@gordonswellrvparkandstorage.com). Season Oct 1 to May 31.
cyclistNotes: The only RV park in the dunes, under new owners since 2020 and remodeled, with men's and women's restrooms with showers and a coin laundry. Duner's Diner restaurant and bar next door is open weekends only. No tent policy is published, so call. Even if they refuse a tent, ask to buy a shower and water: after this it is about 26 mi with no services to Holtville.

name: Tamarisk LTVA (BLM)
address: Hwy 98, 2.7 mi west of I-8 exit 143, then south on a dirt road
access: From Evan Hewes at exit 143, about 2.7 mi west on paved Hwy 98, then a dirt road south. Flat.
priceTent: Tents not permitted. Self-contained only: $40 per 14 days, $80 for 4 weeks, $180 per season.
reservations: Permit required Sept 15 to Apr 15, for self-contained units only.
cyclistNotes: Rule 17a makes it self-contained units only, and rule 26 bans camping within 1 mile outside its boundary. A Nov 2024 reviewer describes a big flat dirt lot about 200 yd from a busy highway, with a trash bin but no toilets and no water. Not a tent option.

name: East Mesa BLM dispersed (along East Evan Hewes Hwy)
address: BLM desert on both sides of East Evan Hewes Hwy, about miles 218.5–222.5
access: Paved Evan Hewes Hwy, flat. Turn off onto any existing dirt route and camp within about 300 ft of it, out of sight of the road. Soft sugar sand lies off the packed tracks.
priceTent: Free (BLM 14-day limit)
reservations: None.
cyclistNotes: This is a map-verified fallback, not a reviewed site: the BLM land layer shows BLM on both sides of the road from about mile 216 to 224. To stay legal, keep more than 1 mile outside the Tamarisk LTVA (Hwy 98 side, about miles 214–217.5) and the Hot Spring LTVA (about miles 223.5–226.5), where camping is banned. Near miles 209–217 the strip south of the road is Bureau of Reclamation canal land; do not camp there.

name: Hot Spring LTVA, North and South (BLM, Holtville Hot Springs)
address: East Evan Hewes Hwy at the Holtville Hot Spring, about 6 mi east of Holtville
access: On the route: paved Evan Hewes Hwy, flat. Inside the LTVA the ground is soft sand.
priceTent: Tents not permitted. Self-contained units: $40 per 14 days (Sept 15 to Apr 15). Day use of the hot spring is free, 5 am to midnight.
reservations: Permit from the camp host or recreation.gov, for self-contained units only.
cyclistNotes: This corrects the app's 'tents OK' record. BLM rule 17a makes Hot Spring LTVA self-contained only (a BLM ranger told a 2016 camper the same), and rule 26 bans camping within 1 mile outside the boundary; a 2025 camper got a $110 ticket just south of the springs. The outdoor rinse shower and pools may be affected: a single Apr 2026 Campendium report says a pipeline leak since mid-March 2026 had eroded the entrance and cut pressure, and that BLM planned to shut the spring. No BLM notice was found. Camp at the free BLM area 2 mi south and come back to soak if it is running. No potable water.

name: BLM 14-day area south of Holtville Hot Springs (free)
address: Holdridge Rd, about 2 mi south of I-8 at the Holtville Hot Spring
access: At the hot spring turn south on Holdridge Rd: about 0.3 mi paved, then compacted gravel with sandy spots, about 1.8 mi in all, flat. Camp past the big power lines and the BLM '14 day' signs, about 2 mi south of I-8. Sugar sand lies off the packed tracks.
priceTent: Free (14 days in any 28)
reservations: None.
cyclistNotes: A legal free BLM area with signs, confirmed in reviews from 2014 to 2025; the land is verified BLM. Reviewers say it is quiet with good AT&T and T-Mobile coverage. A 2021 report mentions theft and a brush fire. Carry water: the nearest is Holtville, about 7 mi. The hot spring rinse shower is 1.8 mi back if it is running.

name: Los Cerritos Ranch (Hipcamp)
address: Holtville, CA (exact address given after booking)
access: Paved roads, then a 2WD gravel pad. The host says it is about 1 minute out of Holtville near the Alamo River; flat.
priceTent: $35/night base (about $41.22 with Hipcamp fees) for one RV or tent site, 2 guests max, 1 vehicle.
reservations: Book on Hipcamp, up to 12 months ahead, 1-night minimum, flexible cancellation. Check-in after 7 AM and you meet the host on arrival, so message ahead if you will arrive in the evening.
cyclistNotes: Star Host Gerardo, 97% recommend (19 ratings), with stays from Dec 2025 to May 2026, including a tent camper in May 2026. Quiet farm with animals and mesquite shade. The listing says no toilets, showers or potable water, but a Jan 2025 guest found porta-potties. Fill water in Holtville. There is only one site, so book as soon as the day is set.

name: NAF El Centro RV park (military only)
address: Naval Air Facility El Centro, near Seeley, CA
access: On the base, behind a security gate.
priceTent: unknown
reservations: Military/DoD ID holders only.
cyclistNotes: This is the baseline's OSM 'Unnamed campground' at 32.8167,-115.6800 (mile 250.9): the community-recreation RV park on Naval Air Facility El Centro. RV LIFE flags it 'Military Only'. Not open to Nick unless he holds military or DoD ID.

name: Superstition Mountain OHV area, 'The Dip' / Wheeler Rd (BLM, free)
address: Off Huff Rd about 7.5 mi north of Evan Hewes Hwy, Seeley, CA
access: North on Huff Rd from Evan Hewes about 7.5 mi (surface not verified), flat. The Wheeler Rd OHV staging is about 2.5 mi further west on dirt.
priceTent: Free (14-day limit)
reservations: None.
cyclistNotes: A large BLM OHV open area with free dispersed camping. It is very busy and dusty on weekends from Oct to Apr and quiet on weekdays. Worth it only as a detour; Plaster City OHV, 6 mi further on and right beside the route, is easier.
sources: freecampsites.net listing #34243 (Superstition Mtn - The Dip Area)
freecampsites.net listing #50725 (Superstition Mt - Wheeler Rd OHV)

name: Plaster City OHV Area staging (BLM, free)
address: North side of West Evan Hewes Hwy (CR S80), about 2 mi east of the Plaster City plant
access: Pull off paved S80 onto the dirt staging area north of the road (railroad tracks run alongside). Flat.
priceTent: Free (14-day limit)
reservations: None.
cyclistNotes: The BLM Plaster City OHV open area (OSM relation 15006797) borders the route from about mile 256.5 to 267, and the land is verified BLM on both sides here. OHV groups make it busy on weekends, and trains pass. No water: the last is Seeley (mile 251.7) and the next is Ocotillo (mile 270–273).

name: Plaster City East OHV (BLM, free)
address: North of Evan Hewes Hwy near Plaster City
access: About 1.7 mi north of S80 on dirt OHV routes near the USG plant; sand is possible.
priceTent: Free (14-day limit)
reservations: None.
cyclistNotes: A second staging point in the same BLM open area, farther from the road and trains. The land is verified BLM. There are no recent reviews.

name: Plaster City West / Painted Gorge Rd (BLM, free)
address: West Evan Hewes Hwy (CR S80) at Painted Gorge Rd (BLM 236), about 6.5 mi east of Ocotillo
access: At the Painted Gorge Rd junction with S80: camp on BLM land just off the pavement, or go up compacted Painted Gorge Rd toward the Coyote Mountains. The wilderness boundary is far up the road, and bikes are not allowed inside it. Flat.
priceTent: Free (14-day limit)
reservations: None.
cyclistNotes: The closest documented free camping to Ocotillo. The land is verified BLM on both sides of S80 here. Ocotillo's Chevron and market are 4–6 mi on.

name: Ocotillo Trailer Park & Motel
access: Paved town streets, flat, next to the Ocotillo community center.
priceTent: unknown
reservations: unknown (the website is an old Flash site with no content)
cyclistNotes: The only private lodging business in Ocotillo (motel plus trailer park). It is unknown whether it rents overnight RV or tent spaces; the motel rooms count as a hotel, which you don't want. Red Feather Market & Cafe and the post office are next door.

name: BLM dispersed land north of Ocotillo (Shell Canyon Rd / S2)
address: BLM desert north of Ocotillo via dirt BLM route 229
access: Paved. From Ocotillo (I-8 exit 89, Imperial Hwy/S2) ride north on Shell Canyon Rd. Public BLM land starts about 1.6-1.8 mi north of I-8, and the road stays paved to about 3.2 mi before turning to dirt. Alternative: BLM land along S2 2-4 mi northwest of town. Flat desert floor.
priceTent: Free (BLM dispersed; 14 days in any 28-day period; campfire permit required)
reservations: None. First come, no check-in, arrive any hour.
cyclistNotes: Free legal fallback at the foot of the In-Ko-Pah grade. Sleeping here lets you start the 2,700-ft climb fresh in the morning instead of fighting afternoon wind. Pitch within 300 ft of the road, or within 50 ft once you are inside the Ocotillo ACEC, which begins about 2.5 mi north. Stay off wind-farm service roads and out of the way of quarry trucks. Do NOT camp south of I-8 along SR-98: the Yuha Basin ACEC allows camping only at designated sites. There is no water, so fill up at the Ocotillo Chevron/Food Mart at exit 89. Expect heavy Border Patrol traffic and November lows in the 40s.

name: BLM dispersed south of Ocotillo (BLM route 321 off Hwy 98)
address: BLM desert south of I-8 at Ocotillo via compacted BLM route 321
access: From the I-8/S2 interchange go south on S2 / Hwy 98 about 0.5 mi, then onto compacted dirt BLM route 321, about 1 mi south. BLM land starts about 0.6 mi south of town. Flat.
priceTent: Free (14-day limit)
reservations: None.
cyclistNotes: Map-verified only (BLM land at 32.714–32.720N), with no user reports. It is near the border, so expect Border Patrol traffic and lights.

name: Jacumba Mountains Wilderness edge, Davies Valley access (BLM, free)
address: South of Ocotillo via S2/Hwy 98 and a BLM dirt road to the wilderness boundary
access: South from Ocotillo on S2 to Hwy 98, east 0.7 mi to the BLM sign, then a bumpy, sandy dirt road to the wilderness boundary. Bikes are prohibited inside the wilderness, so camp outside the boundary.
priceTent: Free (14-day limit)
reservations: None.
cyclistNotes: Remote and next to the border; a 2018 camper left after Border Patrol searchlights. The BLM route 321 spot above is closer and easier.

name: Smuggler's Gulch Dispersed (BLM, I-8 exit 80 Mountain Springs Rd)
access: Halfway up the grade. Leave westbound I-8 at exit 80 (Mountain Springs Rd) onto the old concrete Hwy 80 remnant and dirt spurs. One rough patch needs vehicle clearance, so walk the bike there.
priceTent: Free (BLM dispersed)
reservations: None. First come, any hour.
cyclistNotes: Bail-out spot for when the wind beats you on the In-Ko-Pah climb. The BLM land-status layer puts it on BLM land inside the Ocotillo ACEC, so camp within 50 ft of the route. It is a recreational shooting area: broken glass, rusty metal and shell casings everywhere, so watch your tires. Freeway noise. No water, so carry it from Ocotillo.

name: The Desert View Tower (Hipcamp)
address: Desert View Tower, In-Ko-Pah Park Rd, Jacumba area (exact details on booking)
access: Take I-8 exit 77 (In-Ko-Pah Park Rd) and ride about 1 mi north on paved In-Ko-Pah Park Rd to the tower. The sites are walk-in among the boulders with no vehicle access, so push the bike the last stretch.
priceTent: $45/night per site (Hipcamp all-in price; tent-only; up to 14 people)
reservations: Hipcamp request-to-book (not instant). Arrival is strictly before dark: before 4 pm in winter months. The host will not accept after-dark arrivals.
cyclistNotes: Top of the In-Ko-Pah grade at about 3,000 ft, camping among the boulders beside the historic 1920s tower. Flush toilets and water at the sites, no showers. The host warns the winds can be 'ferocious' and asks you to check the Boulder Park, CA forecast. Book a day ahead and plan to arrive by 4 pm; if the grade runs late, use Smuggler's Gulch or Elliot Mine instead. Active listing with 98% of 164 reviews positive; latest reviews April 2026.

name: In-Ko-Pah Spirit Retreat (Hipcamp)
access: From In-Ko-Pah Park Rd / Old Hwy 80 near I-8 exit 77, 1.6 mi of bumpy, rutted dirt road. The host says it turns to clay mud when wet, so avoid it after rain. Sites 2-3 are a 0.13-mi pack-in on a rough trail.
priceTent: $40/night (Hipcamp; 4 RV/tent sites plus 1 container cabin)
reservations: Hipcamp request-to-book (not instant). Check in before 5 pm in winter months, 7 pm in summer.
cyclistNotes: Off-grid 10-acre retreat running on solar, wind and well water. The host lists flush toilets, showers and a kitchen at the Home Base site. No pets. Rattlesnake and cholla country. No trash service, so pack everything out. Latest reviews September 2026.

name: Elliot Mine area BLM dispersed (Old Hwy 80 spur south of I-8 exit 77)
access: The dirt entrance is off the old Hwy 80 spur just south of I-8 exit 77 (32.6398, -116.1070). The camp spurs beyond are very rough and rocky (4WD, high clearance), so expect to push the bike.
priceTent: Free (BLM dispersed)
reservations: None. First come, any hour.
cyclistNotes: The BLM land-status layer confirms BLM land at the entrance and at the Dyrt 'Elliot Mine' point (32.6254, -116.0819). The app's OSM pin at 32.6258, -116.0963 falls on private/undetermined land, so do not camp there. The site sits beside the border wall with constant Border Patrol trucks and searchlights. No facilities and no water: fill up at Ocotillo or plan on Jacumba. The adjacent Jacumba Wilderness is closed to bikes.

name: DeAnza Springs Resort
address: 1951 Carrizo Gorge Rd, Jacumba Hot Springs, CA 91934
access: From Old Hwy 80 in Jacumba, take Carrizo Gorge Rd north. The first 1.1 mi is paved and passes the I-8 exit 73 Shell/Chevron. Then about 1.75 mi of graded dirt to the resort; dusty but fine on a touring bike when dry.
priceTent: Tent/dry sites from about $39/night on Hipcamp (all-in). Direct booking on Campspot. Campendium users report $73-76 for RV sites.
reservations: Book via Campspot (campspot.com/book/deanzaspringsresort) or Hipcamp (instant book), or call. One Hipcamp reviewer says check-in must be before 4 pm; call if you will be late.
cyclistNotes: Best amenities on this stretch: showers, two pools (one indoor and heated), hot tub, café/bar, Wi-Fi and laundry. It is still a clothing-optional resort: its own 2026 FAQ says so, and Hipcamp campers report the pool and jacuzzi are nude-only. Otherwise family-friendly and pet-friendly. The Goat Canyon Trestle trail starts here. Elevation about 2,800 ft, so expect cold November nights. Recent reviews (Feb and Jul 2026) are positive.

name: BS Ranch, Home of the Big Spots (Hipcamp, Jewel Valley)
access: Jewel Valley, south of Old Hwy 80 between Jacumba and Boulevard. About 3.5 mi via Jewel Valley Rd, partly unpaved/compacted. Exact address on booking; the listing coordinates are approximate.
priceTent: $50/night (Hipcamp); 25 dispersed RV/tent spots on 78 acres
reservations: Hipcamp instant book
cyclistNotes: Backup only: just 5 reviews, the latest from September 2025. No campfires; pets OK.

name: Sagewinds Farm High Desert Camp (Hipcamp)
access: Just off Old Hwy 80 about 3.5 mi west of Jacumba toward Boulevard. Exact address on booking (listing coordinates are approximate); the final approach is probably dirt.
priceTent: $40.50/night (Hipcamp all-in)
reservations: Hipcamp instant book
cyclistNotes: Certified-organic white-sage farm at 3,500-3,800 ft with boulders and caves. Two flush toilets and potable water, no showers, no campfires. 98% of 300-plus reviews recommend it; latest reviews September 2026. Expect cold nights.

name: Lark Canyon Campground (BLM, McCain Valley; lower & upper loops)
access: From Old Hwy 80 about 2 mi east of Boulevard, go north on McCain Valley Rd: 2.4 mi paved, then graded gravel. The lower loop is about 4 mi in; the upper loop (32.7278, -116.2736) is about 5.5 mi.
priceTent: $6/site/night BLM fee (fee tube reported missing at times); 15 sites plus group sites
reservations: First come, no reservations
cyclistNotes: Designated BLM campground in the McCain Valley RCA. BLM's 2020 map lists upper and lower Lark Canyon with non-potable water, fire rings, trash and vault toilets. It is an OHV motorcycle area with wind turbines nearby and a migrant route with Border Patrol traffic. Carry all drinking water from Boulevard (Mountain Top Market, mile 300). Recent reviews are scarce and BLM's web page for it now returns 404, so call the El Centro office to confirm it is operating.

name: Boulevard / Cleveland National Forest KOA Holiday
access: Paved. From Old Hwy 80 at Ribbonwood Rd (Boulevard), follow Hwy 94 about 3.4 mi, then turn right on Shasta Way for 0.7 mi; the entrance is on the left where the pavement ends. From the Golden Acorn / Crestwood exit it is about 6.6 mi via Church Rd (BIA 10), which is partly unpaved.
priceTent: Tent sites roughly $45-55/night (third-party reports: Dyrt low $45, Roadtrippers $53). The KOA site blocks automated price checks, so call.
reservations: Reserve online or by phone (reservations line 800-562-0271). After-hours arrivals use night registration: pick a site and settle up in the morning.
cyclistNotes: Open year-round; an October 2026 reviewer found it quiet with no freeway noise. KOA describes tent pads with water and electric; there is also a store, laundry and showers. Elevation about 4,000 ft, so plan on freezing nights. 2026 reviews are mixed: dusty dirt tent pads in wind, and one scathing review of the owner. The app's old pin (32.677, -116.313, 0.5 mi off) is wrong: the KOA is 4.2 road miles south of the line.

name: Cibbets Flat Campground (Cleveland NF)
access: From Old Hwy 80 at Kitchen Creek Rd (by I-8 exit 54), about 5 mi north on paved Kitchen Creek Rd with a steady climb all the way.
priceTent: $20/night single site, $40 double (USFS fee schedule)
reservations: First come, first served
cyclistNotes: USFS lists the site as 'Site Open', with 24 sites, potable water and vault toilets. Quiet oak and creek setting away from the freeway. Cleveland NF elevated fire restrictions are in effect, so use only established fire rings if fires are allowed at all; a stove is safer. No services: carry food from Boulevard or the Golden Acorn travel center.

name: Boulder Oaks Campground (Cleveland NF)
access: Directly on Old Hwy 80, about 2 mi east of the Buckman Springs Rd / I-8 exit 51 junction. Paved.
priceTent: $5/night walk-in tent site; $20 single, $40 double (USFS fee schedule)
reservations: Family and walk-in sites are first come. Only the equestrian loop is on Recreation.gov, and it showed 'Not Reservable' for Nov 2-9.
cyclistNotes: Best value right on the line: a $5 walk-in site with potable water and vault toilets, and the PCT at the gate. Oak and boulder setting, but you will hear I-8 traffic. A camp host was on site in January 2026. No showers.

name: Lake Morena County Park
access: Paved. At Buckman Springs Rd (I-8 exit 51) go south 5.3 mi on Buckman Springs Rd, right on Oak Dr for 1.6 mi, then 0.5 mi on Lake Morena Dr. The app's 3.5-mi figure is straight-line distance; it is 7.5 mi by road, and you climb back out the next morning.
priceTent: About $24-29 per tent or standard site (Dyrt and reviewer reports; partial-hookup sites with outlets about $29-34), plus an $8 reservation fee. Confirm on the county site.
reservations: County online system (parksres.sandiegocounty.gov), bookable from today with a 1-night minimum, or call 858-565-3600. Camping hours are 24/7. The site grid checked Nov 2 showed about 88-93 of 97 units free Nov 2-5 and Nov 8-9, and about half booked Fri-Sat Nov 6-7.
cyclistNotes: Full facilities: flush toilets, coin showers ($0.50 per 4 min, quarters from the ranger station), tent-only sites, and partial-hookup sites with 110 V outlets if you need to charge. Oak Shores Store is about 0.25 mi away (burgers, groceries, the only Wi-Fi in town). No 2026 closures listed for the campground. Elevation 3,000 ft, frost possible.

name: Bobcat Meadow Campground (Cleveland NF, Corral Canyon OHV Area)
access: From Buckman Springs Rd, take Morena Stokes Valley Rd / Corral Canyon Rd about 5.8 mi to Four Corners, then Los Pinos Rd about 1 mi. A May 2026 camper describes about 7 mi of rough off-road driving. Hard on a loaded touring bike, with heavy climbing.
priceTent: $15/night single site (card only, no cash)
reservations: Recreation.gov. All 18 sites were available Nov 2-6 when checked (4 reserved for Nov 7).
cyclistNotes: Last resort only: no water, a rough dirt approach, and OHV traffic that peaks in the October-April red-sticker season. It was open and clean per Jan and May 2026 reviews.

name: Corral Canyon Campground (Cleveland NF, Corral Canyon OHV Area)
access: Same approach as Bobcat Meadow: Buckman Springs Rd to Morena Stokes Valley Rd, 5.8 mi to Four Corners Staging Area, then 1.4 mi more. Reviewers call it a 7.5-mi dead-end road in an OHV area; rough and steep for a bike.
priceTent: $15/night single site (card only, no cash)
reservations: Recreation.gov. All 19 sites were available Nov 2-6 and Nov 9 when checked.
cyclistNotes: Secluded oak grove, but there is no piped water (a creek may flow after rain; treat it) and it is about 10 mi off the line on a rough road. Only if everything else fails.

name: Kitchen Creek Road dispersed sites (Cleveland NF, free permit required)
access: From I-8 exit 47 (Sunrise Hwy at Laguna Junction), climb Sunrise Hwy about 6.5-7 mi, then ride about 1 mi down paved Kitchen Creek Rd past the 'Leaving Mt. Laguna Recreation Area' sign. Pullout sites on both sides. A big climb, and forest road gates can close as fire danger changes.
priceTent: Free, but you need a free Descanso Ranger District dispersed-camping (visitor) permit
reservations: Request the permit by email (SM.FS.DescansoRD@usda.gov) or phone (Mon-Fri 8:30-3:30, closed 11:30-12:30) a few business days ahead. No campfires; limit of 14 days per calendar year (Forest Order 02-26-11).
cyclistNotes: The only legal free dispersed option near Pine Valley; dispersed camping is banned inside the Laguna Mountain Recreation Area. High elevation, so expect a freezing night. A February 2026 report says the gate was open; another report mentions a closure gate about 3 mi along. Usually a poor trade against Boulder Oaks or Lake Morena.

name: Thousand Trails Oakzanita Springs
access: About 3 mi north on Hwy 79 from Descanso: paved, narrow and curvy with little shoulder, uphill to about 3,800 ft.
priceTent: Unknown: dynamic online pricing. RV sites were reported at about $85 in March 2025; tent sites are listed separately.
reservations: 'No Membership Needed to Book': the public can book online, tent sites included. Online check-in available. Campsite check-in from noon. Ranger station hours Nov 1-Apr 1 are 9 am-6 pm.
cyclistNotes: Open year-round, though pools and activities shut down in winter. Reviewers mention warm, clean bathrooms and Wi-Fi in the lodge. Steep, narrow internal roads (fine on a bike). Trails lead straight into Cuyamaca Rancho SP. Camp store has basics only.

name: Green Valley Campground (Cuyamaca Rancho State Park)
address: Cuyamaca Rancho SP, 13652 Hwy 79, Julian, CA 92036
access: About 4.5 mi north on Hwy 79 from Descanso: paved, narrow, climbing to about 4,000 ft.
priceTent: $40/site/night (+$10 per extra vehicle); no hike/bike rate
reservations: ReserveCalifornia through Nov 30; the park showed open dates Nov 5-17 when checked. Walk up if a site is vacant.
cyclistNotes: Creekside oak campground with flush toilets and pay showers. Elevation about 4,000 ft, so nights near or below freezing. Bikes are limited to pavement and approved trails. Food: Descanso stores (mile 328.9).

name: Paso Picacho Campground (Cuyamaca Rancho State Park)
address: Cuyamaca Rancho SP, 13652 Hwy 79, Julian, CA 92036
access: About 9.6 mi north on Hwy 79 from Descanso, climbing roughly 1,600 ft to about 5,000 ft. Paved, narrow.
priceTent: $40/site/night
reservations: ReserveCalifornia through Nov 30; first come Dec 1-Mar 31
cyclistNotes: Only if Green Valley is full. Nearly 10 mi off the line and about 1,600 ft up, making it the coldest site on the segment. Flush toilets and pay showers.

name: Stallion Oaks Ranch (Hipcamp)
access: Rural roads north of Descanso. Exact address on booking (listing coordinates are approximate); the last stretch is probably dirt.
priceTent: $35/night (Hipcamp)
reservations: Hipcamp instant book. Within the tent areas (Barn Yard, Lake Basin) sites are first come.
cyclistNotes: 240-acre Unity Center retreat with a bathhouse (six flush toilets, six showers). Hipcamp marks the water as not potable, so bring drinking water from Descanso (Perkins Store, mile 328.9). Fires only in the communal ring when the fire marshal approves. Limited cell service. Latest reviews September 2026.

name: King Creek Campground (Hipcamp)
access: Rural dirt roads northwest of Descanso. Exact address on booking (listing coordinates are approximate). The host says some sites need 4WD and are not for small cars.
priceTent: $25/night (Hipcamp)
reservations: Hipcamp request-to-book (not instant)
cyclistNotes: Former 1950s Boy Scout camp on 140 acres of oak meadow. Pit toilets; the host delivers well water to your site on request. No pets. Very secluded. Latest reviews September 2026.

name: Ma-Tar-Awa RV Park (Viejas)
access: Paved roads off Willows Rd / Browns Rd near Viejas Casino.
priceTent: Unknown. Reports: $25 (April 2024 camper who 'boondocked' in the meadow) and $35 (2019 RV).
reservations: Call ahead. The park's own domain (matarawarvpark.com) did not resolve on Nov 2, 2026.
cyclistNotes: On the Viejas reservation near the casino, mostly occupied by long-term residents per reviews. Tent policy is unconfirmed, so call before counting on it. Viejas Casino itself only allows RV parking in its lot (no tents).

name: San Diego Canyon Creek (Hipcamp)
access: South of I-8 between Alpine and El Cajon, in the Harbison Canyon area. Exact address on booking (listing coordinates are approximate). Shallow creek crossing at the entrance.
priceTent: $45/night (Hipcamp)
reservations: Hipcamp request-to-book. The host asks you to arrive in daylight if at all possible.
cyclistNotes: Small creekside property with 3 tent sites and a cabin. Shared outdoor kitchen; the bathroom and shower are in the house, with one water heater, so keep showers short. No campfires. 95% of 358 reviews recommend it; latest reviews October 2026.

name: Lake Jennings Campground (Helix Water District)
access: From Old Hwy 80 at Lake Jennings Park Rd (I-8 exit 23), climb about 2 mi north to the campground kiosk on Bass Rd. Paved, steep in places.
priceTent: $45 Sun-Thu / $50 Fri-Sat for a no-hookup tent site (lake view $53/$58), plus an $8 processing fee. Partial-hookup sites with power start at $58 Sun-Thu.
reservations: Online at reserve.lakejennings.org. The office and reservations line are open daily 8 am-5 pm, so book ahead if you will arrive after 5.
cyclistNotes: Open year-round with 44 non-hookup tent sites. Hot showers open 24 hours, free Wi-Fi, lake and city views. Low elevation, so mild nights. The old app record showing $10 is wrong.

name: Rancho Los Coches RV Park
access: On Old Hwy 80 (Hwy 8 Business) by Los Coches Rd. Flat and paved.
priceTent: $25-40/night tent site (+$5 per extra person over age 3)
reservations: Only 2 tent sites, and tent reservations are by phone only (not online). Check-in after 1 pm. Tent stays are limited to 3 nights.
cyclistNotes: The closest tent site to the line in the Lakeside/El Cajon area. Pool, hot tub, laundry, and clean bathrooms per reviews; free Wi-Fi at the pool/spa. This is the app's OSM 'Unnamed campground' at 32.8375, -116.9021. Call early because there are only two tent sites.

name: Santee Lakes Recreation Preserve campground
access: Paved, about 6.9 bike miles north of El Cajon (Magnolia Ave/Cuyamaca St → Mission Gorge Rd → Fanita Pkwy). Gentle grade, no big climb. The baseline's OSM 'Unnamed campground' (osm-way-130000939, tagged caravan_site) is this campground.
priceTent: 2026 standard sites $62–$97/night (priced by demand) + 10% City of Santee TOT. Tents go only on the 15 designated tent sites (1 tent, max 6 people). Reservations have a 2-night minimum.
reservations: Reserve online or by phone and say you are a tent camper; the park says it is near capacity year-round. FAQ: you can stay without a reservation 'subject to site availability'. Check-in 1 pm. After-hours check-in until about 9:30–10 pm (press the gate call button). Park office at Lake 5, 8 am–5 pm. Cancelling within 48 h gets no refund.
cyclistNotes: Best full-service stop near El Cajon on weeknights: showers, laundry, Wi-Fi, store. Expensive for one tent, and the 2-night reservation minimum hurts. Call the day before and ask for a 1-night walk-in tent site. Most of the 300 sites have hookups, so ask for a tent site with a power pedestal. Adds about 14 miles round trip.

name: Golden Acorn Casino & Travel Center (NOT tent-legal)
access: At I-8 exit 61 (Crestwood Rd), next to Old Hwy 80.
priceTent: No tents. Free overnight RV parking for up to 3 days after registering with security.
reservations: Register with security (RVs only)
cyclistNotes: Use it only as a water, food and restroom stop. AllStays describes overnight parking as RVs only with no tents.

name: PCT backcountry campsites near Kitchen Creek / Fred Canyon (OSM pins; NOT usable by bike)
access: Reachable only on foot via the Pacific Crest Trail. Bicycles are prohibited on every part of the PCT. Applies to the app's OSM pins 'Campsite by large oak tree PCT', the unnamed pins at 32.8125/-116.4209 and 32.8135/-116.4186, and the unnamed pin at 32.7644/-116.4392.
priceTent: n/a (hiker sites; PCT permit or Descanso RD permit required)
reservations: n/a
cyclistNotes: Remove these pins from cyclist options: you cannot legally get a bike there, and some sit inside the Laguna Mountain Recreation Area, where dispersed camping is banned.

name: Unnamed OSM campsite on SDG&E service road north of Lake Jennings (NOT a public campground)
access: Utility service road (Nominatim reverse-geocodes it to 'SDG&E Service Road').
priceTent: n/a
reservations: n/a
cyclistNotes: No evidence this is legal public camping. Use Lake Jennings Campground, 1.5 mi south, instead.

name: Carson Trailer (OSM caravan_site, El Cajon; NOT a tent option)
address: East Main St, Bostonia, El Cajon, CA 92021
access: On E Main St, El Cajon.
priceTent: n/a
reservations: n/a
cyclistNotes: A trailer/mobile-home property with no evidence of overnight or tent sites. Not a camp.

name: Vacationer RV Resort (RV-only; NOT a tent option)
address: 1581 E Main St, El Cajon, CA 92021
access: On E Main St, El Cajon. Flat and paved.
priceTent: n/a (RV sites only)
reservations: n/a for tents
cyclistNotes: RV park with mostly long-term residents (Dyrt lists RV accommodation only; a 2024 review describes permanent dwellers and junk cars). Do not plan a tent night here; Rancho Los Coches, 2.6 mi east, takes tents.

name: Kumeyaay Lake Campground (Mission Trails Regional Park)
address: 2 Father Junipero Serra Trail, San Diego, CA 92119
access: Paved, about 5.9–6.3 bike miles from the La Mesa/Grossmont part of the line. Ride Mission Gorge Rd (busy 4-lane road with shoulder/bike lane) to the second Father Junipero Serra Trail entrance. Mild climb.
priceTent: $22.78 per site/night including 1 vehicle. All sites are primitive/dry with no hookups. Card only, no cash.
reservations: OPEN FRIDAY AND SATURDAY NIGHTS ONLY (day use Sun–Thu). In Nick's window that means Fri Nov 6 and Sat Nov 7. Book online (SDRecConnect/ActiveNet) at least 48 h ahead. Same-day walk-ups are welcome, first come first served. Entry office is open Fri–Sat 12–5 pm in winter. Check-in 2 pm, check-out noon. Cancel 14 days ahead.
cyclistNotes: Cheapest real campground between El Cajon and the coast. The restrooms have potable water, sinks and showers. Quiet lakeside site with 46 sites and a 30-night/yr cap. Useless Sun–Thu nights.

name: Sweetwater Summit Regional Park campground
access: Paved, about 9.5 bike miles south from La Mesa/Lemon Grove. Rolling streets, then a steep final climb up Summit Meadow Rd to the hilltop campground. This takes you away from the coast; you backtrack or cut west via Bonita/National City.
priceTent: $33/night tent-only site (county fee table, effective Jan 2, 2026). $39 partial / $42 full hookup if you want power at the site. Showers take tokens (2 per $1) from the ranger station.
reservations: Book at reservations.sdparks.org up to 24 h before arrival. Same day: phone the reservation center, or pay on site if a site is open. Camping access 24 h/day. About 112 sites, all with water and electricity per the brochure. 24-hour hot showers.
cyclistNotes: Solid county campground if Kumeyaay is closed (Mon–Thu) and you want to stop before the coast. It's a big southward detour with a stiff climb, though; Campland and Mission Bay RV are on the line about 21 miles further. No county closure notice for this park as of 11/2/2026.

name: San Diego RV Resort (La Mesa) — NO TENTS
access: On the line (Alvarado Rd by I-8 and the trolley).
priceTent: n/a — tents not accepted
reservations: n/a for tents
cyclistNotes: RV only. Good Sam lists 'No tents', and AAA and AllStays describe it as RV-only. Only The Dyrt's area page lumps it with tent campgrounds. Remove from tent options.

name: San Diego Metro KOA Resort
access: Paved, about 7.9 bike miles south of the City Heights part of the line on urban streets, flat to rolling. A detour away from the coast.
priceTent: Unknown. KOA advertises 'Tent Sites with hookups' and 'Premium Tent Sites' but publishes no rate. Campers reported about $110/night for RV sites in 2025. Call.
reservations: Open all year. Book by phone; the KOA page says internet reservations are not currently available for this park. Tent check-in 1 pm, check-out noon. Nov 5–8 is an event weekend before Veterans Day (busy).
cyclistNotes: Full-service resort (pool, Wi-Fi, café, laundry) with a power outlet at tent sites. Probably the most expensive tent night on the segment, and well off the coast route. Reviews from Oct 2026 mention lots of kids on e-bikes.

name: Sun Outdoors San Diego Bay
address: Chula Vista Bayfront, CA 91910 (call for street address)
access: Paved, about 10.2 bike miles south of the line, flat. The farthest of the Chula Vista options.
priceTent: Unknown. The Dyrt lists RV sites at about $150–280/night.
reservations: Unknown. The operator's site blocked automated checks (HTTP 403). Call.
cyclistNotes: Sun Outdoors' own blog and press copy advertise 'rustic and premium tent sites', but booking listings (Campspot, California Outdoor Hospitality) show only RV sites and cabins. Last-resort only; confirm tent acceptance by phone before riding 10 miles to it.

name: Camp Balboa (Scouting council camp) — not open to individual cyclists
access: Paved, about 2 miles off the line in Balboa Park.
priceTent: n/a
reservations: Council bookings for Scout units, Scout families and youth groups only.
cyclistNotes: In OSM as a campground (operator Boy Scouts of America), but it is a Cub Scout camping center, not a public campground for a solo adult. Remove from the map.

name: Fiesta Island Youth Camp — youth groups only
address: Fiesta Island, Mission Bay Park, San Diego, CA 92109
access: Paved Fiesta Island loop road off E Mission Bay Dr.
priceTent: n/a
reservations: City permit lottery for organized nonprofit youth groups only. No family or individual camping.
cyclistNotes: City rules restrict it to organized nonprofit youth groups and state 'bicycles of any kind are not permitted'. Remove from tent options.

name: Campland on the Bay
address: 2211 Pacific Beach Dr, San Diego, CA 92109
access: On the line at the NE corner of Mission Bay (Pacific Beach Dr / Rose Creek bike path), flat.
priceTent: Winter 2026 (Tue after Labor Day to Memorial Day) 'Limited' water+electric site, which Campland recommends for tents: $72–$92/night + 12.75% TOT (about $81–104). Optional $10/night site-selection fee. The tent-only 'Primitive' sites ($66–77) are summer-only. City of San Diego residents get 20% off.
reservations: Book online or by phone (can book 2 years out). Check-in 2 pm, check-out noon. Arrivals after 10 pm count as late arrivals; quiet setup is allowed. Cancel at least 72 h ahead for a refund less $30. Tents only on sites with ground to stake (Limited section; J row is popular).
cyclistNotes: First on-route campground after El Cajon (about 27 miles). Market, café, laundry, pool, free (limited) Wi-Fi. The city approved a 15-year lease extension in July 2025, so no closure risk.

name: Mission Bay RV Resort — North section (tent-only sites)
address: 2727 De Anza Rd, San Diego, CA 92109
nearestTown: San Diego (Mission Bay / De Anza Cove)
access: Paved, at De Anza Cove next to Campland (Mike Gotch Memorial Bridge bike/ped path). The North section, across from Mission Bay Golf Course, is about 0.8 bike miles off the line.
priceTent: Winter 2026 'Standard (unpaved) TENT ONLY' site from $52 weekday / $63 weekend + 12.75% TOT (about $59–71). Optional $10/night site selection.
reservations: Book online or by phone. Tents allowed ONLY on the unpaved North-section sites (147 sites added 2023–24). Check-in 2 pm, check-out noon. Arriving after 10 pm you may still set up your tent quietly. 24-h hospitality rangers.
cyclistNotes: Cheapest full-service tent night in San Diego. The North section has two restroom/shower buildings, full-hookup pedestals with 30/50-amp outlets, and Wi-Fi. Guests can use Campland's amenities across the bridge. Lease extended alongside Campland's in 2025.

name: Santa Fe Park RV Resort — NO TENTS
address: 5707 Santa Fe St, San Diego, CA 92109
access: On the line beside I-5.
priceTent: n/a — 'Tent camping is not permitted' (RV sites from $99/night off-season + 12.75% tax)
reservations: n/a for tents (office Mon–Sat 9–5, closed Sun)
cyclistNotes: The operator's rates page says 'Tent camping is not permitted' (and RVs over 10 years old are refused). The Dyrt and RVezy tent tags are wrong. Remove from tent options.

name: Surf & Turf RV Park (Del Mar Fairgrounds)
address: 15555 Jimmy Durante Blvd, Del Mar, CA 92014
access: Paved, about 1 mile off Coast Hwy 101 on Jimmy Durante Blvd/Via de la Valle.
priceTent: Unknown. RV sites reported at $40–77/night (Campendium reviews, 2022–24).
reservations: Historically by reservation, 1-night stays allowed. Closed every summer for the fair and races (normally reopens mid-September).
cyclistNotes: Gravel RV lot between I-5 and Hwy 101 with no restrooms, showers or laundry, and an RV-age rule. No evidence it accepts tents. San Elijo's $15 hike/bike site is 3 miles further, so skip this.

name: San Elijo State Beach — hike & bike site (plus standard sites)
access: Directly on Coast Hwy 101 (bike lanes), flat.
priceTent: $15 per person/night on the shared hike/bike site (HB1, Middle Section). Standard sites from $50/night (Northern/Southern sections) + $8.25 reservation fee; premium and hookup sites cost more.
reservations: parks.ca.gov says the hike/bike site is first come first served: register after 2 pm, out by noon, max 2 consecutive nights, 10 hike/bike nights per calendar year, photo ID requested, pay before entering the site. HB1 also appears in ReserveCalifornia (park 709) with nightly availability: the 11/2/2026 snapshot showed it Available Nov 5–11 at $15, so it may be bookable online. Standard sites are ReserveCalifornia only (1-800-444-7275); online booking closes 2 days before arrival. Snapshot: Fri 11/6 and Sat 11/7 each had 1 of 147 sites free; Tue 11/10 2; Wed 11/11 3.
cyclistNotes: The best cyclist stop on this segment: an official $15 hike/bike site on the blufftop with showers and flush toilets, and markets and taco shops across Hwy 101 in Cardiff. It is the ONLY official hike/bike site between El Cajon and Dana Point; ReserveCalifornia lists no hike/bike site type at South Carlsbad, San Onofre, San Clemente or Doheny.

name: South Carlsbad State Beach campground
access: On Carlsbad Blvd (bike lanes), flat. Entrance at 7201 Carlsbad Blvd; drivers can't turn in from Poinsettia Ln and must U-turn at Breakwater Rd.
priceTent: Standard campsite from $50/night; premium bluff sites from $70 (southern end); + $8.25 reservation fee. No hike/bike site type exists here in ReserveCalifornia.
reservations: ReserveCalifornia only (1-800-444-7275); online booking closes 2 days before arrival. Check-in 2 pm. 11/2/2026 snapshot: Fri 11/6 sold out. Sun 11/8–Thu 11/12: 45–62 of about 200 sites free each night. Fri 11/13: 1. Sat 11/14: 0. Walk-up only if the kiosk has a vacancy, so call first.
cyclistNotes: The earlier 'possible closure / no availability' red flag is resolved: the park is open and taking normal weeknight bookings. Big blufftop campground with stairs to the beach and coin showers; camp store is seasonal. The weeknight backup if San Elijo is full, 6 miles further on.

name: Oceanside RV Resort (Thousand Trails) — tent sites
access: On S Coast Hwy in south Oceanside, flat.
priceTent: Unknown. Dedicated tent sites exist but no public rate; one reviewer was quoted about $58 for a site (type and date unclear). Tent sites have a 2-night minimum (10-night max), so you pay for 2 nights.
reservations: No membership needed; book online or by phone. Check-in 1 pm, check-out 11 am. Welcome Center/store 9 am–5 pm; arrange late arrival in advance. Tents only on designated tent sites ('No camping tents within RV sites').
cyclistNotes: The only tent-legal camp right on the line between South Carlsbad and San Clemente, but the 2-night minimum hurts. Railroad next door (loud). Full services: restrooms/showers, laundry, Wi-Fi, store. Last full-service stop before the 20-mile Camp Pendleton crossing.

name: Guajome Regional Park campground
access: Paved, about 9–10 bike miles inland from the Oceanside coast. Mostly on the car-free San Luis Rey River Trail, then N Santa Fe Ave/Guajome Lake Rd, gently uphill. Return the same way. Mile 415 is where you leave the coast route; the closest point on the line is inside Camp Pendleton (417.2).
priceTent: $42/night (the county's 2026 fee table lists Guajome campsites at the full-hookup rate; the brochure shows water+electric sites). Shower tokens are 2 per $1 at the ranger station.
reservations: 33 tent/RV sites plus a cabin. Book at reservations.sdparks.org up to 24 h ahead; same day by phone, or on site if a site is open. Camping access 24 h/day.
cyclistNotes: The legal fallback near Oceanside when the beach parks are full (weekends) or to avoid the 2-night minimum at Oceanside RV. Costs about 19 extra miles round trip, but mostly on a bike path. No county closure notice for Guajome as of 11/2/2026.

name: San Onofre State Beach — Bluffs Campground (CLOSED Nov 2026)
address: 5200 S Pacific Coast Hwy (Old Hwy 101), San Clemente, CA 92672
access: Directly on the Old Pacific Highway bike route through San Onofre SB. That road is currently closed to all traffic, including bicycles, south of the Trail 1 lot.
priceTent: n/a in Nov 2026 (closed)
reservations: Not bookable — closed.
cyclistNotes: The Scales Fire started Oct 16, 2026 next to the San Onofre campground (about 20 acres; campgrounds evacuated, I-5 lanes closed for hours). Afterwards State Parks reopened only the two northernmost lots. Everything south of the Trail 1 lot, including this campground and the Old Pacific Hwy through it, stays closed to vehicles, pedestrians and bicycles (alert updated 10/23/2026). The Bluffs is also normally a summer-season campground, with cold outdoor showers and chemical toilets. Don't plan on it.

name: San Onofre State Beach — San Mateo Campground
access: Paved, about 2 bike miles off the line: up Cristianitos Rd (gentle climb) from the I-5/Cristianitos interchange at the south end of San Clemente.
priceTent: $40 standard campsite (sites 68–100) or $45 tent/primitive sites (101–157); $65 water+electric hookup sites (1–67, the only sites with power); + $8.25 reservation fee. No hike/bike site.
reservations: ReserveCalifornia (1-800-444-7275); online booking closes 2 days before arrival. Campground hours 6 am–10 pm, so arrive before 10 pm or get gate instructions. Open year-round. 11/2/2026 snapshot: on Sat 11/7 only $65 hookup sites were left (16 free units park-wide); Sun 11/8–Thu 11/12 had 110–123 free units.
cyclistNotes: The state park with the most open sites at the north end of Camp Pendleton: hot indoor showers and flush toilets. 1.5-mile Panhe/Trestles trail to the beach. Freeway and motorcycle noise. A good first stop after the 20-mile base crossing; groceries about 1.5 miles away at Avenida Pico.

name: San Clemente State Beach campground
access: Paved, 0.4 mile off the line up Avenida Calafia, short climb.
priceTent: $45/night tent site (Tent Campground East, sites 100–160, and West, sites 73–99); $50 premium tent; + $8.25 reservation fee. The $70 RV hookup loop (sites 1–72) is tagged tents=no in OSM (baseline osm-way-310354752). No hike/bike site.
phone: 949-670-8276 (pass office and camping late arrival); recorded info 949-492-3156
reservations: ReserveCalifornia only; online booking closes 2 days before arrival. Park hours 6 am–10 pm. Late-arrival line 949-670-8276 (Mon–Thu 9–4, Fri 9–2). 11/2/2026 snapshot: Fri 11/6 3 of 128 sites free (East section), Sat 11/7 0, Sun 11/8 37, Mon 11/9 51, Fri 11/13 2, Sat 11/14 0.
cyclistNotes: Clifftop camp in town with food and groceries nearby (Avenida Del Mar/El Camino Real). The cheapest coastal tent site in Orange County at $45. Weekend nights are nearly sold out.

name: Ronald W. Caspers Wilderness Park campground
address: 33401 Ortega Hwy, San Juan Capistrano, CA 92675
access: Paved but demanding: about 10.9 bike miles from Doheny via the San Juan Creek Trail to San Juan Capistrano, then about 7.5 miles east on Ortega Hwy (SR-74). It's a busy two-lane highway with narrow shoulders near the park and a steady climb of a few hundred feet. Within 11 miles only; return the same way.
priceTent: $20 per site/night (OC Parks camping fee; $15 for seniors 60+ and people with disabilities)
reservations: OC Parks online reservation system; groups of 17+ must phone. Check-in 2 pm, check-out noon. Park office Mon–Fri 7 am–3:30 pm; day use 7 am–sunset. Max 14 nights per 30 days (combined with O'Neill RP). No pets.
cyclistNotes: The only realistic non-state-park fallback in south Orange County if Doheny and San Clemente are full. Cheap, with showers at Live Oak, but a 22-mile round-trip detour on Ortega Hwy. Wilderness park with mountain lion warnings. Drinking water comes from third-party listings, not the official page.

name: Doheny State Beach campground
address: 25300 Dana Point Harbor Dr, Dana Point, CA 92629
access: On the line at Dana Point, flat; paved beach trail through the park.
priceTent: $50 standard campsite (North Loop sites 1–59/120/122, South Loop 60–119/121); $65 premium beachside; + $8.25 reservation fee; $2 off for seniors 62+. ReserveCalifornia lists no hike/bike site type. Touring-community reports of an informal hiker/biker area are unconfirmed (iOverlander says none), so ask the kiosk.
reservations: ReserveCalifornia only, 1–7 nights; online booking closes 2 days before arrival. Since 7/1/2026 the booking window is 3 months, ahead of a construction closure expected 2027–2029; State Parks says the campground stays open through at least the end of 2026. 11/2/2026 snapshot: Fri 11/6 1 of 108 sites free, Sat 11/7 0, Sun 11/8 and Mon 11/9 47 each, Fri 11/13 and Sat 11/14 0.
cyclistNotes: Flat beachside camp at the north end of the segment; trains pass right alongside. After mid-October 2026 coastal flooding the park stayed open during debris cleanup, with some parking closed. Last state-park camp before Crystal Cove (segment I8-F).

name: Crystal Cove State Park — Moro Campground
access: Paved. Turn off PCH at the signal for El Morro School and climb the short campground road to the mesa, about 0.7 mi. The entrance sits inside the current Caltrans PCH work zone between Reef Point Dr and Irvine Cove Dr.
address: 8471 N. Coast Highway, Laguna Beach, CA 92651
priceTent: About $55 for one of the 30 'low-impact' tent/van sites, or about $75 for a hookup site. These are 2020–2025 reported rates; the 2026 rate was not confirmed. Add the $8.25 ReserveCalifornia fee; an extra vehicle is $15. No dedicated hike & bike site was found. A 2022 GearJunkie listing mentions a $5 hike/bike-in fee, which is unconfirmed, so ask at the kiosk.
phone: (949) 494-3539; reservations (800) 444-7275; late-arrival arrangements (949) 494-9143 (per The Dyrt listing)
reservations: Reservations only via ReserveCalifornia; there are no first-come sites. Check-in 3 pm, check-out 1 pm. The entry gate is locked 10 pm–6 am, so if arriving late, call during business hours to make arrangements. A parks.ca.gov availability snapshot checked 11/2/2026 showed two-night availability within 11/5–11/17 only for arrivals on 11/11, 11/15 and 11/16. Check for single nights and cancellations.
cyclistNotes: The best-located full-service camp on the segment, but expensive and mostly booked. There are 58 sites: 30 dry 'low-impact' sites for tents and 28 RV sites with 30/50A water and electric. Showers are hot and token or coin operated. PCH WORK ZONE: since mid-October 2026, emergency bluff stabilization has closed both southbound lanes between Reef Point Dr and Irvine Cove Dr, leaving one lane each way with no end date. Expect no shoulder; ride it in daylight, take the lane, or walk. After the October 2026 storms the Historic District beach, Pelican Point (P2) access and the Moro Cove beach are closed. No wood or charcoal fires. Food: Crystal Cove Shake Shack and Beachcomber Café nearby; Corona del Mar and Laguna Beach stores are about 3 mi either way.

name: Crystal Cove State Park — Lower Moro backcountry camp
access: Start from the Moro Campground entrance (mile 455.5): about 0.7 mi paved, then about 2.8 mi of dirt fire road up Moro Canyon, gaining roughly 750 ft (about 125 ft to about 875 ft). Mountain bikes are allowed on backcountry fire roads but not after dark. Expect to push a loaded bike on the steep pitches. The park describes all primitive sites as a 3–4 mi hike from the parking lot.
address: Crystal Cove State Park backcountry, 8471 N. Coast Highway, Laguna Beach, CA 92651
priceTent: $25 per site per night with one vehicle included (The Dyrt and campers' reports 2019–2026), plus the ReserveCalifornia reservation fee.
reservations: Book through ReserveCalifornia 48 hours to 7 months ahead (per the park site). The park infosheet says the permit can also be obtained at the Moro Campground kiosk, where every backcountry camper must check in for the overnight permit. Within the area you reserve, sites are first-come. Check-in/check-out time is listed as 9 am.
cyclistNotes: The cheapest legal camp on the segment, but a real hike-a-bike: 13 sites, pit toilet, picnic tables, ocean view. There is NO water, so haul 4–5 L up from Moro Campground. Stoves only (no fires), no pets, 4 people per site. Same-day online booking is not possible (48-hour minimum), so ask at the Moro kiosk. Trails close after rain. Corrected position: the baseline camp-res-107 coordinates (33.573,-117.808) are in the canyon bottom; the camp itself is the OSM node used here.

name: Crystal Cove State Park — Deer Canyon backcountry camp
access: From the Moro Campground entrance: about 0.7 mi paved, then about 3.5 mi of dirt fire roads, gaining about 530 ft to about 650 ft. Bikes are legal on fire roads but not after dark.
address: Crystal Cove State Park backcountry, Laguna Beach, CA 92651
priceTent: $25 per site per night, plus the ReserveCalifornia reservation fee.
reservations: Same as Lower Moro: book 48 hours or more ahead on ReserveCalifornia, or get the permit at the Moro Campground kiosk.
cyclistNotes: Smallest of the three camps (OSM lists 5 tent pads). No water, no fires, no dogs.

name: Newport Dunes Waterfront Resort & Marina (RV resort, tents on Small sites)
access: Paved and flat. Leave PCH at Jamboree Rd / Back Bay Dr (bike lanes); the gate at 1131 Back Bay Dr is about 0.5 mi away.
address: 1131 Back Bay Dr, Newport Beach, CA 92660
priceTent: No separate tent rate is published. Tents go on a Small RV site (22×25 ft, full hookups with 30/50A power): $84–$165/night in the winter season (Tuesday after Labor Day to Friday before Memorial Day). Rates include the $5 online fee, change with demand, and tax is added. One vehicle pass included.
reservations: Book online (camplife.com, linked from newportdunes.com) or call 949-729-3863. Walk-up availability is not documented. Check-in is from 2 pm. If you arrive after the registration office closes but before 10 pm, the gate sends you to your reserved site and you register by 11 am the next morning. Arrivals after quiet hours begin (10 pm Sun–Thu, 11 pm Fri–Sat) are sent to the main parking lot until 8 am. Tent stays are capped at 14 nights in any 3 months.
cyclistNotes: The LAST tent-legal campground before Los Angeles on the I-8 line. Pricey, but a full resort: hot showers, laundry, heated pool, basic wifi, and electricity at the site. Tents are allowed only on Small RV sites, two per site at most. The 2025 rules say tents must be FREESTANDING and stakes are strictly prohibited, so weight the tent down. Lock the bike to a fixed object (resort rule). Bikes are welcome on resort roads (5 mph) and the beach promenade (3 mph). Back Bay Bistro is on site; stores in Newport and Costa Mesa are 1–2 mi away.

name: Huntington by the Sea RV Resort (RV only, no tents)

reservations: unknown
cyclistNotes: Listed only so the app stops treating it as an option: listings describe full-hookup RV sites with no tents. Don't plan on it.

name: Huntington Beach RV Campground / Sunset Vista (RV only, no tents)
access: Paved, on the beach path just south of the HB Pier, between 1st St and Huntington St. The coordinates are the Huntington City Beach centroid, which approximates the campground lot.
address: 20903 Pacific Coast Hwy, Huntington Beach, CA 92648
priceTent: Not available to tents (RV rate $75 Sun–Thu, $100 Fri–Sat).
reservations: Online only, up to 3 months ahead and no later than the day before arrival. No phone or same-day bookings. Gate closes at 10 pm.
cyclistNotes: City rule: 'No conversions, tent camping or cassette toilets allowed.' Open for its season, September 3 – May 31, but not for tents. Public beach restrooms are open 7 am–10 pm.

name: Bolsa Chica State Beach Campground (self-contained RVs only, no tents)
access: Paved and flat, along PCH and the beach trail.
address: 17851 Pacific Coast Hwy, Huntington Beach, CA
priceTent: Not available to tents (RVs $60 back row / $70 beach row).
reservations: Reservations only via ReserveCalifornia.
cyclistNotes: The official page says 'Tent camping is not offered at Bolsa Chica State Beach'; only self-contained RVs are allowed and there is no hike & bike site. Still useful for water, restrooms and the 8.5-mile paved beach trail through Huntington Beach.

name: Golden Shore RV Resort (RV only, no tents)
access: Paved, flat, at the foot of the LA River path in downtown Long Beach.
priceTent: Not available to tents (RVs about $85–$150 per aggregator listings).
reservations: RV reservations only; check-in 2–7 pm (CamplinQ).
cyclistNotes: AAA: '80 Sites. No tent. RVs only.' CamplinQ rules: 'No tents or improvised camping setups are allowed.' Tempting location, but not an option.

name: Hipcamp — Vintage Camper in LBC Garden (trailer rental with room for a tent)
access: Urban streets. Hipcamp lists it 3.5 mi from central Long Beach and about 10 minutes from the ports of Long Beach and San Pedro, so it is likely west or north Long Beach near the LA River path. The exact address is given only after booking; the coordinates are the Long Beach city centroid (APPROXIMATE).
address: Long Beach, CA (exact address after booking)
priceTent: unknown. The nightly rate is not shown. You book the 1968 Shasta camper (sleeps up to 4); the listing says there is 'additional room to set a tent, if desired'. Optional driveway parking is $10/night.
reservations: Book on Hipcamp. Check-in 3–11 pm (early or late may be possible), check-out 11 am, 1-night minimum, strict cancellation. Host Lena W. has an 80% response rate, typically within about 5 hours.
cyclistNotes: The ONLY tent-allowing place found between Newport Dunes (mile 461) and Los Angeles. It is a vintage trailer in the host's shared backyard garden (88% recommend). Reviews from October 2025 to October 2026 mention ants, roaches, floodlights, neighborhood noise and weak water pressure. The shower is cold only, and the host says to bring your own drinking water. Book before leaving Newport so you have the address.

name: Millard Campground / Millard Trail Camp (CLOSED — Eaton Fire closure)
access: Beyond the end of the line, about 12.5 mi via Altadena and the steep Chaney Trail road, which is closed to vehicles.
priceTent: Free when open; currently closed.
reservations: First-come when open.
cyclistNotes: CLOSED to camping inside the Eaton Fire Area Closure, extended through Dec 31, 2027. You may pass through but not camp; the restroom, water, bear boxes and fire rings are unavailable. Use Gould Mesa instead.

name: Hopkins Wilderness Park group camps (Pine / Sycamore / Gumwood) — PIER VARIANT, not usable
access: On the Santa Monica Pier variant only (Long Beach to Redondo Beach): about 13.3 riding mi from Long Beach, then 0.3 mi off PCH at Prospect Ave or about 1.5 mi up from the Esplanade/Strand. Paved.
priceTent: Group booking only: $374 staffing fee per overnight reservation, plus per-person fees (a 2024 report says $10 per adult).
reservations: Reserve 2–3 weeks to 6 months ahead through WebTrac or at the Alta Vista Racquet Center, 715 Julia Ave. Check-in Saturday 2 pm, check-out Sunday noon.
cyclistNotes: NOT usable for a touring cyclist. City rules prohibit bicycles in the park. It is tent-only Saturday-night group camping booked weeks ahead, and the staffing fee alone is $374. The app's OSM pins for Pine Camp, Sycamore Camp and Gumwood Camp should be marked unusable.

name: Dockweiler RV Park — PIER VARIANT (no tents)
access: On the Santa Monica Pier variant: directly on the Marvin Braude (Strand) beach bike path in Playa del Rey, about 21.5 riding mi from Long Beach.
address: 12001 Vista del Mar, Playa del Rey, CA 90293
priceTent: Not available to tents ('No tent camping is allowed'). RV full-hookup sites are $65–$75; $45 dry-camper sites take only small RVs and campervans.
reservations: No walk-ins; reservations required, up to 90 days ahead. Check-in 1 pm; office open Mon–Fri 9 am–5 pm.
cyclistNotes: LA County bans tents here, including rooftop tents on SUVs. The only campground on the pier line, but useless for a tent. Beach restrooms and water are along the Strand.

name: Musch Trail Camp, Topanga State Park — beyond the PIER VARIANT end
access: Beyond the Santa Monica Pier end of the variant. About 11.7 mi to Trippet Ranch: 4 mi up PCH, then Topanga Canyon Blvd (SR-27) and the steep Entrada Rd, climbing about 1,170 ft (13 ft to 1,186 ft). Then about 1 mi on the Musch Trail, a foot-only single track (bikes are allowed only on park fire roads), so lock the bike at Trippet Ranch and carry your gear in. This is beyond the 10-mile limit because no tent camp exists near the pier.
address: Trippet Ranch, Entrada Rd, Topanga State Park, Topanga, CA 90290
priceTent: $7 per person per night, paid at the Trippet Ranch entrance station or the iron ranger at the camp.
reservations: First-come, first-served (about 6 sites in two fenced areas). Day-use parking is 8 am to sunset; arrive before dark.
cyclistNotes: Water spigot and flush restrooms, no fires. Topanga State Park is open with restrictions after the Palisades Fire. Since 10/14/26, Santa Monica Mountains park agencies close parks during Red Flag Warnings, which are common in November Santa Ana winds. PCH and Topanga Canyon Blvd had long post-fire closures in 2025, so check Caltrans QuickMap. The Elysian is about 28 mi away.

name: Hipcamp — Cross Bull Ranch / CBR (Topanga) — beyond the PIER VARIANT end
access: Beyond the Santa Monica Pier: about 10 mi via PCH and Topanga Canyon Blvd, climbing to about 800 ft. The exact address is given only after booking; the coordinates are Topanga village (APPROXIMATE). One tent site is hike-in and another is a short walk.
priceTent: unknown (not shown on Hipcamp).
reservations: Hipcamp, same-day bookings allowed. Meet host Lisa on arrival; check-in from 2 pm; stays up to 4 nights; super-strict cancellation.
cyclistNotes: Two tent-only sites (Catalpas, hike-in; Moon Lodge, short walk) plus two RV/tent sites. Every site has a toilet (type not stated) and potable water; no showers, no power, no campfires. Reviews run July–September 2026. The Elysian is about 28 mi back.

name: Hipcamp — Tentsite Over Topanga — beyond the PIER VARIANT end
access: Beyond the Santa Monica Pier: about 12.2 mi via PCH and Topanga Canyon Blvd to the Theatricum Botanicum lot (the coordinates are the Theatricum, APPROXIMATE). From there the site is hike-in only: about 300 steep steps, 10+ minutes.
address: Near Theatricum Botanicum, 1419 N Topanga Canyon Blvd, Topanga, CA 90290
priceTent: unknown
reservations: Hipcamp, bookable up to 9 months ahead; super-strict cancellation. Check-in after 2 pm; the host meets you at the Theatricum lot.
cyclistNotes: One tent site with room for 2–3 tents. Bring water in jugs. The flush toilets are at the Theatricum, which is closed mid-October through March, so toilet access in November is unconfirmed. No fires.
